Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 5:

After the declaration that this Book is a decree from God, whose verses are firm and elaborated, coming from One who is All-Wise and All-Aware, it is shown how wrong is the reaction of some people to these verses when the prophets, who warn and give glad tidings, recite them to them, despite this reality. The Qur'an presents their reaction together with their bodily movement: they bow their heads and turn their chests aside so that they may hide and evade. Can they hide from God? How vain is their effort. God knows even when they, in their own opinion, are hidden under their garments, and indeed God knows every creature that walks or crawls on this earth. He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.

These two verses (verses 5 and 6) present a scene which, if it is brought to mind well and reflected upon, would make a person tremble with fear. How terrifying and shaking this scene is! Just consider: a feeble servant wants to hide from God, while God's knowledge encompasses him. When they are confronted with the verses of God, they hide, but when can they really hide?

اَلَآ اِنَّھُمْ يَثْنُوْنَ صُدُوْرَھُمْ لِيَسْتَخْفُوْا مِنْهُ ۭ اَلَا حِيْنَ يَسْتَغْشُوْنَ ثِيَابَھُمْ ۙ يَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّوْنَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُوْنَ ۚ اِنَّهٗ عَلِيْمٌۢ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُوْرِ

Behold, they fold their chests so that they may hide from Him. Beware, when they cover themselves with their garments, Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal; indeed He knows the secrets within the breasts.

Perhaps this verse depicts certain incidents: that the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to recite the Word of God to these people, and they turned away to avoid it, wishing to pass by with their heads lowered, making an effort to appear as though they had hidden themselves, and having evaded sight. It is possible that on some occasions they actually behaved in this way.

In a brief phrase it is stated how crude this behaviour of theirs is. Allah, who has sent down these verses, is with them in every state, whether they are apparent or concealed. The Qur'an, in a distinctive manner, here exposes their behaviour by bringing to view their most hidden physical condition, declaring it wrong: when they lie at night in their homes, on their beds, in the darkness of the night, Allah is still with them, and they cannot hide. He is the One who is present and observing, and the Irresistible. He knows every apparent and hidden matter.

اَلَا حِيْنَ يَسْتَغْشُوْنَ ثِيَابَھُمْ ۙ يَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّوْنَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُوْنَ (Beware, when they cover themselves with their garments, Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal.) Moreover, Allah knows even more hidden matters than these. What barrier can their coverings form before the knowledge of God? Rather, in such circumstances, only the human being himself feels that he is alone and that no one is watching him. This manner of expression touches human conscience (wijdan), awakens it, and shakes it, so that he reflects upon the Divine Being and understands that an eye is watching him at all times.

اِنَّهٗ عَلِيْمٌۢ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُوْرِ (He indeed knows the secrets within the breasts.) He knows even those secrets which are hidden in hearts. Although these secrets are, in fact, present in the heart and are attached to it in the way an owner is attached to his possession, or a friend to a friend, they are called *dhat al-sudur* (the secrets of the breasts) because of their utmost confidentiality. When Allah knows such inner secrets of the heart, then what else could remain hidden from Him? In short, no movement of a human being, nor any repose of his, can remain concealed from Him.

This is the commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah Hud, verse 6:

This is another form of Allah's all-encompassing knowledge. Consider it with awe: the creatures that walk upon the earth and the crawling insects and worms—everything that moves upon the earth is a dabba (living creature).

Of the countless and innumerable dawab (living beings) that move upon the earth, whatever exists, wherever it is in the regions of the earth, whether above or within, all of it is in Allah's knowledge. Not only is it known to Him; Allah also provides them with sustenance, and Allah also knows where they find rest and tranquility and where they are entrusted. Indeed, all these dawab are under the control and command of Allah's all-encompassing knowledge.

This is a most clear example of Allah's knowledge. This knowledge remains constantly attached to creation. When a human being reflects on this vast knowledge and tries to bring it within his limited imagination, he trembles and is overwhelmed by the mere conception of it.

Now it is not only a matter of knowledge. For each individual of this unimaginable number of dawab al-ard, Allah has also taken upon Himself the guarantee of sustenance. He has created means of sustenance in this earth for every creature and has given every thing the capacity to acquire sustenance according to its need. The sustenance of some is very simple; some produce their own provision; some prepare products and compounds for themselves; and in the modern age the means of sustenance have become very widespread and varied. Some creatures live on the blood of living beings, such as mosquitoes and fleas, etc.

In the same manner in which Allah created this world and brought into existence the various kinds of creatures upon it, He also provided their means of sustenance. And He provided every creature with the capacity and resources according to its created nature. Especially among the dawab of the earth, man deserves our attention and study most, for he is the khalifatullah fil-ard (vicegerent of Allah on earth). He has also been given the capacity for analysis, synthesis, composition and industry. He can advance in progress and production. He can even change the face of this globe. He keeps changing the patterns of life. He provides for himself diverse means of sustenance, but he cannot create anything. He only modifies those resources which Allah has deposited within this earth, and this modification, analysis and composition he carries out in accordance with the laws of nature which Allah has established in this universe. Thus this earth provides every kind of requirement for its living dawab.

That sustenance is with Allah does not mean that someone may receive provision without striving, or that if someone sits idle he will certainly receive it, or that through any negative attitude it cannot be lost, as some people have wrongly understood. If that were so, why would Allah have appointed means and resources, why would He have made it obligatory to adopt means, why would He have made means a part of the laws of nature, and why would He have given different people different capacities among His creatures? And how could the construction and progress of the world have become possible without employing these resources and means, although all of this was within Allah's knowledge, and He made man His khalifa on this globe so that he might play his role.

Sustenance for every creature is decreed; this is the truth. But this sustenance is deposited within this universe and is fixed and determined for every creature in accordance with the sunnah of Allah. And the sunnah of Allah is that every person will strive for what has been decreed for him. Therefore no one should abandon striving, while he knows well that gold and silver do not rain from the heavens but water rains, and every kind of sustenance is hidden within the earth. And this is sufficient for all creatures, provided that these creatures seek it in accordance with the divine sunan. The sunan of Allah do not show favoritism to anyone.

In the world the matter rests on earning and action. Earning and action will either be good (tayyib) or evil and foul (khabith). Striving is necessary for both. Their natures differ and their results are separate. Lawful is lawful, and unlawful is unlawful.

Here only the word rizq is used for dawab, whereas earlier rizq hasan was mentioned for the believers. Choosing the best words for humans and animals within the context is a particular style of the Holy Quran. The choice of words corresponds to the occasion, the setting and the environment.

These two verses are the beginning of the description of the praise and majesty of the Lord, to Whom people have been commanded to devote worship and servitude alone, because He is the All-Knowing, the All-Encompassing, the Provider; no one in His dominion remains hungry. This praise of the Lord and this glorification of the Lord is necessary so that a true relationship may arise between the servant, the creation and the Creator, and people may obey and worship the Lord and Creator correctly, with full insight.

Now, after this, a different aspect of the glory of the Generous Lord is presented. Some of the signs and manifestations of the Lord's power are set forth. A hint is given of His wisdom and workings, so that you may see in what a wise manner Allah has fashioned the heavens and the earth. Here are brought forward those aspects of this universe which are consistent with the beliefs of action, reckoning, and resurrection after death, and which, indeed, give that impression:

﴿And He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water, that He might test you as to which of you is best in deed. But if you say, "Indeed you will be resurrected after death," those who disbelieve will surely say, "This is nothing but clear magic."﴾ And He it is who created the heavens and the earth in six days, while before that His Throne was upon the water. So that He may test you, which of you is best in conduct. Now, if you tell them, O Prophet, that after death you will be raised again, the deniers at once exclaim that this is plain sorcery.

As for Allah creating the heavens and the earth in six days, we have discussed this subject in Surah Yunus. There it came up in its context, namely, that the laws of nature by which the heavens and the earth operate, and the system by which people's lives run, are connected and harmonious.

﴿That He may test you, which of you is best in conduct﴾ (so that He may test you to see which of you is best in deed). What is new here is this: after the description of the creation of the heavens and the earth, this is a parenthetical clause.

﴿And His Throne was upon the water﴾ (while before that His Throne was upon the water). This shows that in the process of creating the heavens and the earth, before they reached their present form, there was water here, and the Throne of Allah was upon the water.

How that water was, where it was, and what its condition was, and how the Throne of Allah was after that, this verse gives no details of these matters. Those commentators who know the limits of their knowledge can say nothing more than this. These are unseen matters, and Allah has given us only the information found in this verse, and it is limited.

It is not our task to present scientific theories in support of Qur'anic texts, even if a text happens to agree with some scientific theory, because scientific theories change repeatedly, and indeed keep being overturned. When scholars of natural science put forward a theory and prove it through scientific experiments, they find that new theory closer to natural phenomena than earlier theories, whereas the Qur'anic text is in itself true and right, whether or not science has been able to reach that truth and reality. Furthermore, there is a difference between a scientific fact and a scientific theory. A scientific fact is that which comes within experience, although experiments too always remain probable and are never certain. As for scientific theories, they are based on hypotheses, and these hypotheses are formed on the basis of certain phenomena of the universe or a collection of a few phenomena, and they can change at any time. Therefore we can neither support the Qur'an by these theories, nor argue from the Qur'an on the basis of these theories, because the method of the Qur'an is one thing and that of science another. In this way, the subject matters of the Qur'an and of science are also different.

In our age, some scientific theories are presented in the Qur'an. I say this way of thinking is contrary to our faith in the texts of the Qur'an. The Qur'an is from the Wise and the All-Aware. This mistake is made because we do not keep science confined within its own domain, but extend it beyond its sphere. This is in fact our moral and intellectual defeatism, while those who do this consider their act a service to the Qur'an, and thereby believe they prove their faith. A faith that is proven by some principle of science, I would say, such a faith needs to be reconsidered. This is open to question. The Qur'an is the principal foundation, and scientific theories, whether they agree with it or oppose it, have no standing before the Qur'an. As for those scientific facts that are proven by experiments, their domain and the domain of the Qur'an are different; both subject matters are distinct. The Qur'an has left the discovery of scientific facts to human reason, and has granted it complete freedom to work in this field and to reach, through experiment, whatever results can be reached. The Qur'an has taken upon itself only the duty to train human reason correctly, soundly and on a straight course, and to lead it out of illusions, superstitions and mythological thinking. Thus the Qur'an has taken upon itself the task of proposing a system for the correct conduct of human life, within whose bounds human reason also advances on the right path, and lives free, in peace and security, and works within its own limited and specific sphere, so that in the light of principles it may discover partial truths. The Qur'an has rarely mentioned scientific facts, for example that all living things are alive from water and water is an important element of their life; and for example that all living animals and plants were created in pairs, and through the union of pairs life develops in human, animal and plant forms. These are certain of the facts the Qur'an has mentioned (for details see Parah 2 and Parah 7).

After this parenthetical clause, we return to the Qur'anic verse:

﴿And He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water, that He might test you as to which of you is best in deed.﴾ He created the heavens and the earth in six days, and while before that His Throne was upon the water, so that He may test you, which of you is best in conduct.

He created the heavens and the earth in six days. After this, several phrases and sentences are omitted; the subsequent text indicates them, namely that in this period He created it and made it fit and useful for human habitation, subjected all things on earth to you, and arranged in the heavens what enables you to live here, and the being of Allah encompasses this entire universe.

﴿That He may test you, which of you is best in conduct﴾ From these verses it is understood that He created this entire universe in six days, and that its keys and control are in the hand of Allah, and that all this arrangement is for the trial of man, so that it may be known that this trial is a serious matter, and that it is not mere play and sport but a purposeful and serious scheme, and that the creation of man has taken place under a purposeful plan.

Just as Allah has prepared the heavens and the earth so that they are helpful and supportive to the human race, so too He has given the human race a particular and distinctive capacity and power. The creation of man has also taken place according to the same law of nature according to which this universe was created. But apart from this creational aspect of man, He has also given him a capacity for choice and will. Through this capacity of choice, he sometimes takes the path of guidance, and Allah assists him, and he receives guidance; and sometimes he takes the path of error, and Allah also gives him respite and leaves such people so that they act, and this is a trial from Him as to who takes the good path and who the bad. Allah tests and gives respite to these people, not because Allah wishes to acquire knowledge, for He already knows. Through trial and action, in fact, the hidden deeds of people become manifest to people, and then they receive recompense for these deeds. In this way Allah prepared this scheme.

Therefore, denial of the resurrection after death and the process of reward and punishment appears strange in this atmosphere, because the law of retribution for deeds is a natural law, and it is one permanent and fundamental principle among the principles of this universe. Those who deny this principle, it appears, do not have a reasonable attitude, and such people are deprived of comprehending the great principles of this universe. Because of this flawed thinking, they are astonished that man will rise again, considering it a strange matter:

﴿And if you say, "Indeed you will be resurrected after death," those who disbelieve will surely say, "This is nothing but clear magic."﴾ Now, if you tell them, O Prophet, that after death you will be raised again, the deniers at once exclaim that this is plain sorcery.

At first sight it appears that the statement of those who consider resurrection after death strange is itself strange, and in the light of the events mentioned above, nothing could be a greater falsehood than this.

...

Just as they deny resurrection after death and do not understand it in the light of the unshakable principles of this universe, so they also fail to grasp the worldly punishment of God and the destructive natural calamities. They ask why the punishment of God is not sent down upon them again, although the delay in it is also for a wise reason. Allah gives respite to everyone.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 8:

The peoples of earlier times were struck by such punishments that they were uprooted from their very foundations. Yet these destructive and annihilating punishments came only after the messengers had presented their miracles to their peoples, and the people had continued to deny them despite those miracles. This all-encompassing destruction kept coming because the messages of that time were temporary messages, meant for a limited period, and at times they were meant only for one generation. The miracles could be witnessed only by those who were present. These miracles were not continuous and enduring, so that later generations could also see them as the first generation had seen them.

The nature of the Muhammadan message differs somewhat from previous messages. He is the Seal of the Prophets. He is a messenger for all generations, and the miracle given to him is not a material miracle. It is a miracle that remains forever. Future generations can also see it, reflect upon it, and believe in it generation after generation. Therefore, the wisdom of Allah required that no punishment be sent down upon his Ummah that would uproot it from its very roots; rather, punishment would fall upon individuals. This same approach was adopted by Allah toward those peoples who had been given a Book. No people possessing a Book has been uprooted and cast away.

However, the condition of the polytheists of Makkah was that they neither understood the system of creation of this universe nor the law of nature which Allah had ordained for it, nor did they understand that Allah has given man opportunities to act with freedom and choice within this universe, and that he has the freedom to adopt good or evil, and that the earth is created in such a way that it provides opportunities for man's freedom and will. Because of this ignorance, they denied resurrection after death, and because of this same ignorance they asked why Allah had not yet destroyed them despite their denial and rejection. They did not know what principles Allah had established for the present message and for earlier messages. Therefore they would ask: several years have passed and the punishment is not coming. These people were acquainted neither with Allah's wisdom nor with His mercy. They did not know that when this punishment comes, no one will be able to turn it back; rather, it will completely encompass them, and it will be the recompense for their mockery and evil deeds. They were asking questions in a manner of extreme obstinacy.

﴿Beware! On the Day it comes to them, it will not be turned away from them, and what they used to mock will surround them.﴾ Indeed, no serious person or believer hastens to demand the descent of the punishment of Allah. If the punishment of Allah does not come, there will also be some wisdom in that, and Allah's mercy will be the barrier to it, so that those who have the capacity for faith may come to believe.

For example, Allah did not hasten to send down punishment upon the Quraysh. They were continually given respite. During this period, countless people embraced faith, and after accepting faith, they performed outstanding services for Islam. Also, many children were born to disbelievers who later rendered services to Islam in subsequent eras. These and other such known and unknown wisdoms may exist, which hasty people cannot comprehend.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verses 9–11:

Commentary on verses 9 to 11: These people are showing impatience in demanding the descent of punishment. Here further light is cast on this aspect of human nature, that man, in any condition, does not remain steadfast and does not form a correct judgement. His disposition is as follows:

If at times We let man taste mercy from Us and then withdraw it from him, he becomes despairing and begins to be ungrateful. And if, after the hardship that had befallen him, We let him taste blessing, he says, "All my troubles have gone from me," and then he becomes exultant and boastful. Those who are free of this fault are only those who are patient and do good deeds, and it is they for whom there is forgiveness and a great reward.

Man is by nature hasty and prone to shortcomings, and in these verses (verses 9 to 11) his portrait is drawn most fittingly. He is so short-sighted that he can see only the present circumstances, and he brings upon himself the very conditions that prevail in his environment. He takes no trouble to reflect on the past, nor does he concern himself with the future. Sometimes he becomes so despairing that he no longer hopes for any good and for better circumstances. And if good days pass, he denies all the past blessings, although these were a gift and a favour from Allah; he had no entitlement to them. And if after difficulties good days come to him, he goes beyond himself and becomes arrogant. He neither bears hardships in the hope of Allah's mercy and compassion, nor does he adopt moderation in his joy, and he does not prepare himself for the decline of joys and blessings.

"Illa alladhina sabaru wa 'amilu as-salihat" (Except those who are patient and do righteous deeds). Ulaika lahum maghfiratun wa ajrun kabir (It is they for whom there is forgiveness and a great reward). That is, they showed patience both over favours and blessings and over hardships. Most people are patient in hardship, because of their self-respect and outward dignity, and so that their weakness and difficulties do not become known to people. But few people are able to restrain themselves in prosperity and wealth, and to protect themselves from arrogance and rebellion. Nevertheless, those who maintain good conduct, who do good works both in hardship and in prosperity, and who are thankful for blessings, that is, who are embodiments of "wa 'amilu as-salihat," are the ones described in the verse.

"Ulaika lahum maghfiratun wa ajrun kabir" (They are the ones for whom there is forgiveness and a great reward). This is because they were patient in hardship, and in prosperity they acted with seriousness and moderation. The truth is that only a serious, sincere and true faith saves a person from disbelieving despair in the most difficult circumstances. Likewise, only true faith in Allah saves a person from pride and arrogance in his prosperity and abundance. In short, it is this true faith that keeps the human heart balanced and upright in both good and bad circumstances. The heart of the believer is firmly bound: it is not shaken by hardships and calamities, and it does not swell with pride in prosperity and wealth. Thus the believers have good conditions in both states, and the high station is attained by the believers alone, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 12:

Those people among God's creatures who are not acquainted with the divine laws (sunan Ilahiyyah) are deprived of an understanding of the wisdom of God's creation. They are shallow in understanding, heedless, despairing, arrogant, and take pride in false notions. They do not know what the wisdom behind the sending of Messengers is, and nor do they know why Messengers were sent from among humankind. Such people demand why the Messenger himself is not an angel, or why an angel has not been appointed to accompany him. These people are so unaware of the station of the Messenger and of prophethood that they consider it necessary for a Messenger to be wealthy. These people remain lost in false beliefs, and such people seek out these crude pretexts for denial. Therefore, do not be affected.

––

The word la'alla (لعل) here is interrogative, though not purely interrogative. The meaning is that human nature might be expected, in such circumstances, to become constricted in heart and abandon this very task, because people are displaying ignorance, obstinacy and stubbornness, and are putting forward these baseless and frivolous proposals, which have no harmony with the temperament of prophethood, its nature, or its rank. God, by presenting an alternative and impracticable course regarding this situation, asks whether, although the circumstances are bad, you could perhaps leave something of your call and of what has been revealed from God, in the hope that they might not display this ignorance and malice? That cannot happen. You cannot leave these matters.

Innama anta nadhir (you are only a warner). Your duty is only that you deliver the message in full and warn people. And warning is necessary because they have adopted such an attitude that they must be warned. Therefore, continue to carry out your duties.

Wallahu 'ala kulli shay'in wakil. Beyond this, God is the guardian of everything. God is responsible for them all, and according to His sunnah He will turn them as He wills, and after that He will requite them for what they earn. You are not their guardian or their trustee. You are not responsible for their disbelief or for their belief. You are only a warner.

This verse shows how difficult the circumstances of the Islamic movement were in that period and how heavy a burden lay on the heart of the Prophet at that time, especially when the supporters, helpers and family protectors of the movement had passed away. The Prophet ﷺ's heart was dominated by anxiety, the small number of Muslims was surrounded by difficulties, and despair hung like a cloud over everything.

The words of this verse indicate how difficult the circumstances were, and how much consolation and reassurance God was giving the Messenger ﷺ in those conditions, and how much calm and refreshment was being bestowed upon his nerves.

Another point, which they kept repeating, was that the Prophet ﷺ was presenting this Book on his own authority. It is said: "Produce ten surahs like it, and call upon whomever you can besides God for help in this endeavour."

Classical exegetes have said that this challenge was in graduated order: first came the challenge to produce a Qur'an like this Qur'an, then the challenge of ten surahs, and finally the challenge of a single surah. But there is no transmitted proof for this particular sequence of the challenge. Apparently the evidence is against it, because Surah Yunus was revealed before this surah, and in it a single surah is challenged, whereas the present surah was revealed after it and contains the challenge of ten surahs. It is also a fact that the revelation of verses did not follow the arrangement of the surahs, for sometimes a verse was revealed and was placed in earlier surahs, and sometimes it was placed in a surah that was revealed after that verse. The determination of the time of revelation rests entirely on transmitted evidence. There is no narration among the occasions of revelation that proves Surah Yunus was revealed after Surah Hud, and a conjectural ruling of one's own on this subject is not acceptable.

The late Allamah Rashid Rida made an effort to explain a specific reason for the challenge of ten surahs. He made a lengthy attempt in this regard (see Tafsir al-Manar, pp. 32 to 41, vol. 12). He states that the challenge here refers to the challenge of the stories of the Qur'an. Investigation shows that among the surahs in which lengthy narratives were revealed, up to the revelation of Surah Hud their number was ten; therefore a challenge was given for ten surahs here, because the challenge of a single surah was more difficult for them than the challenge of ten surahs. This is because ten surahs would, in any case, contain more stories and more styles of expression, and those to whom the challenge was given would have needed ten surahs' worth of imitation if they were to copy it.

But the reality is known to God alone. This matter is not as difficult as they have made it, because in the matter of the challenge one must keep in view both the objections of those who raised them and the circumstances of revelation, since the Qur'an kept being revealed in response to practical situations, and at the time of the revelation of each surah and verse there was a specific set of circumstances. Therefore in some situations it was said, "Bring a book like the Qur'an"; in some it was said, "Bring a surah"; and in some a demand for ten surahs arose. It is not necessary that these demands be in chronological order, because the real purpose of the challenge was: produce speech like the essence of the Qur'an, whether the whole Qur'an, or a part, or a single surah, and so on. Thus the challenge concerned speech like the Qur'an, not a particular quantity. When the opponents were rendered helpless, they were rendered helpless by speech like the Qur'an; it was not that they could not produce any surah. Therefore, on this subject, the mention of the whole and of a part is equivalent, and no order is required in this regard. Rather, the mention of a quantity occurred because of certain specific circumstances, that is, according to the nature of the objections raised by the objectors, it was said: produce one surah, ten surahs, or the entire Qur'an. What those specific circumstances were, today we certainly cannot determine.

"And call upon whomever you can besides God, if you are truthful." (Call upon your associates and your adversaries, call upon the poets and the eloquent, call upon jinn and humans alike, and accept this challenge and produce ten fabricated surahs of your own, if your claim is true, that the Qur'an has been composed by the Prophet ﷺ himself and is not from God.)

Whoever strives in this world will receive the fruit of his striving. Now the matter depends on his aim. Some people keep their eyes on lofty purposes and high horizons, while others look only at their own feet, with near and limited goals before them. Whoever seeks the worldly life and its glitter, they strive only for it. Their deeds' result is given to them in this very world, and then they benefit from it as they wish. But in the Hereafter their share is nothing but the Fire, because such a person has earned nothing for the Hereafter and has not given it any importance. Therefore, whatever good deed he does in the world, its reward will be given to him here, and in the Hereafter that deed will be void; it will have no weight there. In the Hereafter the deeds of such people will be made void, just as a grazing animal is destroyed by poisonous grass: it appears to be fattening, while in reality it is ill, and this apparent fatness is the cause of its destruction.

In this world we see many individuals and nations who work day and night for this world, and they do receive the fruits of their efforts. Their worldly life is highly developed and prosperous, and it swells up just as a sick animal swells. Therefore we should not be impressed by such people, nor should we ask "why?", because in the earth this is the law of God: ﴿Whoever desires the worldly life and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they will not be denied anything therein.﴾ But while accepting this Sunnah of Allah and holding its results as certain, we must not forget this truth: a person can keep the Hereafter in view while working for this world, and while striving in worldly affairs he can also work for the Hereafter. It is possible that his worldly life is good and adorned, that he lacks nothing in this world, and that he also succeeds in the Hereafter.

The truth is that working for the Hereafter does not contradict working for this world; rather, worldly work also counts as work for the Hereafter, provided that turning toward Allah remains established. If a person remembers Allah in his worldly striving, his striving does not decrease but rather is increased in blessing. His earnings become pure and lawful, and along with this world he also receives the Hereafter. Except that whoever in this world follows forbidden desires and unlawful passions, they are not only rejected in the Hereafter, but in this world too they are not approved. The Western nations have experienced this in their individual and collective lives, and those who have studied human history have also clearly reached these conclusions.

Now the discourse turns to the attitude that the polytheists have adopted towards the Messenger of Allah. It is explained that the truthfulness of the Prophet (ﷺ) is from Allah, and that this Qur'an also bears witness to the Prophet's (ﷺ) prophethood and truth. And that the Prophet (ﷺ) is a messenger sent by Allah, and the Book of Moses also bears witness to this. Thus all the proofs and arguments concerning the Messenger of Allah and his call are set forth. In this way, the aim is to comfort the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ). Also intended is to encourage the small community that is working with him for this great purpose. And it is also intended to warn the opponents and disbelievers of their evil end, that if they do not change their course, their end is the Fire. They are presented with one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection, in which they are subjected to shame, disgrace and humiliation, merely because they adopted arrogance and pride in the world. It is shown that these people are now boasting in vain. How utterly humiliated and helpless they will be on the Day of Resurrection, and there will be no opportunity to escape Allah's punishment, nor will they have any protector or helper.

Undoubtedly, in the Hereafter it is they who will be the greatest losers (لاجرم انهم فی الآخرة هم الاخسرون: "Undoubtedly, in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers"). Now (in the following verses) a comparative observation is made between the disbelievers and the believers, and the difference between them is made clear, showing how different their state and final outcome are. Read carefully:

Whoever strives in this world will receive the fruit of his striving. Now the matter depends on his aim. Some people keep their eyes on lofty purposes and high horizons, while others look only at their own feet, with near and limited goals before them. Whoever seeks the worldly life and its glitter, they strive only for it. Their deeds' result is given to them in this very world, and then they benefit from it as they wish. But in the Hereafter their share is nothing but the Fire, because such a person has earned nothing for the Hereafter and has not given it any importance. Therefore, whatever good deed he does in the world, its reward will be given to him here, and in the Hereafter that deed will be void; it will have no weight there. In the Hereafter the deeds of such people will be made void, just as a grazing animal is destroyed by poisonous grass: it appears to be fattening, while in reality it is ill, and this apparent fatness is the cause of its destruction.

In this world we see many individuals and nations who work day and night for this world, and they do receive the fruits of their efforts. Their worldly life is highly developed and prosperous, and it swells up just as a sick animal swells. Therefore we should not be impressed by such people, nor should we ask "why?", because in the earth this is the law of God: ﴿Whoever desires the worldly life and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they will not be denied anything therein.﴾ But while accepting this Sunnah of Allah and holding its results as certain, we must not forget this truth: a person can keep the Hereafter in view while working for this world, and while striving in worldly affairs he can also work for the Hereafter. It is possible that his worldly life is good and adorned, that he lacks nothing in this world, and that he also succeeds in the Hereafter.

The truth is that working for the Hereafter does not contradict working for this world; rather, worldly work also counts as work for the Hereafter, provided that turning toward Allah remains established. If a person remembers Allah in his worldly striving, his striving does not decrease but rather is increased in blessing. His earnings become pure and lawful, and along with this world he also receives the Hereafter. Except that whoever in this world follows forbidden desires and unlawful passions, they are not only rejected in the Hereafter, but in this world too they are not approved. The Western nations have experienced this in their individual and collective lives, and those who have studied human history have also clearly reached these conclusions.

Now the discourse turns to the attitude that the polytheists have adopted towards the Messenger of Allah. It is explained that the truthfulness of the Prophet (ﷺ) is from Allah, and that this Qur'an also bears witness to the Prophet's (ﷺ) prophethood and truth. And that the Prophet (ﷺ) is a messenger sent by Allah, and the Book of Moses also bears witness to this. Thus all the proofs and arguments concerning the Messenger of Allah and his call are set forth. In this way, the aim is to comfort the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ). Also intended is to encourage the small community that is working with him for this great purpose. And it is also intended to warn the opponents and disbelievers of their evil end, that if they do not change their course, their end is the Fire. They are presented with one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection, in which they are subjected to shame, disgrace and humiliation, merely because they adopted arrogance and pride in the world. It is shown that these people are now boasting in vain. How utterly humiliated and helpless they will be on the Day of Resurrection, and there will be no opportunity to escape Allah's punishment, nor will they have any protector or helper.

Undoubtedly, in the Hereafter it is they who will be the greatest losers (لاجرم انهم فی الآخرة هم الاخسرون: "Undoubtedly, in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers"). Now (in the following verses) a comparative observation is made between the disbelievers and the believers, and the difference between them is made clear, showing how different their state and final outcome are. Read carefully:

This passage (verses 17 to 24) is one long critical discourse. Through its hints and guidance, its varied reminders, warnings and forceful blows, it shows what difficulties the small number of Muslims and the Islamic call faced in that period of history, and why this allusive address was necessary at that time. It also shows that the Qur'an has a movement-oriented character: it gives directions for tireless struggle in an actual situation, and it is a guidebook for such movements until the Day of Judgment.

Only the person who has actually plunged into the battle for the revival of Islam can taste this Qur'an, the one who faces the same circumstances in which this Qur'an was first revealed, confronts those circumstances and turns them onto its path. As for those who sit comfortably in their homes wishing to understand the Qur'an and study it in a technical and purely academic manner, such comfort-seeking, cold-hearted and easy-living people cannot understand this Book, those who are far from the practical battle of life and have no interest in any Islamic movement. In short, the secrets of the Qur'an never open up to such comfort-seeking occupants of high seats. Those who are slaves to powers other than God, who are peace-loving and comfort-seeking, and who are content to live under any taghut system, for them the secrets of the Qur'an are like the light of the sun to a person born blind.

﴿Is then one who had a clear proof from his Lord, and a witness from Him recited it, and before it the Book of Moses as a guide and mercy? Such people believe in it. And whoever of the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place. So do not be in doubt about it; indeed it is the truth from your Lord, but most people do not believe.﴾ Then will he who had a clear proof from his Lord, followed by a witness from Him in confirmation of it, and before it the Book of Moses, a guide and mercy, (be like those of worldly mind who deny it?) Such people will certainly believe in it. Whoever of the human groups denies it, the Fire is the place promised for him. So, O Prophet, do not be in doubt about this thing; it is the truth from your Lord, but most people do not accept it.

Countless narrations have come down about the meaning of ﴿on a clear proof from his Lord﴾, what is meant by ﴿a witness recites it﴾, and to what the pronouns in ﴿from his Lord﴾ and ﴿recites it﴾ refer, and to whom the pronoun in ﴿from Him﴾ refers. In my view, the most preferred and appropriate meaning of this expression is that the one (namely the Messenger of Allah) who has clear evidence and proof from his Lord, and after the Messenger of Allah this will include all Muslims, and a further witness from Allah has come, which is an undeniable proof of his prophethood. That is the Qur'an, which itself indicates that it is divine revelation, and people have been unable to produce speech of this kind. And before this witness, that is before the Qur'an, the Book of Moses also exists, which confirms the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), because the Book contains clear glad tidings concerning the Messenger of Allah, and the teachings of that Book and its teachings are exactly alike.

The interpretation and explanation I have stated is also indicated by the style of this entire surah. In this surah all the messengers have expressed that they find proofs within their own selves from the Divine, and they have full certainty and observation that revelation comes to them from Allah. They find the Divine Being within themselves as most clear, most certain and most near, and they have observational certainty regarding the Divine Being and divine revelation. Observe how Noah said: ﴿He said, "O my people, tell me, if I am upon a clear proof from my Lord, and He has given me mercy from Himself, but it has been made obscure to you, shall we compel you to it while you are averse to it?"﴾ (28) "O brothers of my people, think, if I was standing on a clear witness from my Lord, and then He also favoured me with His special mercy, yet it was not visible to you, then what means do we have that you should refuse to accept it and we forcibly thrust it upon your heads?"

And Salih also said: ﴿He said, "O my people, tell me, if I am upon a clear proof from my Lord, and He has given me mercy from Himself, who will help me against Allah if I disobey Him? You would only add to me loss."﴾ (63) "O brothers of my people, have you considered that if I had a clear witness from my Lord and then He favoured me with His mercy, who then would save me from the grip of Allah? If I disobey Him, you cannot be of any use to me, except that you would put me into greater loss."

And Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) said something similar: ﴿He said, "O my people, tell me, if I am upon a clear proof from my Lord, and He has provided me from Himself with good provision"﴾ "O brothers, consider yourselves whether, if I was upon a clear witness from my Lord, and then He gave me good provision from His presence."

All these expressions show that a specific relationship of the messengers with the Divine is described in them. Its nature is such that they find within themselves a kind of insight through which they perceive the reality of divinity as a clear witness within themselves, because through revelation they have a relationship with the Lord like the relationship of a sight with what it observes. This manner of expression and uniformity of expression shows that these verses point to the personal relationship between Allah and the Messenger. Whereas we have said that this bayyinah means the inner witness of the Messenger, to which there is also an indication in the words of other messengers. And here the intention is to show that your observations are the same as those of the earlier messengers. Therefore all the claims of the polytheists of Makkah are false. The purpose of this is that you and your handful of followers should be consoled that they are upon the truth just as the earlier messengers were, and that the teaching the Muslims have accepted is the teaching of all the prophets.

Now the basic meaning of this verse will be that this Prophet, upon whose truthfulness countless proofs and evidences have been established, his faith and conviction and his doctrines are true, because on one hand he himself observes this faith within his own self and has certainty. And upon this certainty of his, from God there also constantly come witnesses in the form of the Qur'an, which are clear proof that this Qur'an too is coming from this same divine source. And the second, external witness is the Book of Moses, which was a guide and leader for the leadership of the Children of Israel and was a mercy, whose revelation was sent down upon the Children of Israel from their Lord, and that Book also confirms the Messenger of Allah, because clear glad tidings concerning him are contained in it, and beyond those glad tidings this Book also agrees with the Qur'an in its fundamental concepts and principles. So is such a person worthy that he be denied as you people are doing, and as the various groups of polytheists are taking it up? This is evidently a most disliked matter, and in the face of such comprehensive proofs and evidences one should not adopt such a course of conduct.

After this, the position of those who believed in the Qur'anic teachings and accepted it is also stated, as well as that of those who denied it, and both are warned of their end.

﴿Such people believe in it. And whoever of the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place. So do not be in doubt about it; indeed it is the truth from your Lord, but most people do not believe.﴾ "Such people will certainly believe in it. Whoever of the human groups denies it, the Fire is the place promised for him. So, O Prophet, do not be in doubt about this thing; it is the truth from your Lord, but most people do not accept it."

Some exegetes have developed a difficulty regarding the meaning of the verse ﴿Such people believe in it﴾, especially in the case where ﴿one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord, and a witness from Him recites it﴾ refers to the person of the Messenger of Allah, as stated earlier. Because in that case ﴿such people﴾ would refer to the community of believers who believe in the revelation that comes to the Prophet, and by that revelation would be meant the same proofs that descend upon the Prophet. But there is no obstacle in this, because the pronoun in ﴿they believe in it﴾ refers to the Qur'an. The meaning will be that people believe in this witness, that is the Qur'an, and the Messenger of Allah is the first Muslim and the first believer in the things revealed to him, and the believers follow the faith of the Prophet. Elsewhere in Surah al-Baqarah it is said: "The Messenger believes in what was sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers too. Each one believes in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers." Here the faith of the Messenger of Allah and of these people has been stated together, and this style of expression is quite familiar in Qur'anic language. Therefore there is no difficulty in the meaning of this verse.

﴿And whoever of the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ "And whoever of the human groups denies it, the Fire is the place promised for him." And this is a promise that will not be broken, because its decree and arrangement have been made by Allah.

﴿So do not be in doubt about it; indeed it is the truth from your Lord, but most people do not believe﴾ "So, O Prophet, do not be in doubt about this thing; it is the truth from your Lord, but most people do not accept it." It is a fact that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not doubt the revelation that was coming to him, nor did any suspicion ever overtake him regarding it. He was upon a special witness from his Lord. But after these proofs and evidences, this guidance was given to the Prophet so that the Prophet would not feel constriction in his heart, and would not grow weary while preaching. And because of the multitude of opponents and their severe hostilities, he feared that the call might fall into a state of stagnation, so these instructions were given to him only for consolation, so that he would continue his work with the utmost steadfastness. Moreover, the Muslim community too was in a state of anguish, distress and narrowness of heart, and in the same way the wind of doubt had blown upon their hearts.

In our age, Islamic movements everywhere face the same kind of circumstances. Everywhere they face such difficult conditions and are afflicted by states of anxiety and narrowness of heart. From every side they are subjected to ridicule and mockery, and people turn away from their call. They are being given the harshest of persecutions, and every intellectual, psychological and material means is being employed against them. From every side the forces of jahiliyyah have fallen upon them. Local non-Islamic powers and global powers are busy day and night in conspiracies against them, a total war against them has begun, and those who work against Islamic movements are being encouraged from every side. In such circumstances Islamic movements have an enormous need for such divine consolations.

It is the duty of all Islamic movements to reflect carefully upon these verses, to understand each and every phrase of them, to derive guidance from the instructions contained in them, and to keep moving forward along their lines.

The emphasis, assurance and truth which Allah is stating in these verses is the first necessity of the Islamic movement. Once again reflect: ﴿So do not be in doubt about it; indeed it is the truth from your Lord, but most people do not believe.﴾ Today every worker of the Islamic movement needs such a shelter of compassion that always overshadowed all the messengers, and which held the station of a witness from the Lord of Majesty. It was a shadow of mercy from the Most Generous Lord. Under that shadow they moved toward their goal, and on that path they had no doubt about their success or the truth of that path. And whatever difficulties they faced on that path, they bore them, just as Salih said:

"O brothers of my people, have you considered that if I had a clear witness from my Lord and then He favoured me with His mercy, who then would save me from the grip of Allah? If I disobey Him, you cannot be of any use to me, except that you would put me into greater loss."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 11, verse 17 (part 2 of 2):

At present, the aims of the movements working for the revival of Islam in the Muslim world are the same as those for which the prophets were sent, namely the revival of Islam. The jahiliyyahs (periods and forces of ignorance) that those prophets confronted are the very same jahiliyyahs that these movements' vanguard units face today. Just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) presented the complete religion to all of humanity, the same religion is being presented to humanity today. It is as though that very era has returned. Today, Islamic movements confront the same jahiliyyah that Ibrahim faced, and that Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub, the Asbat, Yusuf, Musa, Harun, Dawud, Sulayman, Yahya, Isa, and all the other prophets faced.

Some jahiliyyahs outright deny the existence of the Creator, while others acknowledge the existence of the Creator. Yet even while acknowledging the existence of the Creator, they have set up on this earth people as lords and rulers who enforce laws that Allah has not sent down. In this way, people follow the religion of these lords. Today, throughout the Muslim world, the call of Islamic movements is that people, in all the circumstances of their lives, and from their whole society, should eliminate from their values and laws the rule and authority of these lords besides Allah, and enter fully into the lordship of Allah alone, entering in such a way that, in their lives, there is no other lord alongside the lordship of Allah. They should follow only the Shari'ah of Allah and observe only the commands and prohibitions of Allah. As a result of this ideological struggle, a comprehensive conflict now exists between Islam and jahiliyyah, and in this battle all the tawaghit (tyrannical powers) of the world stand in one line against the Islamic movements.

Therefore, it is the duty of these vanguard units of the Islamic movements to derive all their ideas, all their positions, and all their policies from the Qur'an. This is the meaning of what we repeatedly say: only the one who plunges into this kind of battle can taste the flavor of this Qur'an, the battle into which the Companions of the Messenger of Allah plunged, and who adopts the same stance and faces the same circumstances those people faced, and begins to change the course of events in the same way those noble figures changed it. Those who sit in seclusion searching for the meanings of the Qur'an, who do not practically strive for the revival of Islam, who acquire only the technical teaching of the Qur'an, and whose connection with it is merely at the level of speech, cannot attain the reality of the Qur'an. The understanding of the Qur'an by such people is merely rigid and very far from practical life.

Now the context turns toward those who claim that the Messenger (ﷺ) presents this Qur'an of his own accord, God forbid. These people deny both Allah and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They are now present in one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection, and the case of such fabricators is being presented before Allah. Whether their denial is that the Qur'an is sent down from Allah or not, or that they associate others with Allah, or that they make other human "gods" partners in Allah's sovereign authority, the verses are general so that every kind of fabricator is included in their meaning. In short, these people are presented in one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection; they are being exposed and humiliated, openly. In the same scene, on the other side, are the believers, standing at peace, and for them rewards from their Lord await. Allah presents the comparison of these two kinds of people in this way: on one side are the blind and the deaf, and on the other side are those who hear and see: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah? Those will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, "These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers (18), who hinder [others] from the way of Allah and seek to make it crooked, and they, of the Hereafter, are disbelievers (19). Those will not be able to escape on earth, and they will have no protectors other than Allah. Their punishment will be doubled. They were unable to hear, and they used not to see (20). Those are the ones who have lost themselves, and what they used to invent has gone astray from them (21). Undoubtedly, they will be the greatest losers in the Hereafter (22). Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds and humbled themselves to their Lord—those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally (23). The example of the two groups is like the blind and the deaf versus the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in comparison? Then will you not remember? (24)﴾

The telling of a lie is in itself a great crime, and upon whomever a lie is fabricated, it is a great injustice. But if this fabrication is against the Divine Being Himself, then it is a great crime and an extremely dreadful audacity. Because: ﴿Those will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, "These are the ones who lied against their Lord."﴾

Lied against whom? Against their own Lord, and not against anyone else. In this scene such people are thoroughly humiliated, and after that, as the punishment for this shameful crime, the curse and reproach descend upon them.

﴿Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.﴾ The witnesses will also bear this testimony. Who will these witnesses be? The angels, the Messengers, and the believers; all of God's creation will become witnesses. This will be an extremely great disgrace and public condemnation; there will be a great assembly, and before that assembly they will suffer this humiliation.

﴿Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.﴾ By "wrongdoers" are meant the polytheists. And these are the very people who fabricate lies against Allah in order to block the common people from the path of Allah, and ﴿seek to make it crooked﴾ ("yabghunaha 'iwajan"). They neither seek rectitude nor do they prefer the straight path. They are devoted to crookedness, evasion and deviation in every matter, whether they are upon a path, or in some state of living, or whatever matter confronts them. The real cause of this is ﴿and they, of the Hereafter, are disbelievers﴾ ("wa hum bil-akhirati hum kafirun"). The word "hum" has been brought twice, for the purpose of restriction and emphasis, and to show that this denial is ingrained in their very being, and that they deserve that this be their identifying mark. Those who associate partners with Allah are the ones called wrongdoers; when they turn away from the straight path of Islam and the even way, their aim is that the whole system of life be made crooked, and the currents of human thought become complicated.

Allah wishes that a person, walking upon the straight path, attain the station of honour; whereas servitude to other than Allah creates humiliation within the human self, and as a result oppression and transgression are nurtured within society, although Allah's purpose is that justice be established in every society. The striving of people is turned toward the pursuit of this worthless goal: that they wish to make the people of the earth their lords and gods, dance around humans, beat drums, and elevate them so much that these humans take the place of the true Lord—although these dwarfish and insignificant people, who are themselves creatures, how can they fill the void of the true Creator? The insignificant and dwarfish servants of these earthly lords strive day and night that the sovereignty of these false gods be established; these people carry out tireless effort. They keep these earthly idols lit at all times and continually direct people's attention toward their personalities. Around them, and at their shrines and resting-places, they keep festivals and drums beating, and through song, music and other diversions they keep proclaiming their praise and glorification; yet despite all these diversions and all this tireless exertion, no beneficial outcome emerges for humanity. What greater wretchedness for humanity could there be than that the entire striving of a human life should go to waste in this way?
