(Ulā'ika) These are the people who are themselves astray and also lead others astray, and who are deserving of blame and curse in the sight of Allah.

﴿Ulā'ika lam yakūnū mu'jizīna fil-ard﴾ "Their schemes are not capable of overpowering Allah. Therefore Allah can send down His punishment upon them whenever He wills, and even in this world."

﴿Wa mā kāna lahum min dūnillāhi min awliyā'﴾ "They had no supporter apart from Allah who could save them from Allah or help them against Allah. But Allah has granted these people a respite here for the punishment of the Hereafter, so that there they may be given the punishment of both this world and the Hereafter."

﴿Yudā'afu lahumu al-'adhāb﴾ "The punishment will now be doubled for them," because in the world they did not make use of those faculties through which they could have perceived the truth. They forcibly kept their eyes closed. They were like people who could neither hear nor see.

﴿Mā kānū yastaṭī'ūna as-sam'a wa mā kānū yubṣirūn﴾ "They neither could listen to anyone, nor did they have any perception of their own."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 21:

﴿Those are the ones who have lost their own selves.﴾ This is a very great and destructive loss, because in this business, whoever suffers a loss, no other person can come to his aid. People of this kind, by suffering this loss, have also wasted their worldly life: here they lost their human dignity. For a human being can attain dignity in this world only through the Islamic system of life. And they have also lost the Hereafter, because they denied the Hereafter, and as a result the punishment of the Hereafter awaits them.

﴿And that which they used to invent has departed from them.﴾ The false gods they had set up in the world have all vanished. Now no one is seen anywhere. All have disappeared and become lost.

Surah 11, verse 22:

﴿Inevitably, it is they who in the Hereafter will be the greatest losers.﴾ Such is their loss that, in this world and the next, there is no greater loss than theirs. They have ruined both their worldly life and their Hereafter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 23:

In contrast, there are the people of faith, and those who, having believed, also perform righteous deeds. They will be completely content from their Lord; they will have full assurance that they will receive the full reward for their righteous deeds. Extremely tranquil, far from every kind of anxiety and distress.

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and humble themselves [before their Lord]...﴾ (Wa akhbatu). Ikhbat means tranquility, steadfastness, certainty, and submission and contentment. This word presents a very beautiful picture of the relationship between a true believer and his Lord. The believer is wholly inclined towards Allah. Whatever state comes upon him from Him, he is content with it; there is a stillness within his self, his heart is at rest, and he attains a state of peace, steadfastness and contentment.

Now see the commentary on both (in the next verse).

This is a sensory portrayal in which both parties are presented in a concrete form. The first party is like one who is blind and cannot see anything, and like one who is deaf and cannot hear anything. Their faculties of perception are suspended, and they are incapable of grasping intelligible meanings. Since their organs of perception do not function, they are, as it were, deprived of those organs themselves, whereas the second party makes use of them: it hears and sees, and its intellect benefits from these faculties.

﴿أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ ("Will you not then take heed?"). At the end, a question is asked: can these two kinds of people be equal? No answer is given to this question, because what need is there for an answer?

Rather, a second question is put: will you not take a lesson from this example? ﴿أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ ("Will you not then take heed?"). This is because the matter is so clear that there is no need for any deep reflection upon it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 11, verse 25:

Lesson No. 100 at a Glance

The stories of the prophets form the central theme of this surah. However, the story is not the ultimate purpose in itself; the real purpose is the truth which these stories are being used to establish, and which is referred to in summary at the beginning of the surah: "Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book whose verses are made firm and then clearly explained, from One who is All-Wise and All-Aware. [Saying:] Worship none but Allah. I am a warner to you from Him and a bearer of good news. And [say:] seek forgiveness from your Lord and then turn to Him in repentance, and He will give you a good enjoyment until a specified term and will grant every person of virtue his virtue. But if you turn away, then I fear for you the punishment of a great Day. To Allah is your return, and He is over all things competent."

These truths have been discussed several times and repeatedly at the beginning of the surah. Through the systems of the heavens and the earth, the creation of the human soul, and the dialogues of the Day of Gathering, an attempt was made to impress these truths upon the mind. Now these truths are presented in relation to the people spread across the regions of the earth and their history. It is explained that this conflict between Islam and jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) is a historical conflict, and that it has continued in this same way since the beginning of creation.

These stories appear in this surah in some detail, especially the story of the Flood of Prophet Noah. In it there is the same ideological conflict that was mentioned at the beginning of the surah, and the same truths are the subject of dispute which every messenger has brought in every age. It is as if the deniers present today are the same ones who have been denying since before Noah. Their temperament is one, their thinking is alike, and just as the call of the messengers throughout human history is one, so too the response of the deniers is one. The stories in this surah follow historical order. It begins with Noah, then Hud, then Salih, with an allusion to Abraham, then the discussion moves to Lot, then Shu'ayb, and then the narrative proceeds with a reference to Moses. This historical order is maintained here because the purpose is to warn later people with the evil end of earlier ones, and to show that the conduct of all human history is alike.

The story of Noah is earlier both historically and in the surah, so here is the story of Noah, peace be upon him.

...

Lesson No. 100: Explanation of verses 25 to 49

...

Indeed, We sent Noah to his people: "Indeed, I am a clear warner to you. That you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful Day." (And such were the circumstances when) We sent Noah to his people. (He said) "I warn you plainly, that you worship none but Allah; otherwise I fear that a painful day's punishment will come upon you."

These are the same words that at the beginning of the surah are said about the advent of Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and his message: that this is a Book whose verses are firm and detailed, from a wise and all-aware Being, and that I am a warner and a bearer of good news from Him. By expressing the meaning and purpose of the call in the same kind of words, the aim is to establish that the mission and call of all the prophets have remained one; their doctrines have remained one, and for this reason the mode of expression has also been adopted in a similar way. It is also an established fact that the words of Noah himself are not quoted here; rather their meaning has been rendered in Arabic, and this is the preferred view, because we do not know what language Noah spoke.

"We sent Noah to his people": "(And such were the circumstances when) We sent Noah to his people. (He said) 'I warn you plainly.'"

Here the phrase "he said" is not brought in the Qur'anic text. One reason is that the style of the Qur'an is as if Noah stands before us, a living and moving scene is before us, and he is delivering an address while we listen. Therefore the narrative and reported past mode has not been adopted. Second, the duty of prophethood is described here in very brief words and concise meaning: "I am a plain warner to you." This style firmly fixes the aims of prophethood in the conscience of the hearers.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 26:

﴿أَن لَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا اللَّهَ﴾ "That you worship none but Allah." This defines the objective of the Prophethood: the Messenger presents to you only this fundamental initial truth, and if it is not accepted, there is the fear of the punishment of God coming upon you.

﴿إِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾ "Otherwise, I fear that a painful day's punishment will come upon you." These are the foundational realities of Prophethood and of warning: that I warn you of this destruction, and nothing more; and in these brief words, all the objectives of Prophethood have been briefly set down in writing.

"Yawmin Alim" (a painful day). The day is not painful. Alim means mu'lim (painful). Alim in the sense of ma'lum (known, felt). In reality, people will be in pain on that day. But for greater emphasis, this mode of expression has been adopted: that on that day even time will feel the pain; the day itself will feel the hardships of that day. From this one can gauge how painful the condition of the people will be.

This is the reply of the arrogant elites, who sit at the head of every society. This same reply was given to the Messenger (ﷺ) by the arrogant ones of his people, the Quraysh. They too would say: "We see you as nothing but a human being like ourselves, and those among our people of lowest standing have followed you without thinking, because the common people do not have deep thought. What superiority do you have over us? Therefore we consider you a liar."

The same doubts, the same accusations, the same pride and arrogance, and the same ignorance and shallow understanding that the people of Nuh adopted, these people too are afflicted with this disease.

Among humankind there has always been the ignorance that a human being cannot bear prophethood, and that if a human being were to be granted the office of prophethood, then this office should be given to a king or to some creature higher than him. This is an extremely foolish and senseless notion: that the human being, whom Allah has made His vicegerent on this earth and entrusted with the heavy responsibility of earthly vicegerency, is not fit for the office of prophethood. For the office of earthly vicegerency is itself a great office, and it is evident that Allah must have placed within the human being capacities by which he could discharge it. Therefore Allah may grant to some individuals of the human species an even greater capacity, so that through it they may discharge the responsibilities of prophethood, and He may entrust these responsibilities to whomever He wills among His creatures. For Allah alone knows in whom He has placed this capacity, so that He may also place this office in him.

The second misunderstanding that has always afflicted people is that even if Allah grants this office to someone, it is the right of the great and the wealthy, because they already dominate their people and hold a high rank. In reality this is ignorance of the values that Allah has deemed honourable for this human creation, and because of which the human being became worthy of earthly vicegerency, and then among them some of higher rank were deemed fit for the office of prophethood. These values are not connected with wealth, rank, or worldly power. They are connected with the human soul, and with whether a soul possesses the particular strength that can maintain a connection with the higher world. For this connection what is needed is not wealth and riches, nor honour and rank, but special spiritual powers and capacities, which enable one to accept this great trust, the mission of calling, and these values, and which also include the ability to endure hardships on this path. That is, the qualities necessary for the office of prophethood. These qualities are not connected with wealth or status, nor with social position.

But, on the contrary, the thinking of the elite classes of the people of Nuh (peace be upon him) was, as the elite classes of every society think, because on account of their high rank they become blind and remain incapable of perceiving the station of prophethood. They believe that no human being can be a prophet, and if one can be, then they themselves are entitled to that station.

"مَا نَرٰىكَ اِلَّا بَشَرًا مِّثْلَنَا" ("We see you as nothing but a human being like ourselves"): this is one point. The second is "وَمَا نَرٰىكَ اتَّبَعَكَ اِلَّا الَّذِيْنَ هُمْ اَرَاذِلُـنَا بَادِيَ الرَّاْيِ" ("And we see that only those among us who were of the lowest standing have followed you, without considered judgment"), 

These people refer to the poor by the word "arazil" (the lowest, the base), and the arrogant always regard as base those who are not granted wealth and power. Yet in the case of the messengers and Islamic movements, it is always the poor and the sound-natured who take interest first, and in comparison with the high-born they accept the truth quickly. Their hearts are more closely attached to the One Lord, who is exalted and dominant, because wealth, luxury, and rebellion have not corrupted their nature. Therefore the obstacles on their path to accepting the truth are fewer. The poor do not fear that by accepting Islam they will lose the position which, through the heedlessness and ignorance of the common people, they have acquired, and which has plunged the masses into idol-worship and king-worship. And the greatest idol-worship is when people, leaving Allah, make their fellow humans great, give them dominion over the earth, and follow and worship them. The call of all the messengers is in fact a call for the common people to be freed from servitude to their fellow human beings. This is why the elites of society are the first to oppose this call, and the common masses are also summoned not to accept it; and they challenge the Messenger's call, level accusations against him, and turn people away from him.

Consider the words of these people: "We see that only those among us who were of the lowest standing have followed you, without considered judgment." They have not reflected upon your call. This is the accusation which, in every age, the high and influential classes of society level against the believers: that they are simple-minded and lack reflection. And it is not fitting for great people to follow the common people. Now, since these have become believers, how can we become believers, since great people cannot follow the faith and call of small people?

"وَمَا نَرٰي لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِنْ فَضْلٍ" ("And we see no merit in you over us"): now they make one and the same comment against both the caller and his followers, that the believers have no superiority over us such that you would be considered more rightly guided, or that you are closer to truth than we are. Had there been any such thing, we would have been ahead of you. In short, they measure guidance by worldly pursuits: since in worldly pursuits no one is ahead of us, how has someone become ahead in religion? Because we understand matters well, and we hold power, therefore only the wealthy and the powerful can be superior, and only they can be more discerning.

When the belief in the Oneness of Allah disappears from a society, its mentality becomes the one mentioned above. Whenever the belief in tawhid has been lost, people have returned to jahiliyyah and adopted idol-worship in various forms. Although such a society may appear outwardly very orderly and advanced, in reality it is the backwardness of all humanity, because such a society belittles the values through which a human being becomes human, and through which the human being became worthy of earthly vicegerency, and through which the human being was granted the office of prophethood from the higher world. These are the very concepts by which the human being is distanced from the higher world and drawn near to pure animality, materiality, and physicality.

"بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كٰذِبِيْنَ" ("Rather, we think you are liars"): this is the final accusation which they lay upon the Messenger and his followers. But even in this they speak with their arrogant bearing: "We think, we have the impression," which is the cautious manner of speech adopted by this wealthy class. For in their view, to believe every matter and to speak plainly is a vulgar thing, and foolish people of superficial opinion believe immediately. It is the great ones who speak with reserve and caution in a thoughtful manner.

This is the temperament of those who are wealthy, who lead lives of idleness, who consider themselves great, and whose necks are thick and whose bellies are swollen.

Sayyid Qutb's commentary (Fi Zilal al-Quran), Urdu translation, on Surah 11, verse 28:

Hazrat Nuh bears these accusations, this arrogance and this defiance with exceptional good manners. With certainty, steadfastness, and in a most composed manner, he presents before them the truth that Allah has revealed to him. He speaks with great clarity, addressing them in a well-ordered way, with profound awareness and conviction. He does not speak in their language, he does not answer an accusation with an accusation. He does not make a claim that he does not make. He does not give an exaggerated picture of himself instead of the true impression. He speaks before them most truthfully about his prophethood and the office of prophethood.

﴿Qala ya qawmi﴾ ("O my people"). How refined and sincere is this address of a caller to the faith! He attributes them to himself and himself to them. He says: you object that I am only a man like you, and on the surface your objection appears correct. But if I have a prophetic connection with my Lord, then consider how dangerous the consequences of your opinion could be for you. I certainly maintain a clear connection with my Lord, I am aware of it, and this is a distinction from which you are deprived. Allah has given me the office of being His Messenger, and this is a mercy from Him upon me, or He has bestowed upon me qualities by which I have become the bearer of this mercy of Allah, and this is indeed a great mercy. Consider also this position: if this mercy were upon me, and you could not comprehend it, because you are so devoid of reason that you are deprived of even perceiving this great reality, and you cannot see it, then what other means do we have to force this reality into your minds? Neither can I do so, nor is it among my duties. Especially when you dislike accepting it. When a chasm of hatred intervenes, how can you ever understand?

Hazrat Nuh (peace be upon him) gently draws their attention to this reality and stirs their feelings, so that they may strive to understand these lofty truths and come out of the misunderstanding and heedlessness in which they are caught regarding prophethood. He tries to make them understand that the matter of prophethood is not as superficial as they are taking it to be. Yet, in this gentle speech, Hazrat Nuh is teaching them this great principle: the matter of belief rests purely on a person's understanding, and the choice of a belief depends on an individual's own reflection and thought. In this matter no one can be compelled, and no belief can be imposed on anyone, however much coercion and violence anyone may wish to employ to adopt it.

"O my people, those whom you call base are the ones I invited, and they accepted my invitation and believed. My demand from people is only that they believe; beyond that I have no claim upon them. For the call I am giving, I am not entitled to ask any payment from them. Were it otherwise, I would be pursuing the wealthy in opposition to the poor. In my view all people are equal, whether poor or rich. For one who has no interest in the wealth of people, the poor and the rich are alike.

﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾: solely from Allah, and I seek no recompense of any kind from anyone else.

﴿Nor will I drive away those who have believed﴾: This shows that perhaps they had made such a demand, or had given hints that they could not sit together with these common people. If these people were removed, they might consider believing, for they cannot sit in the assembly of Nuh with these base people, nor can they bear that great people like us should follow the way of these base ones. "I am not one who drives away those who have believed"; that is, it is not possible for me to do so. They have believed; now let them and their Lord be the judge.

﴿Indeed, they are to meet their Lord﴾: they themselves are going to appear before their Lord.

﴿But I see you are a people acting in ignorance﴾: that is, you cannot comprehend the values by which people are weighed in the scale of Allah. And you also do not grasp the reality that all people must return to Allah."

Allah exists; He is the Lord of the poor and also the Lord of the rich. He is the Protector of the weak and also the Support of the powerful. The values that carry weight with Allah are different. There, there is only one scale: the scale of faith in Allah (ترازوئے ایمان باللہ). Therefore, these people who have already believed are now under the protection of their Lord.

"And O my people, who would help me against Allah if I drove them away?" (وَيٰقَوْمِ مَنْ يَّنْصُرُنِيْ مِنَ اللّٰهِ اِنْ طَرَدْتُّهُمْ) — "Who would save me from the grip of Allah if I drove away these people? When I have trampled underfoot the values Allah has established, and begun to oppress the servants of Allah who have believed and accepted the call. These people are honoured with Allah. In that case, I would in fact become the one who establishes your values, whereas Allah has sent me as a Messenger precisely so that I might overturn these corrupt values, not so that I myself would follow them."

"Will you not then reflect?" (اَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُوْنَ) — "Can it be that this simple matter does not reach your understanding? The values you are following are corrupt, and they have made you forget the natural values."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 31:

After this, Hadrat Nuh (peace be upon him) presents before them the reality of his own personality and prophethood in an extremely clear manner, in the form of simple and unartificial facts. The personality of the Messenger and the office of prophethood are presented completely apart from the counterfeit values of the world. This is so that they may understand the truth and know what the true values are in the sight of Allah, so that the apparent values of the world become separate before them, and the true values become clear, pure and distinct, so that the Messenger and prophethood stand before them in their real form, without any embellishment, whether they accept it or not. Thus it is said:

﴿And I do not say to you that with me are the treasures of Allah﴾: "And I do not tell you that I have the treasures of Allah." Therefore I neither claim wealth nor have the power to make you wealthy.

﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾: "Nor do I say that I know the unseen." So that I do not claim a power that ordinary human beings do not possess, apart from the connection of prophethood.

﴿Nor do I say that I am an angel﴾: "Nor do I claim that I am an angel." So that I do not claim some false quality higher than ordinary human beings, and become higher in your eyes, and thereby get you to acknowledge my leadership and dominion.

﴿Nor do I say of those whom your eyes look down upon that Allah will not grant them any good﴾: "And I cannot say that those whom your eyes regard with contempt, Allah has given them no good." So that in this way I may please the arrogant ones of society, or in this way I may go along with your worldly superficial values and temporary customs.

﴿Allah knows best what is in their souls﴾: "Allah alone knows best what is within their souls." Only Allah knows the reality of these people. I can only treat them according to their outward condition, and their outward state deserves that I respect them and hope that Allah will make their end good.

﴿Indeed, then I would be of the wrongdoers﴾: "If I said such things, I would be among the wrongdoers." If I had made any of the claims mentioned above, then in that case I would be committing oppression in the guise of truth, whereas I have been commanded to propagate the truth. I would also be oppressing myself by making myself deserving of the wrath of Allah, and I would be oppressing people too, because I would be giving them a station that Allah has not given them.

In this way, Hadrat Nuh (peace be upon him) strips from his own person and from his office of prophethood those false values which his people had associated with the concept of the Messenger and the concept of prophethood. He presents the Messenger and prophethood before his people in their true form, and presents these realities purified of all superficial and fabricated conceptions, because no truth needs artificial colouring. He presents the truth in its true form, with its true strength, and presents it with a most loving appeal, so that they may turn towards it and, if it is written in their destiny, take their share. In short, there is in the call of Hadrat Nuh neither deception, nor any adulteration, nor any pretence, nor any sacrifice of a true value. He presents a simple and straightforward matter in its true form. He does not seek the pleasure of anyone other than Allah, and he gives to the whole of human history a model of presenting the call: present the truth in its true form, without any deception, and without seeking the pleasure of anyone other than Allah. However, it should be in a most encouraging style.

Now at this point the people of Noah are overcome by the contest of Noah's sincerity, Noah's arguments and Noah's method. So they resort to obstinacy: they answer love and reason with arrogance and stubbornness, and, abandoning the path of debate and reflection, they turn to issuing a challenge.

At last these people said: "O Noah, you have disputed with us and have argued with us a great deal. Now then, bring upon us that punishment with which you threaten us, if you are truthful."

This is a strange manner: humility has put on the garment of strength. Weakness is displaying power. In truth these people are afraid, yet by denying with their tongues and by propping up their words with challenge, they make a false display of bravery.

Fa'tinā bimā ta'iduna in kunta mina al-ṣādiqīn ("Bring upon us that which you promise us, if you are among the truthful"): "Now then, bring upon us that punishment with which you threaten us, if you are truthful." Send down upon us now that painful punishment with which you have been frightening us. We are in no way going to affirm you, and we no longer pay any heed to your threat.

Now look at Noah's reaction. This denial and this hostile challenge did not divert him from his religious mission or from the straight path of the Messenger of the Most Merciful. He does not withdraw his hand from preaching truth and reality. He continually presents that truth before them, reminding them of the lesson they had forgotten, even though their attitude is extremely ignorant, and they demand that he bring the punishment. He answers them: "O my brothers, I am only a Messenger, and my responsibility is only to convey the message to you. As for the punishment of Allah, it is subject to the command of Allah, and it is Allah who directs all affairs. It is Allah who decides whether to bring the punishment quickly or to postpone it to a certain time. It will come in accordance with His sunnah, and there is never any deviation in the sunnah of Allah. A prophet can neither change the sunnah of Allah nor turn its course. The duty and responsibility of the Messenger is only that he continues to convey the message until his last moment. Because of people's denial, aversion and challenge, the Messenger never abandons his work."

"If the requirement of the sunnah of Allah is that you be destroyed because of your misguidance, then this sunnah will certainly be enforced upon you, however much I strive. This is not because Allah prevents you from benefiting from my advice, but because you are using your power of discernment in such a way that, in accordance with the sunnah of Allah, you will reach that end. And in this matter you cannot make Allah powerless. You are always within His power; it is Allah who directs affairs, and He determines the faults. To Him you all shall return, and you shall be called to account and become deserving of reward and punishment."

﴿He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned﴾

---

The narrative now takes a sudden turn in its direction of address. At this point the address turns to the Quraysh and the polytheists of Makkah as well, because their condition was the same as that of the people of Prophet Nuh (Noah). Their claim was that Muhammad (ﷺ) fabricates these stories on his own. So, in the middle of the account, the speech is abruptly interrupted to answer this objection, and afterwards the story resumes.

----

Fabricating lies against Allah is indeed a grave crime. O Prophet, say to them: if I have committed this crime, then its sin is upon me. Since I know that it is a very great crime, how could I commit it? And as for the criminal accusation you are leveling against me, I am also free of responsibility for it. Moreover, there are other crimes you yourselves are committing, namely shirk (associating partners with Allah) and denial (takdhib), and I am free of those too.

This interjected statement does not seem out of place in the context of the narrative, because the very purpose and aim of the narrative's context is precisely what has been made explicit in this sentence.

Now the story of Nuh resumes, and its second scene comes into view. Nuh now receives guidance from his Lord, and the commands of Allah come to him thus:

﴿And it was revealed to Nuh: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed. So do not be distressed over what they have been doing."﴾ : "It was revealed to Nuh that those among your people who have already come to faith are the only ones; no one else will believe now."

Those hearts that were inclined to accept faith have already accepted it; those who remained behind no longer have the capacity to believe within them, nor do they have any inclination towards it. This was Allah's final notification to Hadrat Nuh, and it came from Allah, and Allah is All-Knowing. Therefore, there was no longer any benefit in continuing the campaign of invitation. And it was said that he should no longer be concerned about their disbelief, denial, mockery and ridicule.

﴿So do not grieve over what they have been doing﴾ : "Stop grieving over their deeds." You should cease feeling sorrow and anguish over your failure. And do not concern yourself with what these people have done and what they are doing. Do not worry about yourselves; they cannot cause you any harm at all. Nor should you feel sorrow for them, since there is no expectation of good from them. Therefore, bring their matter to an end here.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 11, verse 37:

وَاصْنَعِ الْفُلْكَ بِاَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا: "And construct the ship under Our eyes and according to Our revelation." In accordance with Our will and Our instructions.

وَلَا تُخَاطِبْنِيْ فِي الَّذِيْنَ ظَلَمُوْا ۚ اِنَّهُمْ مُّغْرَقُوْنَ: "And do not plead with Me concerning those who have done wrong; indeed, they are to be drowned." Do not intercede with Me on behalf of those who have wronged, for they are all now destined to drown.

The matter concerning them has already been decided, and their end has already been determined. Therefore, do not speak to Me about such people. Do not pray for their guidance, nor pray against them, because another place in the Holy Qur'an mentions that Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) invoked evil upon them. Hence it appears that this despair came after that. When the decision had been made, addressing Allah on this matter became forbidden.

Now a third scene comes into view. Hazrat Nuh (peace be upon him) is building the ark.

وَيَصْنَعُ الْفُلْكَ (wa yasna'ul-fulk, "and he was making the ark"). Observe the manner of expression: the present action is conveyed with the present-tense verb (fi'l mudari'). This creates an atmosphere of great seriousness and activity. Now, lost in our imagination, we see Hazrat Nuh building the ark, while the people of his nation pass by him in groups and mock him. And whom are they mocking? The one who told them that he was the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds, who invited them, who debated with them, and whose dialogue with them had continued for a long time. Yet this Prophet is now doing the work of a carpenter. And these people mocked because they could only see outward matters. The commands and guidance of Allah behind this action were hidden from their sight. They were looking at outward matters like cattle. The divine wisdom and the decree of Allah working behind the outward circumstances were behind a veil. As for Nuh (peace be upon him), he was completely at peace. What Allah has decreed will come to pass. In the face of their mockery, he was engaged in his work with great composure, dignity and grandeur. He kept saying: ﴿If you mock us, then we too mock you, just as you mock﴾ ("If you mock at us, then indeed we mock at you, just as you mock"). We are mocking you because you are ignorant of the background of matters and events. Allah's decree awaits you, and your end is about to come to light.

فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُوْنَ ۙ مَنْ يَّاْتِيْهِ عَذَابٌ يُّخْزِيْهِ وَيَحِلُّ عَلَيْهِ عَذَابٌ مُّقِيْمٌ۔

﴿So you will soon know who it is upon whom will come a punishment that will disgrace him, and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment.﴾

Soon you will come to know upon whom comes a punishment that humiliates him, and upon whom a calamity descends that will not be averted. Consider: will we be the ones who deserve this punishment, or you? Wait a little for the curtain to fall.

Now a third scene comes into view. Hazrat Nuh (peace be upon him) is building the ark.

وَيَصْنَعُ الْفُلْكَ (wa yasna'ul-fulk, "and he was making the ark"). Observe the manner of expression: the present action is conveyed with the present-tense verb (fi'l mudari'). This creates an atmosphere of great seriousness and activity. Now, lost in our imagination, we see Hazrat Nuh building the ark, while the people of his nation pass by him in groups and mock him. And whom are they mocking? The one who told them that he was the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds, who invited them, who debated with them, and whose dialogue with them had continued for a long time. Yet this Prophet is now doing the work of a carpenter. And these people mocked because they could only see outward matters. The commands and guidance of Allah behind this action were hidden from their sight. They were looking at outward matters like cattle. The divine wisdom and the decree of Allah working behind the outward circumstances were behind a veil. As for Nuh (peace be upon him), he was completely at peace. What Allah has decreed will come to pass. In the face of their mockery, he was engaged in his work with great composure, dignity and grandeur. He kept saying: ﴿If you mock us, then we too mock you, just as you mock﴾ ("If you mock at us, then indeed we mock at you, just as you mock"). We are mocking you because you are ignorant of the background of matters and events. Allah's decree awaits you, and your end is about to come to light.

فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُوْنَ ۙ مَنْ يَّاْتِيْهِ عَذَابٌ يُّخْزِيْهِ وَيَحِلُّ عَلَيْهِ عَذَابٌ مُّقِيْمٌ۔

Soon you will come to know upon whom comes a punishment that humiliates him, and upon whom a calamity descends that will not be averted. Consider: will we be the ones who deserve this punishment, or you? Wait a little for the curtain to fall.

The commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 11, verse 40:

And when Our decreed time arrives and the oven gushes forth, the scene unfolds as follows:

"Until, when Our command came and the oven boiled over, We said: 'Load into it a pair of every kind, two of each, and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and those who believe.' And none believed with him except a few."

How did the oven boil over? Some sayings are far-fetched, being based on conjecture, and some carry the flavour of Isra'iliyyat (narratives from Jewish and Christian sources). As for us, we do not wander through uninhabited valleys without guidance. The reports the Quran gives are reports of the Unseen (al-ghayb), and in this matter one should stop at the limit the Quran itself specifies, and should not add further marginal speculation to the apparent meaning of the text.

At most we can say that a fountain gushing from the oven, especially from an oven in operation, could be that a spring of water burst forth from it, or that volcanic activity began within it, and that Allah appointed this as the final warning signal and danger for Noah, or that it was a part of the arrival of Allah's punishment. Simultaneously, water began to well up from the earth and torrential rain began to pour from the sky.

When these events began, Allah gave the command:

قُلْنَا احْمِلْ فِيْهَا مِنْ كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ ("We said: Load into it a pair of every kind, two of each"). The practical system required that Noah be given commands at the proper time for each stage. First it was said to him that he should build the ship, and he began to build it; and in the context of the discourse it was not stated why this command was being given, nor was it stated that Noah himself had been informed of it.

حَتّٰٓي اِذَا جَاۗءَ اَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ التَّنُّوْرُ ("Until, when Our command came and the oven boiled over"). And after this, a command was given for the second stage:

قُلْنَا احْمِلْ فِيْهَا مِنْ كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ وَاَهْلَكَ اِلَّا مَنْ سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ الْقَوْلُ وَمَنْ اٰمَنَ ("We said: Load into it a pair of every kind, two of each, and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and those who believe").

Now, regarding the meaning of زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ too, there is difference of opinion among the commentators; and most of this difference is a matter of personal taste and carries an Isra'ili colouring. Therefore, we do not gallop our imagination regarding this verse either, as to how many pairs of living creatures Noah took with him and which he did not. This is merely groping in the dark.

وَاَهْلَكَ اِلَّا مَنْ سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ الْقَوْلُ وَمَنْ اٰمَنَ ("and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and those who believe"). That is, those who, according to the Sunnah of Allah, have already become deserving of punishment.

وَمَنْ اٰمَنَ ("and those who believe"): that is, apart from your family, those people who have believed.

وَمَآ اٰمَنَ مَعَهٗٓ اِلَّا قَلِيْلٌ ("And none believed with him except a few"): that is, only a few people believed along with Noah.

Thus the command of Allah was carried out, and those who were destined to perish perished.

In the name of Allah be its course and its anchoring. The meaning of "Bismillah majreha" is that now this ship is in the hands of Allah's will. Its sailing upon the water, and then its coming to rest at some point, is in accordance with the laws of Allah's will. When uncontrollable waves rise, the limits of human strength come to an end in them, and both the human being and the ship are handed over to the storm, and then it is Allah, the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful, who decides.

Now the scene that is coming up (in the following verses) is extremely frightening, namely the storm and the drowning of the disbelievers.

Here two fears meet: the silent fear of nature and the fear of the human soul.

﴿And it sailed with them through waves like mountains﴾: the ark was carrying them along, and each wave rose like a mountain.

Noah saw such frightening conditions that one of his sons was running away from him and was not boarding the ark with them. Here a father's hidden paternal affection awakens, and he calls out to that misguided son.

﴿And Noah called out to his son, who was apart [from them], "O my son, board with us and do not be with the disbelievers."﴾ The son was at a distance. Noah called out, "Son, board with us, and do not remain with the disbelievers."

But this disobedient son pays no heed to his affectionate father. He is young and arrogant, and cannot judge how severe the storm is, and he says:

﴿He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water."﴾ He replied, turning back, "I will climb a mountain right now, and it will save me from the water."

But the compassionate father knows how terrible this punishment is, and he makes a final appeal: ﴿He said, "Today there is no protector from the command of Allah, except for the one on whom He has mercy."﴾ Noah said, "Today nothing can save from the command of Allah, except for the one whom Allah shows mercy."

Neither mountains can avert Allah's punishment, nor can anyone hide from it in caves. No one can stand against it, and no one can save. Only the one upon whom Allah's mercy descends can be saved.

﴿And a wave came between them, and he was among those who were drowned.﴾ Meanwhile a wave came between the two of them, and he too was among those who drowned. Thousands of years have passed, yet even today, when we imagine this terrifying situation, our breath stops and such awe overtakes us that it is as if this scene is before our eyes. The ark is tossing amid waves like mountains. Noah repeatedly calls out to his son, and his arrogant son refuses and keeps climbing the mountain. Suddenly a huge wave like a mountain comes, and in the blink of an eye the matter is over. All affairs end; now there is neither calling nor refusal.

This frightening scene can be contemplated from two aspects. One is that between father and son there is a real and living bond. The other is the natural disposition of man: after the storm has enveloped mountains and valleys, it now reaches out to envelop human children. Both kinds of feelings exist within the personality of a human being, and the Qur'an has portrayed them beautifully.

The address now turns to the earth and the sky, as though they understand. Both comply. The earth began to absorb and swallow up the water, and the sky stopped raining. The water went into the belly of the earth, and the surface of the earth returned to its normal state. What Allah had willed was accomplished, and this ship came to rest upon Mount Judi.

"And it was said: Away with the people of the wrongdoers." This is a short sentence, yet it expresses a very decisive and final outcome, and it contains great depth. The style "it was said" (qīla) leaves the speaker unnamed. The meaning is that this chapter has now been closed, and "bu'dan lil-qawm" (ba'dan lil-qawm) means: now they have been annihilated, they have been removed from life, they have fallen far from the mercy of Allah, and now they have passed from the memory of the people and have been erased from the history of nations.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 45:

When this calamity passes, the state of fear departs, and the ship comes to rest on Mount Judi, then a real father's heart is stirred with pain and his grief increases. He calls upon his Lord, saying: "My son is from my family, and Your promise is true, and You are the most just of judges. Your judgments are based on wisdom and planning."

Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) was saying this so that Allah would fulfil the promise He had made, and this promise concerned the salvation of his family members. Moreover, Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) also wished to inquire about the wisdom behind the promise and the judgment.

The answer to this question is very important. The truth had escaped Noah's notice: in Allah's standard of right and wrong, blood and kinship hold no status. Here the importance lies in ideological kinship. Your son was not a believer, therefore he was no longer a member of your family. You are a prophet and the first of the believers, and this answer was given in a most decisive and plain manner, and in a tone of severe admonition and questioning.

In the reply it was said: "He said: O Noah, he is not of your family; he is indeed a deed unrighteous. So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge. I admonish you lest you become one of the ignorant."

This is a great principle of the religion of Islam. The root to which all the threads lead is the root of creed. In Islam, the fundamental relationship between one individual and another is the relationship of faith. Lineage and kinship hold no significance here.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 46:

He said: "O Noah, he is not of your family; he is indeed (an act) of unrighteous conduct." He has cut himself off from you, and you have cut yourself off from him, even though he is your real son, because in Islam the real bond and connection is the ideological bond, and no other bond or strength is recognised within the Islamic community.

The circumstances in which Noah made his supplication were such that his supplication was not accepted, and therefore the answer given to him contains a measure of warning and admonition.

﴿So do not ask Me for that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, I advise you, lest you be among the ignorant.﴾ "Therefore do not request from Me that whose reality you do not know. I advise you not to make yourself like the ignorant." Out of fear of this, I give you an earnest admonition, lest you err in understanding the reality of Islamic ties and the nature of Islamic brotherhood, or err in understanding what Allah promised. Allah's promise has indeed been fulfilled, and all of your household and dependants have been saved, and this is the truth.

Upon hearing this admonishing reply, Noah trembled, just as a true believer trembles when the thought comes to him that some error or impropriety may occur in the presence of Allah. Thereupon Noah immediately repented and sought forgiveness.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 47:

The mercy of Allah enveloped Prophet Nuh (Noah), and his heart was reassured. He, his progeny, and his companions were saved, while the others were swept away by the flood.

The matter ends here. Prat Nuh (Prophet Nuh) receives good news: his believing companions are saved, and from them a believing lineage continues. As for those among them who only desired basic progress and worldly provisions, they are given the good news of a painful punishment. At the beginning of the surah too, this same good news and this same warning were given to the people. And it was for this very purpose that these stories were brought here, so that through examples and scenes the people might be made to understand.

After the introduction to the surah and these illustrations, the conclusion is drawn as follows: ﴿That is from the news of the unseen﴾ and so on. O Prophet, these are reports of the unseen which We reveal to you. Neither you nor your people knew them before this. So be patient, for the ultimate outcome belongs to the God-fearing (muttaqun).

This final commentary shows the purposes for which the stories of the Qur'an were brought:

• That the revelation is from Allah, which the polytheists of Makkah denied. The stories prove revelation in this way: neither the Arabs nor any other nation had any record of these narratives. These are accounts of the unseen, and everyone knew beforehand that the Prophet (ﷺ) had no means of acquiring such knowledge. This revelation was coming from the All-Wise, the All-Aware.

• The second purpose of bringing these stories is that, from Noah, who is the second Adam for mankind, down to the present day, the creed and belief of all the prophets has remained one. The message of all the prophets has been one, and their modes of expression have also been nearly one.

• These stories are meant to show that the objections raised by all the deniers have been of one kind. Although signs and proofs were presented to them, and although in the history of the prophets these objections have been repeatedly proven false, yet the same objections are repeated again and again.

• To state the truth of what the messengers gave glad tidings of and what they warned against, and that today the Prophet (ﷺ) too gives glad tidings and warnings about the same matters. This is historical testimony to the truthfulness of the Prophet (ﷺ).

• And to show what is the divine sunnah (the established divine way and law, sunnat Ilahiyyah) that is operating and prevailing in this universe: it makes no concession for anyone, nor does it consider any kinship. The essence is that the final outcome is for the righteous. In the end, the divine sunnah must prevail.

• The reality of the bonds that will exist in the Islamic system between one individual and another, and between one generation and the next, is that they are based solely on the Islamic creed, which makes all Muslims brothers, whose God is one, and whose Lord and Sovereign is Allah alone, with no partner and no rival to Him.

....

Now there are several questions about the flood of Noah. The first question is whether this flood covered the whole earth or was confined to the region in which Noah was sent. Where was that land, what were its boundaries in the ancient world, and how far do its boundaries extend in the modern world? These are questions which are answered only through conjecture and estimation, and conjecture and estimation cannot establish certainty or truth. Or else these questions are answered from Israʼiliyyat (narratives derived from Jewish and Christian sources), and Israʼiliyyat itself is a doubtful record. Moreover, in relation to the purposes for which the Qur'an has narrated these stories, the answers to these questions have no importance at all.

However, from the texts of the Qur'an there are indications that in the time of Noah, the whole population was that to which Noah had been sent, and that the people of Noah lived in a region where the human population of that time resided. The flood enveloped that entire region in which humans lived, and only those who were in the Ark of Noah were saved from its destruction.

This great cosmic event, about which the Qur'an informed us, while the Qur'an is the only authentic document of it, is also an event of the period of pre-history. Written human history is silent about it, for at that time there was no record of history. Human history is a thing of recent times, and even the record that history has produced contains the possibility of much error: a historical event may be both true and false. Such events can be examined by the rational principles of criticism and evaluation. It is not appropriate to ask about this from any other source when a truthful informant has already given information about it, for if we were to seek such matters from elsewhere, we would be turning things upside down, and no intellect in which the reality of religion has firmly settled would accept it.

At present, among the numerous nations inhabiting the world, the ancient, complex and unauthenticated literature of many of them also mentions the flood of Noah. These accounts state that in ancient times such a flood once passed, and that this great calamity befell those nations because of their disobedience and ignorance. The stories compiled by the Children of Israel, which they call the Old Testament, also contain a mention of the flood of Noah. But in regard to what the Qur'an has said about the flood of Noah, it is not fitting to mention those Israʼili stories. One should not mix the true and clear stories of the Qur'an with those obscure-origined, complex fables that have no chain of authority behind them. Although from all these stories one reality becomes clear and emerges before us: that a flood also struck the lands of those nations, or that those people who survived in the Ark of Noah, and their descendants wherever they went, carried those memories from one place to another by oral transmission from chest to chest. Thus those people spread across the regions of the world and populated the earth.

It should be carefully noted here that none of the documents called the Holy Book, whether the Old Testament made up of the books of the Jews or the New Testament made up of Christian literature, is a revelation sent down from Allah. This is because the copy of the Torah which Allah had revealed was destroyed and distorted by the people of Babylon, at the time when they enslaved all the Jews and took them captive to Babylon. Until about five centuries before the coming of Jesus, the Old Testament could not be compiled again even in book form. It was compiled by Ezra the priest, and it is possible that Ezra is in fact ʿUzayr, who gathered the remaining parts of the Torah. Whatever exists besides the Torah is their own composition. The same is the case with the Gospels. Their contents are the matters preserved in the memories of the disciples of the Messiah, and they were written down only about a century after Jesus was raised up. After that, countless stories, tales and fables were also gathered into them. Therefore the guidance to Muslims is that they should not consider anything in these books to be guidance.

Now we must see what lesson a person derives from this story. The truth is that there are many aspects of lesson in it for mankind; it is not just one lesson. In the following pages we will point out some of them, and after that the discussion will return to the story of Hud.

....

From the story of Noah, the characteristics of his people that become apparent are these: these people were extremely ignorant. They insisted stubbornly upon falsehood and continually rejected the pure call of Noah. Yet his call was that our Creator is the one Allah, and it is the duty of all human beings to serve that one God alone, to regard Him as their King and Ruler, and not to consider anyone other than Allah as sovereign.

The people of Noah were from the progeny of Adam, and the story of Adam has already been mentioned earlier in Surah al-Aʿraf. Likewise, it has also been mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah. Adam was sent down from Paradise to the earth so that he might discharge the duty of vicegerency (khilafah) on this earth, and this is the responsibility for which Allah had placed all the capacities within Adam. The lapse that occurred in Paradise was pardoned after Allah taught him words for his forgiveness. He learned certain words from Allah, and after he recited them, Allah forgave him. After this, Allah took a covenant from him, from his wife and from his descendants, that whenever a messenger came to them from Allah with guidance, they would surely believe in him. And that they would not follow Satan, because Satan is their own enemy, the enemy of their offspring, and an enemy until the Day of Resurrection.

Now Adam descended from Paradise to the earth as a Muslim, descended in obedience to Allah's instructions. There is no doubt that Adam, generation after generation, arranged for the instruction of his descendants in Islam. And Islam is the first and true way of life that humanity learned and was taught, because in the face of Adam there was no other lineage and no other creed. And when, centuries after Adam, Noah appeared (although today we have no means of knowing how long after Adam Noah came), in that period all the descendants of Adam had abandoned Islam and adopted the creed of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance). The details of that jahiliyyah are given by the Qur'an in this story. So we can say with certainty that the present idolatries, mythological tales, superstitious beliefs, idol-worship, false conceptions and false customs of jahiliyyah were imposed upon mankind by its environment and its jahiliyyah, and that man was originally upon the straight path, and that he became misguided and became a follower of jahiliyyah through the ill-fated endeavor of the accursed Satan. This misguidance was imposed upon him because, alongside Satan's external efforts, Allah had placed certain weaknesses within the human soul itself, and by exploiting these weaknesses Satan misled man, who is an enemy of Allah as well as the eternal enemy of man. Satan attacks man successfully at the time when man does not firmly hold on to Allah's guidance in every matter, great or small. Allah created man and gave him a measure of choice. And this very power of discernment and choice is for him a cause of trial. If he uses this power of discernment rightly and holds firmly only to Allah's rope and guidance, then the designs of his enemy Satan will have no effect upon him. And man also has the option to deviate from this guidance, even if the deviation is slight. When a person commits even a slight deviation, Satan then throws him far away from Islam and the straight path, and eventually makes him a complete follower of jahiliyyah, just as the people of Noah adopted jahiliyyah. And this process is completed only after the changes of centuries, the knowledge of which belongs to Allah alone.

The fact that Islam is the creed through which this world first became acquainted, and that this creed is that deity, sovereign, supreme authority and Lord is Allah alone, leads us to the conclusion that the view of so-called scholars of religions, and of those who make comparative studies of religions, that the belief in Tawhid (the oneness of God) has evolved step by step until it reached its present form, and that it passed through various stages before that present form, is merely a hypothesis and has no reality. Their notions are that earlier people believed in many paths: they considered natural forces to be deities, then they considered spirits to be deities, then they considered the sun, moon and various stars to be deities. The reality of the views of these people is that they first connect religions with the psychological, political and environmental circumstances of people. In this way they, in effect, deny the heavenly religions and put into people's minds the idea that religious concepts also passed through various stages to reach their present position, and that the environment of the times played a part in these changes and developments. Thus these people, in fact, by denying divine revelation and the office of prophethood, seek to prove that all religions and their fundamental concepts are also made by humans and are the product of human thought.

Now let us examine the approach of those who write about the revealed religions and who are influenced by those Western scholars. These people fall into the same error, and they conduct their research according to the method devised by the Orientalists, and unconsciously they fall into the same mistake into which their teachers, the Orientalists, fell. But the regrettable thing is that Muslim writers of this kind, in their own opinion, are defending Islam and are its supporters, yet in reality they uproot Islam and deny those true principles and beliefs of Islam whose affirmation is found throughout the whole Qur'an. The Qur'an, with great clarity and in very plain words, establishes the belief that Adam (peace be upon him) descended from Paradise to the earth with a complete Islamic view of life and Islamic beliefs, and then, centuries later, Nuh (Noah) invited the descendants of Adam to that same Islam, but Satan led them astray and plunged them into idol-worship. These beliefs and principles were based on complete Tawhid. After Nuh, this satanic cycle began again, and it returned the people to jahiliyyah. After this, messengers kept coming at intervals, seizing humanity and placing it back on the straight path, and they continued to give it a worldview based on absolute Tawhid. It is completely false to say that any change or development has occurred in the correct beliefs contained in the revealed Scriptures. Rather, if any development and change has occurred, it has occurred in those legal systems which were established at various times on the basis of the Islamic worldview. If some change and development has occurred in one of the beliefs of jahiliyyah, how does that prove that a process of evolution has also occurred in the Islamic worldview? And if some evolutionary process has occurred in the beliefs of jahiliyyah as well, then that too has occurred because of the influence of the true belief of Tawhid of Islam, which from time to time affects generations. Despite the fact that later generations have deviated from the belief in Tawhid, they have gradually continued to come closer to the belief in Tawhid. As for the belief in Tawhid, in its reality it is the oldest belief in history, and it existed before all idolatrous beliefs. Since the time Adam presented it, it has always existed in its original form. This is because the belief in Tawhid is not an invention of the human mind, but has come from Allah. Since the time Allah created man and taught him the belief in Tawhid, this belief has existed, and since that very time it has existed in this form. This is the truth; it has come from Allah, and from the very first day it has been in its complete form.

This is the reality which the Qur'an presents as an unshakeable truth, and upon this reality the whole Islamic conception of life rests. Therefore no Muslim researcher, especially one who takes up the pen in defence of Islam, can ignore this reality, nor can he conduct research along any line other than these lines, because the notions about religions that are found among Arab scholars are incorrect, and they have been compiled for a specific purpose.

Here in Fi Zilal al-Quran we could discuss such incorrect notions in detail, since for this I have a separate book in preparation, whose title will be "Necessary Corrections in Islamic Thought in the Present Age." However, here we will present one topic by way of example, to show what some researchers say and what the Qur'an says. Ustadh Aqqad, in his book "Allah," writes:

Man has progressed in beliefs just as he has progressed in knowledge. And just as he has progressed in knowledge, he has progressed in crafts. In the early period, his beliefs were as his life was; the same circumstances apply to his knowledge and crafts. Therefore the knowledge and crafts of his early period are no more advanced than the religions and worships of his early period, and the elements of truth in any one of them are no more than the elements of truth found in any other.

It is likely that in the matter of religion, human efforts have been far greater than human efforts in the field of knowledge and crafts.

The reason for this is that reaching this great truth of the universe is a far more difficult task than reaching the truth of those scattered things and isolated items, the attainment of which is only sought in a purely scholarly or purely industrial sense.

Look how the sun rises every day, and it is among the things of this universe which are completely apparent and which the human body perceives. Until the recent past, people's ideas about it were that the sun revolves around the earth, and astronomers used to present explanations about the movements of the sun and its conditions in the way that riddles are explained, or merely describe imaginations. But no one dared to deny the sun altogether, because the ideas people held about the sun were in layers of thick darkness, and perhaps even now people remain in darkness about the sun.

Therefore, the return of people in the ancient periods of jahiliyyah to the principle of religion does not prove that there is no reality to religiosity, or that religiosity attempts things that are impossible. What is known from the study of religions is only this: that the great truth did not appear to people all at once, and they could not understand the supreme truth in a single era. People became ready to grasp the great truth only after the passing of ages, and in this path they had to traverse long roads, and they reached this truth by reflecting through various methods, just as they discovered other smaller truths after a patience-testing struggle.

The comparative study of religions has shown that a countless number of facts on which people of the earliest period believed were proven false, and even today the remnants and examples of those people exist among the backward tribes of the world; indeed, even among those civilized nations which have a fairly long history of culture and civilization, such people are found. The purpose of the science of comparative religion is nothing other than this. And it is not possible that the religions of the early period were free of the ignorance and misguidance that we have mentioned. This is the reasonable conclusion which can be expected from any reasonable mode of thinking. There is nothing astonishing in this mode of thought that any scholar would regard as far-fetched, or that would lead anyone to adopt a new view about the reality and authenticity of religion. Those researchers of the science of religions who are searching for whether any such truth existed in the earliest religions, or whether they had a concept of truth free of every kind of doubt and suspicion, are chasing the impossible.

In the chapter "Evolution in the Concept of God" of this book, he writes:

Scholars of comparative religion agree that in the early conception of religion among the peoples, the concept of God and the concept of Lord passed through three stages. In the first period there was polytheism; then in the second period people distinguished among these gods and lords and gave preference to one over others (henotheism); and at the very end came the period of monotheism.

In the early period the number of lords was tens or even hundreds of lords and gods. In that period every family and every tribe had its own god; this god was either considered a god in itself or a deputy god, and people sought refuge in it, and this god accepted sacrifices and worship.

The second period, called the period of distinction and preference, although the gods and lords remained numerous in it, some of these lords and gods became more prominent than others for various reasons. For example, if a tribe became politically dominant in a region or country, its deity also became dominant in the region, and people sought from that god help for economic needs and protection from calamities. Some gods became prominent because, according to people's assumptions, they were more beneficial to more people and fulfilled more of man's demands than other gods. For example, the rain god was widely revered in areas where rain was needed, or gods of greater fear, such as the god of calamities or the god of storm and rain; that is, where there was fear, people feared that god, and where there was hope, people hoped in that god. In short, in this universe, the concept of gods also took shape in accordance with other natural phenomena.

In the third period, when tribes took the form of nations and peoples, despite the existence of various lords, they devised a common method of worship, and different methods of worship became prevalent among different regions and different nations. A distinctive feature of this period was that just as one nation imposed its authority, leadership, dominance and culture on other nations, so too it imposed its method of worship on them. Sometimes the rulers accepted the gods of the vanquished, just as a king accepts the words of his courtiers; in this way a relationship of follower and followed was established among them.

The consideration of the secrets and mysteries of the universe was included in worship, and talk of the profound wisdom working behind this universe began. Among those nations and peoples, true lordship was accorded to Allah, and all other good-ranked gods began to be given the station of angels, or were declared to be gods who had been cast out from the sacred enclosure of Allah, that is, were evil.

Now there are several questions about the flood of Noah. The first question is whether this flood covered the whole earth or was confined to the region in which Noah was sent. The flood enveloped that entire region in which humans lived, and only those who were in the Ark of Noah were saved from its destruction.

This great cosmic event, about which the Qur'an informed us, while the Qur'an is the only authentic document of it, is also an event of the period of pre-history. Written human history is silent about it, for at that time there was no record of history. Human history is a thing of recent times, and even the record that history has produced contains the possibility of much error: a historical event may be both true and false. Such events can be examined by the rational principles of criticism and evaluation. It is not appropriate to ask about this from any other source when a truthful informant has already given information about it, for if we were to seek such matters from elsewhere, we would be turning things upside down, and no intellect in which the reality of religion has firmly settled would accept it.

At present, among the numerous nations inhabiting the world, the ancient, complex and unauthenticated literature of many of them also mentions the flood of Noah. These accounts state that in ancient times such a flood once passed, and that this great calamity befell those nations because of their disobedience and ignorance. Although from all these stories one reality becomes clear and emerges before us: that a flood also struck the lands of those nations, or that those people who survived in the Ark of Noah, and their descendants wherever they went, carried those memories from one place to another by oral transmission from chest to chest. It should be carefully noted here that none of the documents called the Holy Book, whether the Old Testament made up of the books of the Jews or the New Testament made up of Christian literature, is a revelation sent down from Allah. So we can say with certainty that the present idolatries, mythological tales, superstitious beliefs, idol-worship, false conceptions and false customs of jahiliyyah were imposed upon mankind by its environment and its jahiliyyah, and that man was originally upon the straight path, and that he became misguided and became a follower of jahiliyyah through the ill-fated endeavor of the accursed Satan. This misguidance was imposed upon him because, alongside Satan's external efforts, Allah had placed certain weaknesses within the human soul itself, and by exploiting these weaknesses Satan misled man, who is an enemy of Allah as well as the eternal enemy of man. Satan attacks man successfully at the time when man does not firmly hold on to Allah's guidance in every matter, great or small. Allah created man and gave him a measure of choice. And man also has the option to deviate from this guidance, even if the deviation is slight. When a person commits even a slight deviation, Satan then throws him far away from Islam and the straight path, and eventually makes him a complete follower of jahiliyyah, just as the people of Noah adopted jahiliyyah. And this process is completed only after the changes of centuries, the knowledge of which belongs to Allah alone.

The fact that Islam is the creed through which this world first became acquainted, and that this creed is that deity, sovereign, supreme authority and Lord is Allah alone, leads us to the conclusion that the view of so-called scholars of religions, and of those who make comparative studies of religions, that the belief in Tawhid (the oneness of God) has evolved step by step until it reached its present form, and that it passed through various stages before that present form, is merely a hypothesis and has no reality. Their notions are that earlier people believed in many paths: they considered natural forces to be deities, then they considered spirits to be deities, then they considered the sun, moon and various stars to be deities. The reality of the views of these people is that they first connect religions with the psychological, political and environmental circumstances of people. In this way they, in effect, deny the heavenly religions and put into people's minds the idea that religious concepts also passed through various stages to reach their present position, and that the environment of the times played a part in these changes and developments. Thus these people, in fact, by denying divine revelation and the office of prophethood, seek to prove that all religions and their fundamental concepts are also made by humans and are the product of human thought.

Now let us examine the approach of those who write about the revealed religions and who are influenced by those Western scholars. These people fall into the same error, and they conduct their research according to the method devised by the Orientalists, and unconsciously they fall into the same mistake into which their teachers, the Orientalists, fell. This is the reality which the Qur'an presents as an unshakeable truth, and upon this reality the whole Islamic conception of life rests. The reason for this is that reaching this great truth of the universe is a far more difficult task than reaching the truth of those scattered things and isolated items, the attainment of which is only sought in a purely scholarly or purely industrial sense.

Until the recent past, people's ideas about it were that the sun revolves around the earth, and astronomers used to present explanations about the movements of the sun and its conditions in the way that riddles are explained, or merely describe imaginations. Therefore, the return of people in the ancient periods of jahiliyyah to the principle of religion does not prove that there is no reality to religiosity, or that religiosity attempts things that are impossible. What is known from the study of religions is only this: that the great truth did not appear to people all at once, and they could not understand the supreme truth in a single era. People became ready to grasp the great truth only after the passing of ages, and in this path they had to traverse long roads, and they reached this truth by reflecting through various methods, just as they discovered other smaller truths after a patience-testing struggle.

The comparative study of religions has shown that a countless number of facts on which people of the earliest period believed were proven false, and even today the remnants and examples of those people exist among the backward tribes of the world; indeed, even among those civilized nations which have a fairly long history of culture and civilization, such people are found. The purpose of the science of comparative religion is nothing other than this. And it is not possible that the religions of the early period were free of the ignorance and misguidance that we have mentioned. This is the reasonable conclusion which can be expected from any reasonable mode of thinking. There is nothing astonishing in this mode of thought that any scholar would regard as far-fetched, or that would lead anyone to adopt a new view about the reality and authenticity of religion. Those researchers of the science of religions who are searching for whether any such truth existed in the earliest religions, or whether they had a concept of truth free of every kind of doubt and suspicion, are chasing the impossible.

In the chapter "Evolution in the Concept of God" of this book, he writes:

Scholars of comparative religion agree that in the early conception of religion among the peoples, the concept of God and the concept of Lord passed through three stages. In the first period there was polytheism; then in the second period people distinguished among these gods and lords and gave preference to one over others (henotheism); and at the very end came the period of monotheism.

In the early period the number of lords was tens or even hundreds of lords and gods. In that period every family and every tribe had its own god; this god was either considered a god in itself or a deputy god, and people sought refuge in it, and this god accepted sacrifices and worship.

The second period, called the period of distinction and preference, although the gods and lords remained numerous in it, some of these lords and gods became more prominent than others for various reasons. For example, if a tribe became politically dominant in a region or country, its deity also became dominant in the region, and people sought from that god help for economic needs and protection from calamities. Some gods became prominent because, according to people's assumptions, they were more beneficial to more people and fulfilled more of man's demands than other gods. For example, the rain god was widely revered in areas where rain was needed, or gods of greater fear, such as the god of calamities or the god of storm and rain; that is, where there was fear, people feared that god, and where there was hope, people hoped in that god. In short, in this universe, the concept of gods also took shape in accordance with other natural phenomena.

In the third period, when tribes took the form of nations and peoples, despite the existence of various lords, they devised a common method of worship, and different methods of worship became prevalent among different regions and different nations. A distinctive feature of this period was that just as one nation imposed its authority, leadership, dominance and culture on other nations, so too it imposed its method of worship on them. Sometimes the rulers accepted the gods of the vanquished, just as a king accepts the words of his courtiers; in this way a relationship of follower and followed was established among them.

A nation reached even this weak form of mental unity only after a long struggle for civilization, and it reached the next stage when a considerable amount of knowledge and understanding came into existence within it, and because of that knowledge and understanding it became difficult for a human being to accept purely ignorant concepts. Then man began to attribute to God the better qualities that were closer to God's purity and holiness, from the rubble of his earlier concepts. The consideration of the secrets and mysteries of the universe was included in worship, and talk of the profound wisdom working behind this universe began. Among those nations and peoples, true lordship was accorded to Allah, and all other good-ranked gods began to be given the station of angels, or were declared to be gods who had been cast out from the sacred enclosure of Allah, that is, were evil.
