In the chapter "Evolution in the Concept of God" of this book, he writes:

Scholars of comparative religion agree that in the early conception of religion among the peoples, the concept of God and the concept of Lord passed through three stages. In the first period there was polytheism; then in the second period people distinguished among these gods and lords and gave preference to one over others (henotheism); and at the very end came the period of monotheism.

In the early period the number of lords was tens or even hundreds of lords and gods. In that period every family and every tribe had its own god; this god was either considered a god in itself or a deputy god, and people sought refuge in it, and this god accepted sacrifices and worship.

The second period, called the period of distinction and preference, although the gods and lords remained numerous in it, some of these lords and gods became more prominent than others for various reasons. For example, if a tribe became politically dominant in a region or country, its deity also became dominant in the region, and people sought from that god help for economic needs and protection from calamities. Some gods became prominent because, according to people's assumptions, they were more beneficial to more people and fulfilled more of man's demands than other gods. For example, the rain god was widely revered in areas where rain was needed, or gods of greater fear, such as the god of calamities or the god of storm and rain; that is, where there was fear, people feared that god, and where there was hope, people hoped in that god. In short, in this universe, the concept of gods also took shape in accordance with other natural phenomena.

In the third period, when tribes took the form of nations and peoples, despite the existence of various lords, they devised a common method of worship, and different methods of worship became prevalent among different regions and different nations. A distinctive feature of this period was that just as one nation imposed its authority, leadership, dominance and culture on other nations, so too it imposed its method of worship on them. Sometimes the rulers accepted the gods of the vanquished, just as a king accepts the words of his courtiers; in this way a relationship of follower and followed was established among them.

A nation reached even this weak form of mental unity only after a long struggle for civilization, and it reached the next stage when a considerable amount of knowledge and understanding came into existence within it, and because of that knowledge and understanding it became difficult for a human being to accept purely ignorant concepts. Then man began to attribute to God the better qualities that were closer to God's purity and holiness, from the rubble of his earlier concepts. The consideration of the secrets and mysteries of the universe was included in worship, and talk of the profound wisdom working behind this universe began. Among those nations and peoples, true lordship was accorded to Allah, and all other good-ranked gods began to be given the station of angels, or were declared to be gods who had been cast out from the sacred enclosure of Allah, that is, were evil.

In the chapter "Evolution in the Concept of God" of this book, he writes:

Scholars of comparative religion agree that in the early conception of religion among the peoples, the concept of God and the concept of Lord passed through three stages. In the first period there was polytheism; then in the second period people distinguished among these gods and lords and gave preference to one over others (henotheism); and at the very end came the period of monotheism.

In the early period the number of lords was tens or even hundreds of lords and gods. In that period every family and every tribe had its own god; this god was either considered a god in itself or a deputy god, and people sought refuge in it, and this god accepted sacrifices and worship.

The second period, called the period of distinction and preference, although the gods and lords remained numerous in it, some of these lords and gods became more prominent than others for various reasons. For example, if a tribe became politically dominant in a region or country, its deity also became dominant in the region, and people sought from that god help for economic needs and protection from calamities. Some gods became prominent because, according to people's assumptions, they were more beneficial to more people and fulfilled more of man's demands than other gods. For example, the rain god was widely revered in areas where rain was needed, or gods of greater fear, such as the god of calamities or the god of storm and rain; that is, where there was fear, people feared that god, and where there was hope, people hoped in that god. In short, in this universe, the concept of gods also took shape in accordance with other natural phenomena.

In the third period, when tribes took the form of nations and peoples, despite the existence of various lords, they devised a common method of worship, and different methods of worship became prevalent among different regions and different nations. Sometimes the rulers accepted the gods of the vanquished, just as a king accepts the words of his courtiers; in this way a relationship of follower and followed was established among them.

The consideration of the secrets and mysteries of the universe was included in worship, and talk of the profound wisdom working behind this universe began. Among those nations and peoples, true lordship was accorded to Allah, and all other good-ranked gods began to be given the station of angels, or were declared to be gods who had been cast out from the sacred enclosure of Allah, that is, were evil.

In the chapter "Evolution in the Concept of God" of this book, he writes:

Scholars of comparative religion agree that in the early conception of religion among the peoples, the concept of God and the concept of Lord passed through three stages. The second period, called the period of distinction and preference, although the gods and lords remained numerous in it, some of these lords and gods became more prominent than others for various reasons. For example, if a tribe became politically dominant in a region or country, its deity also became dominant in the region, and people sought from that god help for economic needs and protection from calamities. Some gods became prominent because, according to people's assumptions, they were more beneficial to more people and fulfilled more of man's demands than other gods. For example, the rain god was widely revered in areas where rain was needed, or gods of greater fear, such as the god of calamities or the god of storm and rain; that is, where there was fear, people feared that god, and where there was hope, people hoped in that god. In the third period, when tribes took the form of nations and peoples, despite the existence of various lords, they devised a common method of worship, and different methods of worship became prevalent among different regions and different nations. Sometimes the rulers accepted the gods of the vanquished, just as a king accepts the words of his courtiers; in this way a relationship of follower and followed was established among them.

A nation reached even this weak form of mental unity only after a long struggle for civilization, and it reached the next stage when a considerable amount of knowledge and understanding came into existence within it, and because of that knowledge and understanding it became difficult for a human being to accept purely ignorant concepts. Then man began to attribute to God the better qualities that were closer to God's purity and holiness, from the rubble of his earlier concepts. The consideration of the secrets and mysteries of the universe was included in worship, and talk of the profound wisdom working behind this universe began. Among those nations and peoples, true lordship was accorded to Allah, and all other good-ranked gods began to be given the station of angels, or were declared to be gods who had been cast out from the sacred enclosure of Allah, that is, were evil.

• The reality of the bonds that will exist in the Islamic system between one individual and another, and between one generation and the next, is that they are based solely on the Islamic creed, which makes all Muslims brothers, whose God is one, and whose Lord and Sovereign is Allah alone, with no partner and no rival to Him.

Now there are several questions about the flood of Noah. The first question is whether this flood covered the whole earth or was confined to the region in which Noah was sent. Where was that land, what were its boundaries in the ancient world, and how far do its boundaries extend in the modern world? These are questions which are answered only through conjecture and estimation, and conjecture and estimation cannot establish certainty or truth. Or else these questions are answered from Israʼiliyyat (narratives derived from Jewish and Christian sources), and Israʼiliyyat itself is a doubtful record. Moreover, in relation to the purposes for which the Qur'an has narrated these stories, the answers to these questions have no importance at all.

However, from the texts of the Qur'an there are indications that in the time of Noah, the whole population was that to which Noah had been sent, and that the people of Noah lived in a region where the human population of that time resided. The flood enveloped that entire region in which humans lived, and only those who were in the Ark of Noah were saved from its destruction.

This great cosmic event, about which the Qur'an informed us, while the Qur'an is the only authentic document of it, is also an event of the period of pre-history. Written human history is silent about it, for at that time there was no record of history. Human history is a thing of recent times, and even the record that history has produced contains the possibility of much error: a historical event may be both true and false. Such events can be examined by the rational principles of criticism and evaluation. It is not appropriate to ask about this from any other source when a truthful informant has already given information about it, for if we were to seek such matters from elsewhere, we would be turning things upside down, and no intellect in which the reality of religion has firmly settled would accept it.

At present, among the numerous nations inhabiting the world, the ancient, complex and unauthenticated literature of many of them also mentions the flood of Noah. These accounts state that in ancient times such a flood once passed, and that this great calamity befell those nations because of their disobedience and ignorance. The stories compiled by the Children of Israel, which they call the Old Testament, also contain a mention of the flood of Noah. But in regard to what the Qur'an has said about the flood of Noah, it is not fitting to mention those Israʼili stories. One should not mix the true and clear stories of the Qur'an with those obscure-origined, complex fables that have no chain of authority behind them. Although from all these stories one reality becomes clear and emerges before us: that a flood also struck the lands of those nations, or that those people who survived in the Ark of Noah, and their descendants wherever they went, carried those memories from one place to another by oral transmission from chest to chest. Thus those people spread across the regions of the world and populated the earth.

It should be carefully noted here that none of the documents called the Holy Book, whether the Old Testament made up of the books of the Jews or the New Testament made up of Christian literature, is a revelation sent down from Allah. This is because the copy of the Torah which Allah had revealed was destroyed and distorted by the people of Babylon, at the time when they enslaved all the Jews and took them captive to Babylon. It was compiled by Ezra the priest, and it is possible that Ezra is in fact ʿUzayr, who gathered the remaining parts of the Torah. Whatever exists besides the Torah is their own composition. Now Adam descended from Paradise to the earth as a Muslim, descended in obedience to Allah's instructions. There is no doubt that Adam, generation after generation, arranged for the instruction of his descendants in Islam. And Islam is the first and true way of life that humanity learned and was taught, because in the face of Adam there was no other lineage and no other creed. So we can say with certainty that the present idolatries, mythological tales, superstitious beliefs, idol-worship, false conceptions and false customs of jahiliyyah were imposed upon mankind by its environment and its jahiliyyah, and that man was originally upon the straight path, and that he became misguided and became a follower of jahiliyyah through the ill-fated endeavor of the accursed Satan. This misguidance was imposed upon him because, alongside Satan's external efforts, Allah had placed certain weaknesses within the human soul itself, and by exploiting these weaknesses Satan misled man, who is an enemy of Allah as well as the eternal enemy of man. Satan attacks man successfully at the time when man does not firmly hold on to Allah's guidance in every matter, great or small. Allah created man and gave him a measure of choice. And this very power of discernment and choice is for him a cause of trial. If he uses this power of discernment rightly and holds firmly only to Allah's rope and guidance, then the designs of his enemy Satan will have no effect upon him. And man also has the option to deviate from this guidance, even if the deviation is slight. When a person commits even a slight deviation, Satan then throws him far away from Islam and the straight path, and eventually makes him a complete follower of jahiliyyah, just as the people of Noah adopted jahiliyyah. And this process is completed only after the changes of centuries, the knowledge of which belongs to Allah alone.

The fact that Islam is the creed through which this world first became acquainted, and that this creed is that deity, sovereign, supreme authority and Lord is Allah alone, leads us to the conclusion that the view of so-called scholars of religions, and of those who make comparative studies of religions, that the belief in Tawhid (the oneness of God) has evolved step by step until it reached its present form, and that it passed through various stages before that present form, is merely a hypothesis and has no reality. Their notions are that earlier people believed in many paths: they considered natural forces to be deities, then they considered spirits to be deities, then they considered the sun, moon and various stars to be deities. The reality of the views of these people is that they first connect religions with the psychological, political and environmental circumstances of people. In this way they, in effect, deny the heavenly religions and put into people's minds the idea that religious concepts also passed through various stages to reach their present position, and that the environment of the times played a part in these changes and developments. Thus these people, in fact, by denying divine revelation and the office of prophethood, seek to prove that all religions and their fundamental concepts are also made by humans and are the product of human thought.

Now let us examine the approach of those who write about the revealed religions and who are influenced by those Western scholars. These people fall into the same error, and they conduct their research according to the method devised by the Orientalists, and unconsciously they fall into the same mistake into which their teachers, the Orientalists, fell. These beliefs and principles were based on complete Tawhid. After Nuh, this satanic cycle began again, and it returned the people to jahiliyyah. If some change and development has occurred in one of the beliefs of jahiliyyah, how does that prove that a process of evolution has also occurred in the Islamic worldview? Since the time Allah created man and taught him the belief in Tawhid, this belief has existed, and since that very time it has existed in this form. This is the truth; it has come from Allah, and from the very first day it has been in its complete form.

This is the reality which the Qur'an presents as an unshakeable truth, and upon this reality the whole Islamic conception of life rests. Man has progressed in beliefs just as he has progressed in knowledge. And just as he has progressed in knowledge, he has progressed in crafts. The reason for this is that reaching this great truth of the universe is a far more difficult task than reaching the truth of those scattered things and isolated items, the attainment of which is only sought in a purely scholarly or purely industrial sense.

Until the recent past, people's ideas about it were that the sun revolves around the earth, and astronomers used to present explanations about the movements of the sun and its conditions in the way that riddles are explained, or merely describe imaginations. Therefore, the return of people in the ancient periods of jahiliyyah to the principle of religion does not prove that there is no reality to religiosity, or that religiosity attempts things that are impossible. What is known from the study of religions is only this: that the great truth did not appear to people all at once, and they could not understand the supreme truth in a single era. People became ready to grasp the great truth only after the passing of ages, and in this path they had to traverse long roads, and they reached this truth by reflecting through various methods, just as they discovered other smaller truths after a patience-testing struggle.

The comparative study of religions has shown that a countless number of facts on which people of the earliest period believed were proven false, and even today the remnants and examples of those people exist among the backward tribes of the world; indeed, even among those civilized nations which have a fairly long history of culture and civilization, such people are found. The purpose of the science of comparative religion is nothing other than this. And it is not possible that the religions of the early period were free of the ignorance and misguidance that we have mentioned. This is the reasonable conclusion which can be expected from any reasonable mode of thinking. There is nothing astonishing in this mode of thought that any scholar would regard as far-fetched, or that would lead anyone to adopt a new view about the reality and authenticity of religion. Those researchers of the science of religions who are searching for whether any such truth existed in the earliest religions, or whether they had a concept of truth free of every kind of doubt and suspicion, are chasing the impossible.

In the chapter "Evolution in the Concept of God" of this book, he writes:

Scholars of comparative religion agree that in the early conception of religion among the peoples, the concept of God and the concept of Lord passed through three stages. In the first period there was polytheism; then in the second period people distinguished among these gods and lords and gave preference to one over others (henotheism); and at the very end came the period of monotheism.

In the early period the number of lords was tens or even hundreds of lords and gods. In that period every family and every tribe had its own god; this god was either considered a god in itself or a deputy god, and people sought refuge in it, and this god accepted sacrifices and worship.

The second period, called the period of distinction and preference, although the gods and lords remained numerous in it, some of these lords and gods became more prominent than others for various reasons. For example, if a tribe became politically dominant in a region or country, its deity also became dominant in the region, and people sought from that god help for economic needs and protection from calamities. Some gods became prominent because, according to people's assumptions, they were more beneficial to more people and fulfilled more of man's demands than other gods. For example, the rain god was widely revered in areas where rain was needed, or gods of greater fear, such as the god of calamities or the god of storm and rain; that is, where there was fear, people feared that god, and where there was hope, people hoped in that god. In short, in this universe, the concept of gods also took shape in accordance with other natural phenomena.

In the third period, when tribes took the form of nations and peoples, despite the existence of various lords, they devised a common method of worship, and different methods of worship became prevalent among different regions and different nations. A distinctive feature of this period was that just as one nation imposed its authority, leadership, dominance and culture on other nations, so too it imposed its method of worship on them. Sometimes the rulers accepted the gods of the vanquished, just as a king accepts the words of his courtiers; in this way a relationship of follower and followed was established among them.

A nation reached even this weak form of mental unity only after a long struggle for civilization, and it reached the next stage when a considerable amount of knowledge and understanding came into existence within it, and because of that knowledge and understanding it became difficult for a human being to accept purely ignorant concepts. Then man began to attribute to God the better qualities that were closer to God's purity and holiness, from the rubble of his earlier concepts. The consideration of the secrets and mysteries of the universe was included in worship, and talk of the profound wisdom working behind this universe began. Among those nations and peoples, true lordship was accorded to Allah, and all other good-ranked gods began to be given the station of angels, or were declared to be gods who had been cast out from the sacred enclosure of Allah, that is, were evil.

• The reality of the bonds that will exist in the Islamic system between one individual and another, and between one generation and the next, is that they are based solely on the Islamic creed, which makes all Muslims brothers, whose God is one, and whose Lord and Sovereign is Allah alone, with no partner and no rival to Him.

Now there are several questions about the flood of Noah. The first question is whether this flood covered the whole earth or was confined to the region in which Noah was sent. Where was that land, what were its boundaries in the ancient world, and how far do its boundaries extend in the modern world? These are questions which are answered only through conjecture and estimation, and conjecture and estimation cannot establish certainty or truth. Or else these questions are answered from Israʼiliyyat (narratives derived from Jewish and Christian sources), and Israʼiliyyat itself is a doubtful record. Moreover, in relation to the purposes for which the Qur'an has narrated these stories, the answers to these questions have no importance at all.

However, from the texts of the Qur'an there are indications that in the time of Noah, the whole population was that to which Noah had been sent, and that the people of Noah lived in a region where the human population of that time resided. The flood enveloped that entire region in which humans lived, and only those who were in the Ark of Noah were saved from its destruction.

This great cosmic event, about which the Qur'an informed us, while the Qur'an is the only authentic document of it, is also an event of the period of pre-history. Written human history is silent about it, for at that time there was no record of history. Human history is a thing of recent times, and even the record that history has produced contains the possibility of much error: a historical event may be both true and false. Such events can be examined by the rational principles of criticism and evaluation. It is not appropriate to ask about this from any other source when a truthful informant has already given information about it, for if we were to seek such matters from elsewhere, we would be turning things upside down, and no intellect in which the reality of religion has firmly settled would accept it.

At present, among the numerous nations inhabiting the world, the ancient, complex and unauthenticated literature of many of them also mentions the flood of Noah. It should be carefully noted here that none of the documents called the Holy Book, whether the Old Testament made up of the books of the Jews or the New Testament made up of Christian literature, is a revelation sent down from Allah. This is because the copy of the Torah which Allah had revealed was destroyed and distorted by the people of Babylon, at the time when they enslaved all the Jews and took them captive to Babylon. Now we must see what lesson a person derives from this story. The truth is that there are many aspects of lesson in it for mankind; it is not just one lesson. In the following pages we will point out some of them, and after that the discussion will return to the story of Hud.

From the story of Noah, the characteristics of his people that become apparent are these: these people were extremely ignorant. They insisted stubbornly upon falsehood and continually rejected the pure call of Noah. Yet his call was that our Creator is the one Allah, and it is the duty of all human beings to serve that one God alone, to regard Him as their King and Ruler, and not to consider anyone other than Allah as sovereign.

The people of Noah were from the progeny of Adam, and the story of Adam has already been mentioned earlier in Surah al-Aʿraf. Likewise, it has also been mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah. Adam was sent down from Paradise to the earth so that he might discharge the duty of vicegerency (khilafah) on this earth, and this is the responsibility for which Allah had placed all the capacities within Adam. The lapse that occurred in Paradise was pardoned after Allah taught him words for his forgiveness. He learned certain words from Allah, and after he recited them, Allah forgave him. After this, Allah took a covenant from him, from his wife and from his descendants, that whenever a messenger came to them from Allah with guidance, they would surely believe in him. And that they would not follow Satan, because Satan is their own enemy, the enemy of their offspring, and an enemy until the Day of Resurrection.

Now Adam descended from Paradise to the earth as a Muslim, descended in obedience to Allah's instructions. There is no doubt that Adam, generation after generation, arranged for the instruction of his descendants in Islam. And Islam is the first and true way of life that humanity learned and was taught, because in the face of Adam there was no other lineage and no other creed. And when, centuries after Adam, Noah appeared (although today we have no means of knowing how long after Adam Noah came), in that period all the descendants of Adam had abandoned Islam and adopted the creed of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance). The details of that jahiliyyah are given by the Qur'an in this story. So we can say with certainty that the present idolatries, mythological tales, superstitious beliefs, idol-worship, false conceptions and false customs of jahiliyyah were imposed upon mankind by its environment and its jahiliyyah, and that man was originally upon the straight path, and that he became misguided and became a follower of jahiliyyah through the ill-fated endeavor of the accursed Satan. This misguidance was imposed upon him because, alongside Satan's external efforts, Allah had placed certain weaknesses within the human soul itself, and by exploiting these weaknesses Satan misled man, who is an enemy of Allah as well as the eternal enemy of man. Satan attacks man successfully at the time when man does not firmly hold on to Allah's guidance in every matter, great or small. Allah created man and gave him a measure of choice. And this very power of discernment and choice is for him a cause of trial. If he uses this power of discernment rightly and holds firmly only to Allah's rope and guidance, then the designs of his enemy Satan will have no effect upon him. And man also has the option to deviate from this guidance, even if the deviation is slight. When a person commits even a slight deviation, Satan then throws him far away from Islam and the straight path, and eventually makes him a complete follower of jahiliyyah, just as the people of Noah adopted jahiliyyah. And this process is completed only after the changes of centuries, the knowledge of which belongs to Allah alone.

The fact that Islam is the creed through which this world first became acquainted, and that this creed is that deity, sovereign, supreme authority and Lord is Allah alone, leads us to the conclusion that the view of so-called scholars of religions, and of those who make comparative studies of religions, that the belief in Tawhid (the oneness of God) has evolved step by step until it reached its present form, and that it passed through various stages before that present form, is merely a hypothesis and has no reality. Their notions are that earlier people believed in many paths: they considered natural forces to be deities, then they considered spirits to be deities, then they considered the sun, moon and various stars to be deities. The reality of the views of these people is that they first connect religions with the psychological, political and environmental circumstances of people. In this way they, in effect, deny the heavenly religions and put into people's minds the idea that religious concepts also passed through various stages to reach their present position, and that the environment of the times played a part in these changes and developments. Thus these people, in fact, by denying divine revelation and the office of prophethood, seek to prove that all religions and their fundamental concepts are also made by humans and are the product of human thought.

Now let us examine the approach of those who write about the revealed religions and who are influenced by those Western scholars. These people fall into the same error, and they conduct their research according to the method devised by the Orientalists, and unconsciously they fall into the same mistake into which their teachers, the Orientalists, fell. But the regrettable thing is that Muslim writers of this kind, in their own opinion, are defending Islam and are its supporters, yet in reality they uproot Islam and deny those true principles and beliefs of Islam whose affirmation is found throughout the whole Qur'an. The Qur'an, with great clarity and in very plain words, establishes the belief that Adam (peace be upon him) descended from Paradise to the earth with a complete Islamic view of life and Islamic beliefs, and then, centuries later, Nuh (Noah) invited the descendants of Adam to that same Islam, but Satan led them astray and plunged them into idol-worship. These beliefs and principles were based on complete Tawhid. After Nuh, this satanic cycle began again, and it returned the people to jahiliyyah. After this, messengers kept coming at intervals, seizing humanity and placing it back on the straight path, and they continued to give it a worldview based on absolute Tawhid. It is completely false to say that any change or development has occurred in the correct beliefs contained in the revealed Scriptures. Rather, if any development and change has occurred, it has occurred in those legal systems which were established at various times on the basis of the Islamic worldview. If some change and development has occurred in one of the beliefs of jahiliyyah, how does that prove that a process of evolution has also occurred in the Islamic worldview? And if some evolutionary process has occurred in the beliefs of jahiliyyah as well, then that too has occurred because of the influence of the true belief of Tawhid of Islam, which from time to time affects generations. Despite the fact that later generations have deviated from the belief in Tawhid, they have gradually continued to come closer to the belief in Tawhid. As for the belief in Tawhid, in its reality it is the oldest belief in history, and it existed before all idolatrous beliefs. Since the time Adam presented it, it has always existed in its original form. This is because the belief in Tawhid is not an invention of the human mind, but has come from Allah. Since the time Allah created man and taught him the belief in Tawhid, this belief has existed, and since that very time it has existed in this form. This is the truth; it has come from Allah, and from the very first day it has been in its complete form.

This is the reality which the Qur'an presents as an unshakeable truth, and upon this reality the whole Islamic conception of life rests. Therefore no Muslim researcher, especially one who takes up the pen in defence of Islam, can ignore this reality, nor can he conduct research along any line other than these lines, because the notions about religions that are found among Arab scholars are incorrect, and they have been compiled for a specific purpose.

Here in Fi Zilal al-Quran we could discuss such incorrect notions in detail, since for this I have a separate book in preparation, whose title will be "Necessary Corrections in Islamic Thought in the Present Age." However, here we will present one topic by way of example, to show what some researchers say and what the Qur'an says. Ustadh Aqqad, in his book "Allah," writes:

Man has progressed in beliefs just as he has progressed in knowledge. And just as he has progressed in knowledge, he has progressed in crafts. In the early period, his beliefs were as his life was; the same circumstances apply to his knowledge and crafts. Therefore the knowledge and crafts of his early period are no more advanced than the religions and worships of his early period, and the elements of truth in any one of them are no more than the elements of truth found in any other.

It is likely that in the matter of religion, human efforts have been far greater than human efforts in the field of knowledge and crafts.

The reason for this is that reaching this great truth of the universe is a far more difficult task than reaching the truth of those scattered things and isolated items, the attainment of which is only sought in a purely scholarly or purely industrial sense.

Look how the sun rises every day, and it is among the things of this universe which are completely apparent and which the human body perceives. Until the recent past, people's ideas about it were that the sun revolves around the earth, and astronomers used to present explanations about the movements of the sun and its conditions in the way that riddles are explained, or merely describe imaginations. But no one dared to deny the sun altogether, because the ideas people held about the sun were in layers of thick darkness, and perhaps even now people remain in darkness about the sun.

Therefore, the return of people in the ancient periods of jahiliyyah to the principle of religion does not prove that there is no reality to religiosity, or that religiosity attempts things that are impossible. What is known from the study of religions is only this: that the great truth did not appear to people all at once, and they could not understand the supreme truth in a single era. People became ready to grasp the great truth only after the passing of ages, and in this path they had to traverse long roads, and they reached this truth by reflecting through various methods, just as they discovered other smaller truths after a patience-testing struggle.

The comparative study of religions has shown that a countless number of facts on which people of the earliest period believed were proven false, and even today the remnants and examples of those people exist among the backward tribes of the world; indeed, even among those civilized nations which have a fairly long history of culture and civilization, such people are found. The purpose of the science of comparative religion is nothing other than this. And it is not possible that the religions of the early period were free of the ignorance and misguidance that we have mentioned. This is the reasonable conclusion which can be expected from any reasonable mode of thinking. There is nothing astonishing in this mode of thought that any scholar would regard as far-fetched, or that would lead anyone to adopt a new view about the reality and authenticity of religion. Those researchers of the science of religions who are searching for whether any such truth existed in the earliest religions, or whether they had a concept of truth free of every kind of doubt and suspicion, are chasing the impossible.

In the chapter "Evolution in the Concept of God" of this book, he writes:

Scholars of comparative religion agree that in the early conception of religion among the peoples, the concept of God and the concept of Lord passed through three stages. In the first period there was polytheism; then in the second period people distinguished among these gods and lords and gave preference to one over others (henotheism); and at the very end came the period of monotheism.

In the early period the number of lords was tens or even hundreds of lords and gods. In that period every family and every tribe had its own god; this god was either considered a god in itself or a deputy god, and people sought refuge in it, and this god accepted sacrifices and worship.

The second period, called the period of distinction and preference, although the gods and lords remained numerous in it, some of these lords and gods became more prominent than others for various reasons. For example, if a tribe became politically dominant in a region or country, its deity also became dominant in the region, and people sought from that god help for economic needs and protection from calamities. Some gods became prominent because, according to people's assumptions, they were more beneficial to more people and fulfilled more of man's demands than other gods. For example, the rain god was widely revered in areas where rain was needed, or gods of greater fear, such as the god of calamities or the god of storm and rain; that is, where there was fear, people feared that god, and where there was hope, people hoped in that god. In short, in this universe, the concept of gods also took shape in accordance with other natural phenomena.

In the third period, when tribes took the form of nations and peoples, despite the existence of various lords, they devised a common method of worship, and different methods of worship became prevalent among different regions and different nations. A distinctive feature of this period was that just as one nation imposed its authority, leadership, dominance and culture on other nations, so too it imposed its method of worship on them. Sometimes the rulers accepted the gods of the vanquished, just as a king accepts the words of his courtiers; in this way a relationship of follower and followed was established among them.

A nation reached even this weak form of mental unity only after a long struggle for civilization, and it reached the next stage when a considerable amount of knowledge and understanding came into existence within it, and because of that knowledge and understanding it became difficult for a human being to accept purely ignorant concepts. Then man began to attribute to God the better qualities that were closer to God's purity and holiness, from the rubble of his earlier concepts. The consideration of the secrets and mysteries of the universe was included in worship, and talk of the profound wisdom working behind this universe began. Among those nations and peoples, true lordship was accorded to Allah, and all other good-ranked gods began to be given the station of angels, or were declared to be gods who had been cast out from the sacred enclosure of Allah, that is, were evil.

Whether in the above extracts the author has expressed his own views, or whether he has quoted the views of those scholars who fabricate their own beliefs for themselves, in any case these views are against Islam, because in the religious conceptions of these people, human intellectual, scientific, cultural and political events appear to intervene. And according to the line of their thought, progress has happened thus: people, after believing in polytheism and countless gods, returned to Tawhid. This is clear from the very first sentence of the author's introduction to his book, in which he says: "The subject of this book is how man adopted the belief in God. When man accepted various gods as lords for himself, then he discovered Allah alone, and then he entered into the purity of the belief in Tawhid."

These are the views of the modern scholars of religions and of the author of the book "Allah." In this book the author appears influenced by the modern scholars of comparative religion, although Allah has stated a completely different and plain matter about the reality of religion. It is that Adam, the father of mankind, fully knew the reality of Tawhid, and his belief in Tawhid was as clear and pure as that of Muhammad, and there was no pollution of shirk in it, no plurality and no duality. Adam received guidance directly from Allah and followed only Allah's instructions, and Adam taught this pure and clean teaching to his descendants. Therefore, in the most ancient history of mankind, there were generations who knew of no religion other than Islam. Their belief was solely the belief in Tawhid. Yes, when a long period passed after Adam upon his descendants, his descendants deviated from the belief in Tawhid. Sometimes they adopted the view of two gods, and sometimes of many gods, and adopted the religion of many deities. After this, Nuh was sent, and he re-established the whole human race upon the belief in Tawhid; and those who committed shirk and insisted upon the system of jahiliyyah were all overtaken by the flood. And only those who knew the pure and clean Tawhid were saved from that flood, and they were averse to the religion of two gods or countless deities and many lords. According to this history, it is incumbent upon us to hold the belief that for a long time the descendants of those who sailed in Noah's ark remained upon the belief in absolute Tawhid. After a long period they again abandoned the belief in Tawhid and adopted shirk and idol-worship. Now we must see what lesson a person derives from this story. The truth is that there are many aspects of lesson in it for mankind; it is not just one lesson. In the following pages we will point out some of them, and after that the discussion will return to the story of Hud.

Now Adam descended from Paradise to the earth as a Muslim, descended in obedience to Allah's instructions. So we can say with certainty that the present idolatries, mythological tales, superstitious beliefs, idol-worship, false conceptions and false customs of jahiliyyah were imposed upon mankind by its environment and its jahiliyyah, and that man was originally upon the straight path, and that he became misguided and became a follower of jahiliyyah through the ill-fated endeavor of the accursed Satan. This misguidance was imposed upon him because, alongside Satan's external efforts, Allah had placed certain weaknesses within the human soul itself, and by exploiting these weaknesses Satan misled man, who is an enemy of Allah as well as the eternal enemy of man. Satan attacks man successfully at the time when man does not firmly hold on to Allah's guidance in every matter, great or small. Allah created man and gave him a measure of choice. And this very power of discernment and choice is for him a cause of trial. If he uses this power of discernment rightly and holds firmly only to Allah's rope and guidance, then the designs of his enemy Satan will have no effect upon him. And man also has the option to deviate from this guidance, even if the deviation is slight. When a person commits even a slight deviation, Satan then throws him far away from Islam and the straight path, and eventually makes him a complete follower of jahiliyyah, just as the people of Noah adopted jahiliyyah. And this process is completed only after the changes of centuries, the knowledge of which belongs to Allah alone.

The fact that Islam is the creed through which this world first became acquainted, and that this creed is that deity, sovereign, supreme authority and Lord is Allah alone, leads us to the conclusion that the view of so-called scholars of religions, and of those who make comparative studies of religions, that the belief in Tawhid (the oneness of God) has evolved step by step until it reached its present form, and that it passed through various stages before that present form, is merely a hypothesis and has no reality. Their notions are that earlier people believed in many paths: they considered natural forces to be deities, then they considered spirits to be deities, then they considered the sun, moon and various stars to be deities. The reality of the views of these people is that they first connect religions with the psychological, political and environmental circumstances of people. In this way they, in effect, deny the heavenly religions and put into people's minds the idea that religious concepts also passed through various stages to reach their present position, and that the environment of the times played a part in these changes and developments. Thus these people, in fact, by denying divine revelation and the office of prophethood, seek to prove that all religions and their fundamental concepts are also made by humans and are the product of human thought.

Now let us examine the approach of those who write about the revealed religions and who are influenced by those Western scholars. These people fall into the same error, and they conduct their research according to the method devised by the Orientalists, and unconsciously they fall into the same mistake into which their teachers, the Orientalists, fell. But the regrettable thing is that Muslim writers of this kind, in their own opinion, are defending Islam and are its supporters, yet in reality they uproot Islam and deny those true principles and beliefs of Islam whose affirmation is found throughout the whole Qur'an. The Qur'an, with great clarity and in very plain words, establishes the belief that Adam (peace be upon him) descended from Paradise to the earth with a complete Islamic view of life and Islamic beliefs, and then, centuries later, Nuh (Noah) invited the descendants of Adam to that same Islam, but Satan led them astray and plunged them into idol-worship. These beliefs and principles were based on complete Tawhid. After Nuh, this satanic cycle began again, and it returned the people to jahiliyyah. After this, messengers kept coming at intervals, seizing humanity and placing it back on the straight path, and they continued to give it a worldview based on absolute Tawhid. It is completely false to say that any change or development has occurred in the correct beliefs contained in the revealed Scriptures. Rather, if any development and change has occurred, it has occurred in those legal systems which were established at various times on the basis of the Islamic worldview. If some change and development has occurred in one of the beliefs of jahiliyyah, how does that prove that a process of evolution has also occurred in the Islamic worldview? And if some evolutionary process has occurred in the beliefs of jahiliyyah as well, then that too has occurred because of the influence of the true belief of Tawhid of Islam, which from time to time affects generations. Despite the fact that later generations have deviated from the belief in Tawhid, they have gradually continued to come closer to the belief in Tawhid. As for the belief in Tawhid, in its reality it is the oldest belief in history, and it existed before all idolatrous beliefs. Since the time Adam presented it, it has always existed in its original form. This is because the belief in Tawhid is not an invention of the human mind, but has come from Allah. Since the time Allah created man and taught him the belief in Tawhid, this belief has existed, and since that very time it has existed in this form. This is the truth; it has come from Allah, and from the very first day it has been in its complete form.

This is the reality which the Qur'an presents as an unshakeable truth, and upon this reality the whole Islamic conception of life rests. Therefore no Muslim researcher, especially one who takes up the pen in defence of Islam, can ignore this reality, nor can he conduct research along any line other than these lines, because the notions about religions that are found among Arab scholars are incorrect, and they have been compiled for a specific purpose.

Here in Fi Zilal al-Quran we could discuss such incorrect notions in detail, since for this I have a separate book in preparation, whose title will be "Necessary Corrections in Islamic Thought in the Present Age." However, here we will present one topic by way of example, to show what some researchers say and what the Qur'an says. Ustadh Aqqad, in his book "Allah," writes:

Man has progressed in beliefs just as he has progressed in knowledge. And just as he has progressed in knowledge, he has progressed in crafts. In the early period, his beliefs were as his life was; the same circumstances apply to his knowledge and crafts. Therefore the knowledge and crafts of his early period are no more advanced than the religions and worships of his early period, and the elements of truth in any one of them are no more than the elements of truth found in any other.

It is likely that in the matter of religion, human efforts have been far greater than human efforts in the field of knowledge and crafts.

The reason for this is that reaching this great truth of the universe is a far more difficult task than reaching the truth of those scattered things and isolated items, the attainment of which is only sought in a purely scholarly or purely industrial sense.

Look how the sun rises every day, and it is among the things of this universe which are completely apparent and which the human body perceives. Until the recent past, people's ideas about it were that the sun revolves around the earth, and astronomers used to present explanations about the movements of the sun and its conditions in the way that riddles are explained, or merely describe imaginations. But no one dared to deny the sun altogether, because the ideas people held about the sun were in layers of thick darkness, and perhaps even now people remain in darkness about the sun.

Therefore, the return of people in the ancient periods of jahiliyyah to the principle of religion does not prove that there is no reality to religiosity, or that religiosity attempts things that are impossible. What is known from the study of religions is only this: that the great truth did not appear to people all at once, and they could not understand the supreme truth in a single era. People became ready to grasp the great truth only after the passing of ages, and in this path they had to traverse long roads, and they reached this truth by reflecting through various methods, just as they discovered other smaller truths after a patience-testing struggle.

The comparative study of religions has shown that a countless number of facts on which people of the earliest period believed were proven false, and even today the remnants and examples of those people exist among the backward tribes of the world; indeed, even among those civilized nations which have a fairly long history of culture and civilization, such people are found. The purpose of the science of comparative religion is nothing other than this. And it is not possible that the religions of the early period were free of the ignorance and misguidance that we have mentioned. This is the reasonable conclusion which can be expected from any reasonable mode of thinking. There is nothing astonishing in this mode of thought that any scholar would regard as far-fetched, or that would lead anyone to adopt a new view about the reality and authenticity of religion. Those researchers of the science of religions who are searching for whether any such truth existed in the earliest religions, or whether they had a concept of truth free of every kind of doubt and suspicion, are chasing the impossible.

In the chapter "Evolution in the Concept of God" of this book, he writes:

Scholars of comparative religion agree that in the early conception of religion among the peoples, the concept of God and the concept of Lord passed through three stages. In the first period there was polytheism; then in the second period people distinguished among these gods and lords and gave preference to one over others (henotheism); and at the very end came the period of monotheism.

In the early period the number of lords was tens or even hundreds of lords and gods. In that period every family and every tribe had its own god; this god was either considered a god in itself or a deputy god, and people sought refuge in it, and this god accepted sacrifices and worship.

The second period, called the period of distinction and preference, although the gods and lords remained numerous in it, some of these lords and gods became more prominent than others for various reasons. For example, if a tribe became politically dominant in a region or country, its deity also became dominant in the region, and people sought from that god help for economic needs and protection from calamities. Some gods became prominent because, according to people's assumptions, they were more beneficial to more people and fulfilled more of man's demands than other gods. For example, the rain god was widely revered in areas where rain was needed, or gods of greater fear, such as the god of calamities or the god of storm and rain; that is, where there was fear, people feared that god, and where there was hope, people hoped in that god. In short, in this universe, the concept of gods also took shape in accordance with other natural phenomena.

In the third period, when tribes took the form of nations and peoples, despite the existence of various lords, they devised a common method of worship, and different methods of worship became prevalent among different regions and different nations. A distinctive feature of this period was that just as one nation imposed its authority, leadership, dominance and culture on other nations, so too it imposed its method of worship on them. Sometimes the rulers accepted the gods of the vanquished, just as a king accepts the words of his courtiers; in this way a relationship of follower and followed was established among them.

A nation reached even this weak form of mental unity only after a long struggle for civilization, and it reached the next stage when a considerable amount of knowledge and understanding came into existence within it, and because of that knowledge and understanding it became difficult for a human being to accept purely ignorant concepts. Then man began to attribute to God the better qualities that were closer to God's purity and holiness, from the rubble of his earlier concepts. The consideration of the secrets and mysteries of the universe was included in worship, and talk of the profound wisdom working behind this universe began. Among those nations and peoples, true lordship was accorded to Allah, and all other good-ranked gods began to be given the station of angels, or were declared to be gods who had been cast out from the sacred enclosure of Allah, that is, were evil.

Whether in the above extracts the author has expressed his own views, or whether he has quoted the views of those scholars who fabricate their own beliefs for themselves, in any case these views are against Islam, because in the religious conceptions of these people, human intellectual, scientific, cultural and political events appear to intervene. And according to the line of their thought, progress has happened thus: people, after believing in polytheism and countless gods, returned to Tawhid. They were the descendants of the riders of Noah's Ark, but they deviated from their true religion, the religion of Noah, and sank into jahiliyyah. At this stage of history, Prophet Salih (peace be upon him) was commissioned to reform them, so that he might bring them back into Islam anew.

In this story we see that they themselves demanded a miracle contrary to habit. That miracle was shown to them, but they did not respond to it with faith and acceptance of the truth; rather, they plainly rejected it and hamstrung the she-camel and killed it.

The polytheists of Arabia likewise demanded such miracles from the Messenger ﷺ, so that they would believe. They are told that the people of Salih (peace be upon him) also demanded miracles. The miracles came, they did not accept them, and it brought them no benefit. Those who believe do not demand miracles. Islam is a simple and natural call; no miracle is needed to accept it. Only reflection, reasoning and contemplation are needed. But because of jahiliyyah, veils fall over people's intellects and their reason becomes distorted.

In this story too, the Reality of the Divine appears before us in the form in which it exists in the minds of Allah's chosen servants, namely the minds of Allah's Messengers. Consider carefully the words of Prophet Salih (peace be upon him):

﴿He said: "O my people, tell me, if I have a clear proof from my Lord, and He has given me mercy from Himself, then who will protect me from Allah if I disobey Him? You would only add to my loss."﴾ (11:63) Salih said, after this statement: "O my people, have you considered: if I had a clear evidence from my Lord and He had bestowed upon me mercy from Himself, then who would save me from the grip of Allah if I disobeyed Him? You would add nothing to me except loss."

﴿Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive.﴾ (11:61) The reality of the Divine Being is reflected in the minds and hearts of the prophets in such a way, and exists with such beauty and perfection, that it is not present in the heart of anyone else in this manner. For the hearts of the prophets are like polished mirrors, and the reflection of the Divine Being appears in them with great clarity and in a remarkably unique manner.

Another aspect of this story is that we see in it that jahiliyyah presents itself in the form of guidance and clothes guidance in the garb of misguidance. With great cunning, it begins to marvel at the truth. It cannot even conceive of the truth. The people of Salih (peace be upon him) had placed great hopes in him, for he was a righteous, wise, well-mannered and admirable young man. But now his people express deep despair concerning him. Why? Merely because he calls them to the Islamic system of life, commands obedience to the Islamic system alone, and his call differs from the inherited path of their forefathers.

Remember that when human thought and vision deviate even a hair's breadth from the straight path, it does not stop at any limit of misguidance. Eventually, the state of human thinking becomes such that even the clearest and simplest truth appears to it as error; it hears the truth and begins to wonder, and human thought and imagination become so restricted that not even the simplest reality fits within it, and no natural and straightforward logic is comprehended.

Observe: Prophet Salih (peace be upon him) says to them, "O my people, worship Allah alone; you have no deity other than Him. It is He who brought you into being from the earth and made you prosper upon it." They say: look, you exist on this earth; this existence was granted to you by Allah. This is a reality that you see and cannot deny, for they did not create themselves, nor did they arrange their own life and sustenance.

This matter was quite clear, for they did not even deny the fact that Allah had created them. It is He who gave man the intellect through which he is developing this earth; yet, having accepted this premise, they refused to accept its logical conclusion: that Allah alone is the Deity, and that He has made man His khalifah (vicegerent) and mukhtar (one entrusted with choice) here. What is incumbent upon man, and what is appropriate for him, is that he acknowledge only Allah's lordship, associate none with Him, and obey none other than Him. This was the simple reality to which Prophet Salih (peace be upon him) called.

(یٰقَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللّٰهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلٰهٍ غَيْرُهُ) — "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him." What was the issue? The issue was that of divinity and lordship: who would be the ruler and the one obeyed. This is the issue around which all the missions of the prophets revolve, and around which all the call movements after the prophets revolve, and it is still today the axis of the struggle between Islam and jahiliyyah.

Lesson No. 102: An Overview

Now, after the era of Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him), the caravan of history enters other eras in the Islamic narrative. Now on the stage of history some other blessed nations appear, and some other nations appear who were destroyed like 'Ad and Thamud. One aspect of the life events of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is taken here. Casting a glance at the aspect of goodness and blessing in his story, we then move history on to the people of Prophet Lut (peace be upon him), who deserved punishment and were given a severe punishment. In the stories of Prophet Ibrahim and Prophet Lut (peace be upon him), the promise of Allah that He made to Prophet Nuh (peace be upon him) takes concrete form. It was said. 

﴿It was said: O Nuh, descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon the nations from those who are with you. And there are nations whom We will grant enjoyment, then a painful punishment from Us will seize them.﴾ (11:48) "It was said, O Nuh, descend in safety from Us, and with blessings upon you and upon the nations who are with you, and upon nations whom We shall provide for, but then a painful punishment from Us will seize them."

The ones who deserved the blessings were Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his offspring, and from the offspring of Prophet Ibrahim, through Prophet Ishaq and Prophet Isma'il (peace be upon them), prophets came, and the Seal of the Prophets (ﷺ) came last of all. Some of the offspring of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) also deserved punishment.

Verses 69 to 83

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 11, verse 70:

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was born in the Ladaniyyin of Iraq, and from there he migrated, crossing the river Jordan, and settled in the desert land of Canaan. And just as, according to rural customs, a person who does not eat food is feared, because it is suspected that he intends some crime or enmity, whereas all rural people refrain from committing treachery against the household after eating their food, when Ibrahim (peace be upon him) saw that the guests were not eating, fear naturally seized him and he began to think all kinds of things. In short, seeing this situation, he considered it appropriate to introduce himself and inform them of his purpose.

قَالُوا لا تَخَفْ إِنَّا أُرْسِلْنَا إِلَى قَوْمِ لُوطٍ (70)

'.' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) immediately understood what the sending of angels to the people of Lut meant, but suddenly the direction of the speech turned to a topic that was not under discussion.

Why did Prophet Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) wife laugh? Because she too knew against what evil and filth Prophet Lut was struggling.

Since she was barren, she had no children, and she had also grown old, so this good news was a wonder to her. This joy doubled when they were given the good news that Prophet Ya'qub (peace be upon him) would be born among the descendants of Prophet Ishaq (peace be upon him). A woman, and moreover a barren one, who receives such good news is bound to show an extraordinary and sudden joy.
In reality, this was a remarkable matter: after a fixed period a woman's menstruation ends, and after that her ability to conceive stops. But God's power is not bound by the laws He has set.

Undoubtedly, there is no room for astonishment at the command of Allah, for if a routine is proceeding according to a particular rule, this does not mean that this habit and rule cannot be changed. But when the wisdom of Allah wills, this routine can also be altered. Here Allah altered it out of mercy upon the household of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Yet when we apparently see that the routine of events has changed and some event is contrary to habit, in reality it too conforms to a deeper habit.

Because we do not have comprehensive knowledge of the Sunan Ilahiyyah (the divine laws and patterns of Allah's dealings). Its limits are very vast. We can see the realities only up to a certain extent, and this extent is very brief and limited, while we are unable to inductively survey and comprehend the reality of events in their entirety.

Those who measure the power and wisdom of the Divine Being by the limited scale of their knowledge, and even those who confine the will of Allah within the rules that Allah Himself has made, such people have not been able to understand the essence and reality of the Divine Being. For the will of Allah is free even from the rules that Allah Himself has made; the will of Allah is not bound even by the laws of nature that Allah Himself has established.

It is true that Allah Almighty runs this universe according to the laws of nature that He has laid down for this world, but this is one matter, and to say that the will of Allah is bound by the physical laws is another matter. The actual reality is that the physical laws operate with precision, but each time, the particular operation of these laws produces its effects by the command of Allah. These effects do not occur automatically. So if at some occasion Allah Almighty commands that some particular physical process will not produce those effects, then it will not happen, and then we would not say that the law of nature of Allah has changed; rather, the correct statement would be that the law of nature now is this, which appears as something beyond habit. Therefore, the laws of nature and the physical laws are in reality a manifestation of Allah's will; when Allah's will desires something else, that becomes the law of nature. The true law of nature is the unrestricted will of Allah.

Thus, here Ibrahim (peace be upon him) became content that these are the emissaries of Allah's power, and then he was also content that the good news they brought for him would certainly come to pass. Yet even in these circumstances he did not forget Lut and his people, because he was the son of his brother Azar and they lived near him. Now, since he understood that those whom Allah had sent would uproot the people of Lut (peace be upon him) from their very root, and Ibrahim was extremely compassionate and merciful, he therefore began this dialogue with the angels concerning the people of Lut (peace be upon him).

The curtain falls and this delightful, charming scene slips from the eyes. The flow of the discourse falls silent. Certainly, before the command of the Lord, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) too must have fallen silent. But suddenly before the eyes appears another scene, full of commotion. In a city of Jordan, the people of Lut (peace be upon him) come into view. These cities are Amoriyah and Sadum:

You know your people well, and the corruption and filth that had arisen in their nature were unimaginable and without parallel. They would leave women and enter into sexual relations with men. This act was contrary to the natural order (nizam-i-fitrat) according to which Allah created all creatures in the form of male and female, so that the survival and continuity of all species might remain, and so that the pleasure and joy which the laws of nature have placed in man might be enjoyed through it.

Man cannot attain this path of nature through his own reflection, his devices and his effort; this pleasure can be obtained only through steadfastness on the right path and through divine guidance. Regarding sexual deviance, it may be said that such rare and exceptional deviance among human beings is part of human history. Some people fall ill, but the illness of the people of Lut (peace be upon him) was a strange and all-encompassing illness. This shows that psychological illnesses also spread in the same way that physical illnesses spread, and that if the standard of good and evil of a society changes, then such illnesses also spread within it, and the entire nation becomes a victim of moral corruption, and this corruption arises as a result of the corrupted concepts of society. Yet this corruption clashes with the sound human nature (fitrat-i-salima), because the sound nature is in harmony with the laws of the universe and supports the means of life; it does not clash with them, whereas this sexual deviance clashes with the system of the continuation of life. Man sows the seed of life in a land from which the growth of life cannot arise. For this reason, this kind of sexual deviance clashes with human nature not only morally, but the laws of nature also abhor it, because the deed of the people of Lut is contrary not only to nature, but also to the system of the continuation of life and to true pleasure.

Sometimes a person feels in death a pleasure that is absent in life, but this pleasure is for the attainment of exalted values and lofty aims. It is not sensory and physical pleasure, and sacrificing one's head in jihad does not clash with the system of the preservation of life; rather, reducing life in this way is elevating life from another aspect. Life does not end through martyrdom in the way of Allah; rather, life assumes another form.

So when Prophet Lut (peace be upon him) saw the guests, he became very distressed, because he knew what his people would do to those beautiful guests, and thus he would be greatly humiliated. ﴿هَذَا يَوْمٌ عَصِيبٌ﴾ "This is a day of great distress."

(Verse 11:78) They came rushing to him, as one who is seized with fever trembles and hurries. Hurry, restlessness; "har'" means trembling in the state of fever.

Previously, ill treatment of guests was common among them. Therefore Prophet Lut (peace be upon him) was deeply distressed on account of those angels, and he described that day as a day of calamity.

When Prophet Lut (peace be upon him) saw that these people were rushing towards immorality involuntarily, like a person afflicted with fever trembles involuntarily, and that they were bent on insulting his guests, he appealed to the innate pure nature within them. He drew their attention: look, there are women present whom Allah has created for this very purpose. In Prophet Lut's own house there were daughters, and at that very moment they could satisfy the surge of their desire through lawful means, for whose sake they had been created. He was ready at that very moment to give them in lawful marriage to them, so that they might provide tranquility for their frenzied lustful passion.

He said: "O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you. So fear Allah and do not disgrace me regarding my guests. Is there not among you a right-minded man?" (11:78)

"They are purer for you" (11:78): that is, they are pure in every respect. Psychologically pure, physically pure, and morally pure. They have a pure nature and are ready for the satisfaction of pure desires. Their morals and their religion are pure, and nature has also prepared them for this pure and great purpose, and this path is also purer compared to the path which they are adopting.

"So fear Allah" (11:87): In the first sentence they were advised to adopt the naturally pure path; here they are told to fear Allah and refrain from this wrong conduct.

"And do not disgrace me regarding my guests" (11:87): This sentence was said to awaken their human sense of honour. Villagers generally respect guests, and insulting a guest is considered very shameful.

"Is there not among you a right-minded man?" (11:78): This matter also concerns guidance, goodness and righteousness. Moreover, nature, chivalry and morality also demand this. But all these appeals did not affect those ill-natured people, because their hearts had turned away. Their intellect had been impaired, and their unparalleled sexual passion had overpowered them.

They said: "You know very well that we have no desire for your daughters, and you know what we want!" This was a most vile hint at their filthy and wicked intention.

At this point Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) was distressed. He realised that he was now utterly powerless against them. He was among that people like a stranger, as if he had no clan or family here, and no helper who could come to his aid in this hour of calamity. In such circumstances, the anxiety he expresses is this:

When Lot (peace be upon him) was saying these words, his address was directed to those young men, that is, to the angels who were present in the form of handsome youths. In Lot's (peace be upon him) estimation, these young men were not strong enough to defend themselves. Hence Lot (peace be upon him) wished to hint that if you people were strong, these oppressors could still be confronted, or that if he had some other supporter and helper, he would seek his aid and assistance, but there is no one.

Amid the difficulties Lot (peace be upon him) was facing and the distress in which he was afflicted, this reality momentarily escaped his sight: that he was in the refuge of a mighty support. When the Prophet ﷺ recited this verse, he said in a hadith, "May Allah have mercy on Lot (peace be upon him); he was in the refuge of a mighty support even at that time."

In short, when the distress of Lot (peace be upon him) reached its extremes and the circle of calamity closed in upon him, then the messengers of Allah introduced themselves and made known that they were in the refuge of an exceedingly mighty support. The power of God stood behind them.

So they informed him about their mission and commanded that he should leave with his pure family. "However, your wife is not with you; she is among the group of the wicked (fasiqin)."

﴿أَلَيْسَ الصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ﴾ (11:81) "Is not the morning near?" This sentence has come so that the spirit of Hazrat Lut (peace be upon him) might be cheered, because he had spent the previous gathering in great distress.

The purpose was that the end of these people was very near. As soon as morning arrives, these people will be destroyed. Now Allah will fulfil the desire which Hazrat Lut could not fulfil because of his lack of strength.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verses 82–83:

That is, when the time came for Our punishment to be enforced upon them, We turned their town upside down. This punishment was prescribed for them because they too had debased themselves from the station of humanity down to the level of animality. Rather, they had fallen even below the animals, because animals, in any case, are subject to the principles of their animal nature and remain within their limits. But man is a creature who transgresses even the limits of nature.

﴿And We rained upon it stones of baked clay﴾ (11:82). That is, stones with clay adhering to them. In this context, stones covered in clay were more fitting for their condition and their station.

﴿Layered, one upon another﴾ (11:82). Manḍūd means stones that come one on top of another, and these stones

﴿Marked by your Lord﴾ (11:83). Just as livestock are branded and released so that they may be identified, these stones were released by Allah in such a way that they fell by their own automatic action and carried out their task when the need arose. This is a striking image. It leaves a powerful impression on the mind, and the impression it creates on the mind is not produced by lengthy explanations.

﴿And it is not far from the wrongdoers﴾ (11:83). This punishment is near, ready, and Allah can send it down at any moment.

The words used here to describe the punishment of the people of Lot (peace be upon him) closely resemble certain volcanic mountains. In volcanic activity, stones and dust-laden rocks rain down, and Allah punishes oppressive peoples for their oppression in this way.

We do not mean, by mentioning this resemblance, to claim that this punishment was a volcanic eruption that occurred at a particular time. Nor do we deny it, since it is possible that Allah has ordained volcanic punishment for these people in His own presence. This too is a form of punishment.

The real matter is that it is possible that Allah punished this people through an ordinary, common volcanic eruption, and that this was prescribed for them from eternity. It is also within Allah's power that He specified one of the operations of His power for this guilty people. And it is also possible that this volcanic activity was not part of ordinary natural processes, and that Allah rained stones upon them in a manner that broke the normal course of things, having no connection with natural volcanism at all. This event would be extraordinary in the same way that the birth of a child to Abraham occurred in a manner entirely contrary to the usual course. Allah has power over all things; He can do as He wills. His will is unconstrained, and for a human being, understanding this is no difficult matter.
