Lesson No. 103 — At a Glance

The Islamic worldview is the only, enduring and continuous worldview in human history. Now we arrive at the time of Hadrat Shu'ayb (peace be upon him). He takes up the task among his people, the people of Madyan. But along with the Islamic worldview, another important social issue also comes before them in his call: to establish in society the principles of trustworthiness, justice and good dealing. These matters too are connected with Islamic beliefs, because entering the religion of Allah, the One, means following only the Shari'ah of Allah. Yet when the people of Madyan heard this call of Hadrat Shu'ayb (peace be upon him), they were greatly astonished and it seemed strange to them. It did not make sense to them what connection religion has with worldly matters such as weights and measures. What is the relationship between prayer and the scales? Worship and financial dealings are of entirely different natures.

This story comes after the story of Hadrat Hud (peace be upon him) and his people 'Ad, and the story of Hadrat Salih (peace be upon him) and his people Thamud. But the outcome of this story, its manner of expression and the nature of the punishment bear greater resemblance to the story of Salih. Their punishment is similar, and the manner of describing that punishment is also alike.

Lesson No. 103 — Explanation of the Verses

84 to 95

Worshipping Allah alone is the first brick of the religion of Islam and the foundation of the Islamic system of life. It is also the first principle of the Islamic Shari'ah. The entire system of action of the Islamic society is based on this principle. This is the belief without which no creed, no worship and no mode of conduct can be called complete and Islamic.

The important matter raised in these verses is justice and equity, trustworthiness and honesty, and the regulation of economic affairs. The verses before this established the ideological foundation of Islam. But the financial guidance given here is a natural consequence of that worldview. The territory of the people of Madyan lay on the trade route running from the Hijaz to Syria, and among them existed the weakness that they cheated people in weights and measures. They would give less value for people's goods. This is a weakness that corrupts both the heart and the conduct of a person, and the lofty qualities of dignity and self-respect disappear from him. Besides this baseness, these people would also plunder the caravans going to and from Syria through northern Arabia, and would oppress travellers by imposing unlawful tolls. In this context, the details of their defect are given.

The purpose of this is to show that in the Islamic system of life, the connection of beliefs and ideologies is direct, leading to trustworthiness, honesty, justice, the establishment of the principles of fairness in dealings, and the eradication from society of theft, robbery and all kinds of economic crimes. It should be remembered that justice can be established in a society only when its members have within them the fear of God and a sense of accountability before the Hereafter. Only through such beliefs and such morality can justice, a fair economic system and equitable economic relations be established in society, and a solid human society be brought into being.

In any healthy society it is necessary that the system of mutual dealings and the moral system of the society be based on a firm ideological foundation, and that dealings and morality not rest on principles and notions that change from day to day. This is the excellence of the Islamic worldview. In this respect the Islamic system is unique among all other systems, and the Islamic society is unique among all other societies, because in it the entire life of individuals is built upon Islamic beliefs and concepts; it does not look only at temporary and superficial appearances and interests.

When an Islamic society places its morals and dealings on these principles and firm foundations, then it is not altered by the temporary influences of the turning of time, nor is it affected by any fashionable transient flood or heat.

The moral outlook of people, and the moral colouring of their mutual dealings, is not determined by whether they depend on an agricultural economy, whether they live by raising livestock, or whether they belong to the professions of industry and crafts. These factors do not influence their morals and conduct. In the moral viewpoint of Islam and in the moral principles of Islam, these factors have no role, because the source of Islamic ethics and of the Shari'ah and laws of Islam is the Qur'an and the Sunnah, and the ultimate aim of Islamic law and ethics is only the attainment of the pleasure of Allah; the fear of the punishment of the Hereafter and the hope of reward are the true motivating force in the Islamic system and society. Since the systems of law and morality devised by humans in the world are framed and formulated with an eye to commercial relations, economic conditions and personal and national interests, those notions and ethics, from the Islamic standpoint, are utterly futile and feeble. (For details, see the book "Islam ka Akhlaqi Nuqta-e-Nazar" by Sayyid Abul A'la Mawdudi, Amir of Jamaat-e-Islami Pakistan, and the chapter "Nizam-e-Akhlaq" in the author's book "Nahw Mujtama' Islami".)

﴿And do not diminish the measure and the scale. Indeed, I see you in prosperity.﴾ (11:84) Meaning: Allah has given you good provision, so you have no need, nor any compulsion, to engage in such a base act. You are already prosperous. If you give up this irregularity in the measures and scales, you will not become poor; and if you continue it, you cannot become richer. Rather, the danger is that because of this irregularity your good days will end and your opportunities for financial plunder will disappear altogether.

﴿But indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an encompassing Day.﴾ (11:84) This punishment may come in the Hereafter, where every matter, small and great, will be judged, and it may also come in this world, when your wrongdoing becomes evident to the people, your trade grows dull, conflict begins within society, you become opposed to one another, and a tug-of-war starts.

O my people, give full measure and weight with justice. [Qur'an 11:85]

Here it says: give full measure and weight. In contrast to giving short measure, giving full measure means giving something that is even more than full. Thus, in the expression أَوْفُوا الْمِكْيَالَ (85 : 11) there is more beauty than in وَ لَا تَنْقُصُوا الْمِکْیَالَ (84 : 11). It indicates: take the path of measuring and weighing that leans toward excess.

And do not defraud people of their things. [Qur'an 11:85] This phrase is not limited to measured and weighed goods. It is general, meaning all valuable things, whether related to measure or weight, price or value, because the word "shay'" (thing) has a very broad application. It applies to both tangible and intangible things.

Diminishing people's possessions is, in one respect, injustice, but it has other harmful consequences too. It produces hatred and other bad feelings among people. They are distressed, and hatred of one another arises within society. When people's trust in the institutions of justice and fairness is lost, collective evils arise in society, people's hearts fill with enmity toward one another, and the effect of reform and goodness is erased from collective life.

And do not spread corruption in the land, causing mischief. [Qur'an 11:85] ʿathw (عثو) means to create disorder. That is, do not go about making plans to spread corruption. After this, Allah stirs up the inclinations toward goodness that exist within them: the wealth Allah has given them through lawful means is far better than the forbidden wealth they gain by cheating in measure and weight and by usurping people's rights.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 86:

"What remains with Allah (baqiyyat Allah) is better for you, if you are believers." (11:85) "Because the reward that is with Allah, or the earnings obtained through lawful means in accordance with Allah's Shari'ah, are more valuable and more lasting. My duty is only clear conveyance (iblagh mubin), and it is evident that I have fulfilled the obligation of conveying the religion.

"And I am not a guardian over you." (11:86) This manner of speech compels the listener to realise that the matter is very grave. But the people had become corrupt, they had become accustomed to mischief and waywardness, and they had been exploiting people for centuries. Thus they say:

The response is a bit reserved. This answer is "This reply is extremely insulting and arrogant. It is the reply of an ignorant person whose nature is corrupted and distorted, and the one who replies harbours intense hostility and enmity towards the one addressed. Just consider it.

﴿They said, "O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we abandon what our forefathers worshipped, or that we should not have the freedom to do as we wish with our wealth?"﴾ (11:87)

"They replied, 'O Shu'ayb (peace be upon him), does your prayer teach you that we should abandon all those deities which our forefathers used to worship? Or that we should not have the authority to dispose of our wealth as we wish?'"

They either do not understand, or do not want to understand, that prayer is a necessary requirement of the Islamic worldview and faith, and the prescribed way of worshipping and serving Allah. They do not understand that no creed or ideology can be true without the creed of Tawhid (the oneness of God), and that no system can be correct unless all the wrong practices of the forefathers are completely rejected. Moreover, the Islamic worldview and the Islamic system cannot be established until the Islamic Shari'ah (divine law) is established, and the Shari'ah is not implemented in all spheres of life: in trade and financial dealings, in individual affairs and in collective affairs. Because belief and action are one whole in the Islamic system. They cannot be separated, and in Islam there is no value in empty slogans without action.

Before we discuss further the refutation of this foolish notion of a separation between religion and worldly dealings, it is necessary to note here that the standard-bearers of today's jahiliyyah (the state of ignorance of divine guidance) think on this matter exactly as the people of Shu'ayb thought. And the jahiliyyah of the modern age has offered no arguments beyond those of the people of Shu'ayb for this wrong thinking. Just as the people of Shu'ayb were polytheists in this matter, the followers of modern jahiliyyah are also engaged in this polytheism, whether they are Jews, whether Christians, or whether they are today's so-called Muslims. Because all these people, in the modern age, separate faith and belief from practice and rituals, separate Shari'ah from action; they reserve beliefs and worship for Allah, and conduct transactions and worldly affairs according to the commands of their other deities and leaders. This is the real and true shirk (associating partners with Allah).

Yes, it would not be unjustified to acknowledge that those who follow Jewish beliefs, whose beliefs have undergone many distortions, nevertheless, when the issue was raised in their assembly that their ships were serving some passengers non-Shari'ah, forbidden food, their assembly ordered such ships that, however much loss there might be, they should serve every passenger only lawful food according to Israelite law. Now those people, who claim to be Muslims while doing all this, should reflect on their own conduct.

Today there are many people among us who claim to be Muslims, but who do not observe the Shari'ah in the fields of morality, economics and transactions.

And there are also those who hold degrees from the most famous universities of the world. These people ask with great surprise: what is the connection of Islam to our personal and individual affairs? What is Islam's concern with whether someone goes naked on the beaches or dresses modestly? What is Islam's concern with what clothes a woman wears while walking in the streets? Then what does Islam have to do with how someone uses his sexual energy? Then, if someone drinks alcohol to correct his temperament, what is it to Islam? Then there are the demands of this modern age, and some people fulfil these demands; what is it to Islam? What is the difference between these questions and the question of the people of Shu'ayb? (﴿Does your prayer command you that we should abandon all those deities which our forefathers used to worship?﴾)

Then they ask with great vehemence and arrogance the second question: why should Islam interfere in economic relations, or prescribe for us an economic ethical system? What is the connection of religion with interest-based dealings? What concern is it of religion if someone collects wealth from people through cunning and deception, provided that this cleverness and trickery remains within the boundaries of the law made by human beings? Rather, these people go so far, with great audacity, as to say that when ethics interferes in business, the business is ruined. Such people also consider the ethical economic system of some Western thinkers to be wrong, and they think that it is a delusion of some sincere people of our age.

We should not go too far in condemning the ancient standard-bearers of jahiliyyah, the people of Madyan, while we see that the jahiliyyah of the modern age has gone far beyond them. Although modern jahiliyyah claims knowledge, progress and civilisation, this jahiliyyah accuses those who call for the coordination of faith, personal conduct and the material and economic conduct of the marketplace of reactionism, ignorance, stagnation and bigotry.

No person can become a true monotheist (muwahhid) unless he links his personal affairs and his collective affairs with his creed, because if anyone does not do so, he is a polytheist. And polytheism and Tawhid (the oneness of God) cannot be gathered together in one heart in any way. It should be remembered that shirk (associating partners with Allah) has many kinds and many forms. One form of it is the one that is prevalent today, in which we are living, and like the real and true shirk, all polytheists agree upon it, whether modern or ancient, in whatever age they live and wherever they are.

Just observe how the people of Madyan mocked Shu'ayb (peace be upon him), and today the claimants of Tawhid do the same thing.

﴿Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided﴾ (11:87). "Are you then the only one left who is a man of high character and righteousness?" Their meaning was not that they actually considered Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) to be righteous; rather, they thought the opposite, because in their view wisdom and righteousness meant worshipping the idols which their forefathers had worshipped, doing this without thought, and keeping trade and transactions free from the sphere of worship. And this same dispute is going on today in the same manner between the so-called progressives and the so-called reactionaries.

Now Shu'ayb (peace be upon him), like a caller to the truth who is completely certain of his truth, speaks to them with great gentleness. He seriously ignores their mockery, and does not take into account their ignorance and their fault. He conveys to them the impression that he possesses complete evidence from his Lord, that he has certainty about his mission, and that he has been given the knowledge of prophethood which these people lack. Moreover, when they arrange their affairs according to the Islamic method, they will soon come to know the benefits of the Islamic economic system, just as Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) himself acts upon it and is a man of wealth and trade. Because he does not seek any personal benefit from them for this call, nor does he wish to exhort other people to good conduct while acting upon bad deeds himself, and to find the marketplace empty and then gather the profit for himself. His call is open to these people and to the common people, all of them, and there is no loss in it for them either. It is merely an illusion that, by the enforcement of Islamic guidance in the economy, they will perhaps suffer a loss.

The prophet (Shu'ayb, peace be upon him) addresses them in his speech with great sympathy, affection and brotherly feeling.

﴿He said: "O my people! Tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord"﴾ (11:88). Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) said: "Brothers, consider for yourselves: if I were upon a clear proof from my Lord." There is a reality present within my own self, and I hold it to be true. Then revelation comes to me and I am commanded to convey the message, and after such clear evidences I present this call before you with great confidence.

﴿And He has given me from Himself good provision﴾ (11:88). "Then He has also bestowed upon me good provision from Himself." I myself am wealthy, and in my wealth I am not in need of anything from you, nor do I dispose of your affairs for my own gain.

﴿And I do not intend to differ from you in that which I forbid you﴾ (11:88). "And I certainly do not wish that I should myself commit the things from which I forbid you." That is, my aim is not that I forbid you from this evil act while going to the shop and committing it myself and earning wealth. Never! Rather:

﴿I intend only reform as far as I am able﴾ (11:88). "I only want to bring about reform, insofar as I am able, and as far as your cooperation allows."

By reform is meant general reform, in which the welfare of the entire society is achieved, the welfare of all individuals and all groups of society. Although some people are deluded by the false notion that adopting the Islamic way of life causes material loss and that opportunities for profit disappear, the reality is that a person is not only saved from gathering unlawful, impure and filthy wealth, but in place of unlawful and impure earnings he receives lawful provision, and as a result of the Islamic way of life a pure society comes into being in which the needs of all people are guaranteed, and in which there is no bigotry, nor any war or conflict.

﴿And my success is only through Allah﴾ (11:88). "And whatever I wish to do, its entire dependence is upon Allah's enabling (tawfiq)." It is He who can bring my reformative work to success, for He knows well what my intention and purpose are, and it is He who can reward me for this struggle.

﴿Upon Him I have relied﴾ (11:88). That is, my trust rests upon Him alone, and I place no reliance on anyone other than Him.

﴿And to Him I turn penitently﴾ (11:88). "I turn towards Him in all matters." My direction is towards Him, and in all affairs my return is to Him alone. My intention, my purpose and my action are directed towards Him, and all my striving is for Him.

Now Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) admonishes them in another sphere. He tells them: consider the fate of the people of Noah, the people of Hud, the people of Salih and the people of Lot. Historical events have a greater effect upon dull-witted individuals. Upon rigid and hard-hearted people, the impact of events is greater than that of rational arguments.

"That is, let not my opposition and enmity compel you to go so far in opposition and denial that you end up [suffering the same fate as the people of Nuh, the people of Hud, the people of Salih, or the people of Lut]."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 90:

Hazrat Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) would admonish them, remind them, warn them, and assure them of a good end, and he would strive to guide them to the right path by every other means. He used every method so that their hearts might soften and the fear of God might arise within them. But the hearts of these people had sunk into corruption and mischief to the utmost degree. Their very conception of life was wrong, and therefore their way of living was also wrong. Consequently, as a result of his heartfelt and earnest words, they only advanced further along the path of defiance.

Truth is perfectly clear, but their chests are constricted against it; they do not want to be able to perceive the truth.

They said: "O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say." (11:91)

Why is this? Because they determine the values of life solely according to the principles of material interests, and they look only at the outward aspect of every matter.

﴿And we see that you are a weak man among us.﴾ (11:91) These people can see only material strength. In their view, the truth and the strength that Prophet Shu'ayb (عليه السلام) presents before them carry no weight.

﴿And were it not for your kinsmen, we would certainly have stoned you.﴾ (11:91) In their view, the strength of family is more important than the strength of conviction. The bond of lineage is stronger than the bond of the heart. But these people are in fact heedless of this: that Allah is more protective of His friends than a brother is protective of his brother's honour.

﴿And you are not mighty against us.﴾ (11:91) That is, you are not dominant over us either as a brother and a respected man, nor does your weight tip the scale as a powerful person. If we are restrained, we are restrained from laying hands on you only because of family ties.

When a person is deprived of a firm ideology, and high values and lofty traditions are not before his eyes, he falls to the ground. In his mind, the interests of this world alone become supreme and exalted, and he becomes a captive of worldly values; therefore he does not value a call as precious and elevated as this one. He is deprived of perception of high realities. If people of this mindset do not raise their hands against such a lofty call, they do not refrain merely out of fear of worldly power. Such people regard only material power. As for lofty beliefs, noble ideas and elevated values, these are things that carry no significance in the eyes of a materialistic person. The mentality of fallen, base people is always of this kind.

Now the zeal of faith stirs in Prophet Shu'ayb (عليه السلام). He cannot bear this insult to Allah, Lord of the worlds. He renounces the material power of his people and kin. He leaves them to the evil end that is destined in this universe for such people, condemns their insolent attitude toward Allah, and places before them a final and decisive call, saying: "My deeds are mine and your deeds are yours." Now he hands them over to divine powers and plainly tells them that a great punishment is always ready with Allah for people like them; so take the end you have chosen for yourselves.

He said: "O my people, is my kinsfolk more powerful against you than Allah, while you have cast Him behind your backs? Indeed my Lord encompasses what you do." (11:92) "And O my people, act according to your position; indeed I am acting. You will soon know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him, and who is a liar. Wait, and indeed I am waiting along with you." (11:93)

Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) said: "O my people, is my kinsfolk more powerful against you than Allah?" My kinsfolk are merely a collection of human beings. However strong they may be, they are still human, a weak creation. They are indeed slaves and servants of Allah. Do you fear a few people and not fear Allah? How feeble is your thinking.

﴿And you have cast Him behind your backs.﴾ This is a very specific manner of expression for turning away from someone and abandoning them, in the style of a vivid picture. Since these people turn away from Allah and disregard Him, their act is extremely abominable, for it is Allah who created them. In the good circumstances in which they live, it is He who is their Provider. Thus their act is extremely arrogant, ungrateful and contemptuous, and in legal terms it is the state of disbelief and denial, and it is a most evil judgment that they have made.

﴿Indeed my Lord encompasses what you do.﴾ Know that whatever you are doing is not beyond the grasp of Allah. The meaning of encompassing (ihata) is that whatever is encompassed is fully within the control and power of the one who encompasses it; it refers to perfect power.

It is a great boldness on the part of a believer before the Lord of Honour to touch upon Allah's honour and invite His wrath. Whenever the punishment of Allah descends, people, tribes and servants become helpless before it. Although Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) acknowledged the strength of his family and tribe, he was a believer in Allah. He paid no heed to this trifling strength, nor did he consider it worth mentioning that, because of his people, they could do him no harm. Nor did he rest content with the strength of his people and tribe, and this is the attitude of a true believer. A true believer relies only upon his Lord. He wishes that people too fear Allah alone. A believer also uses the strength and solidarity of his people and tribe for Islam and for the Lord. This is the difference between Islamic and non-Islamic nationalism. In every age, this has been the Islamic and Jahili view and distinction concerning people and tribe.

This is the emotion of faith and the fervour of belief, at the root of which there is nothing but reliance upon Allah. From this, Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) now gives his people this strong challenge, and separation occurs between them, and now the paths of the two part ways.

Lesson No. 104: An Overview

Here the narratives come to a close, and in this conclusion a reference is made to the story of Moses and Pharaoh, so that the destruction of Pharaoh's people may also be placed on record, and it may be shown that Pharaoh's people too obeyed Pharaoh rather than the Messenger of Allah, and therefore were destroyed. This allusion also points to the unspoken links of the story of Pharaoh, while some of its important glimpses are also present in this scene. The fundamental principle under discussion in all these narratives is that in Islam every individual is responsible for his own deeds, and if someone follows chiefs and great ones, he cannot be absolved of the duty to obey Allah and His Messenger.

The story of Pharaoh begins with the scene in which Moses (peace be upon him) is sent with signs and clear proofs to Pharaoh, which carry a divine power, because Pharaoh possessed great material power. Therefore, against his power, there had to be a power of equal force.

Lesson No. 104: Explanation of the Verses

In the context here, this story is presented in brief, because the aim is to show the final scene of the story. Thus we see that Pharaoh walks in front and his people follow right behind him. These people, by disobeying Allah, obey the commands of Pharaoh, even though Pharaoh's command is ignorant, foolish and feeble.

﴿Then they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not rightly guided.﴾ (97)

These people, who were followers of Pharaoh, therefore follow him, just as here they used to follow him without thought or deliberation. They did not use their own opinion and intellect. They were content with humiliation, and they renounced the blessings of intellect, will and freedom that Allah had given them, and adopted the path of slaves. This is why on the Day of Resurrection they will enter the punishment in the same servile manner. Pharaoh will be their leader there too.

Consider this scene! The narration begins in the past tense, while the warning of a bad end is in the future. Suddenly the scene effectively begins: the future turns into the past, and on the screen the state of the past is visible. It is as though Pharaoh has already led them into the Resurrection.

(فَأَوْرَدَهُمُ النَّارَ) "He will bring them to the Fire as cattle are brought to the watering place" (Hud 11:98). Just as a shepherd takes his goats to the watering place to give them water, so too these people were indeed nothing but a herd of animals. Has a herd ever reflected? Did they not deny the noble qualities of humanity, namely reflection and reasoning, and did they not renounce freedom of choice and will? Therefore they deserve to arrive at the watering place of Hell, where their thirst will never be quenched. There, the water will not cool their chests; rather, that water will roast their intestines and lips and burn their hearts.

بِئْسَ الْوِرْدُ الْمَوْرُودُ (11:98) "Wretched is the watering place to which they are brought." This was a scene in which Pharaoh leads them and brings them to the Fire. But the commentary on this scene is as follows:

This is a scornful remark, calling the fire a "gift" (bi'sa al-rifd / a mockery of reward): "the reward for their labour." This was the gift that Pharaoh gave them. There he had promised the sorcerers that he would give them a great reward and recompense. This is the reward and prize he has given. This is his great prize. How evil is the watering-place onto which he led his people, and how evil is the reward he gave his people for following him.

Here the Qur'an's manner of expression is such that a person is left astonished, and this is indeed the inimitability (i'jaz) of this noble Book, which only those can appreciate who have a taste for the Qur'anic style.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verses 100–102 (part 1 of 2):

Lesson No. 105 at a Glance

This lesson is the concluding section of this surah. It draws many observations and diverse conclusions. Taking into account all the themes of the surah, it forms a complete conclusion. The beginning of the surah and its narratives are all summarized here. These observations and conclusions are in full harmony with the subjects of the surah and fully correspond to its aims and purposes.

For example, the first conclusion is clearly connected with the stories of the Qur'an.

ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الْقُرَى نَقُصُّهُ عَلَيْكَ مِنْهَا قَائِمٌ وَحَصِيدٌ (100) وَمَا ظَلَمْنَاهُمْ وَلَكِنْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ فَمَا أَغْنَتْ عَنْهُمْ آلِهَتُهُمُ الَّتِي يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ لَمَّا جَاءَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ وَمَا زَادُوهُمْ غَيْرَ تَتْبِيبٍ (101) وَكَذَلِكَ أَخْذُ رَبِّكَ إِذَا أَخَذَ الْقُرَى وَهِيَ ظَالِمَةٌ إِنَّ أَخْذَهُ أَلِيمٌ شَدِيدٌ (102) (11 : 100 to 102)

"This is part of the news of the towns which We relate to you; some of them are still standing and some have been mown down. We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves, and when the command of your Lord came, the gods they used to call upon besides Allah did not avail them anything; and they added nothing to them but ruin. Such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoing. Indeed His seizing is painful and severe."

The second observation concerns the destruction of those nations that were destroyed in this world. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 11, verse 100–102 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves﴾ (11:101). They did not wrong them; rather, they themselves inflicted injury upon themselves.

"They had rendered inoperative the means of their understanding and perception. They had turned away from guidance, denied the signs and miracles of Allah, and they mocked the things with which they had been warned. Therefore, they were not the oppressed; rather, they were those who wronged themselves."

﴿So their gods, whom they invoked besides Allah, did not avail them anything when the command of your Lord came; and they added nothing to them but ruin﴾ (11:101). "And when the command of Allah came, the gods they used to call upon besides Allah were of no use to them at all, and they gave them nothing but destruction and ruin."

This is another purpose for bringing these narratives. The beginning of this surah itself was with the point that those who follow a religion and system other than Allah's will not have a good end. After that, in the narratives of the messengers, all the messengers warned their peoples, one after another, of an evil end. All the messengers told their peoples that the self-invented deities they had adopted as their guides could not save them. Thus the essence of all these narratives is that no deity other than Allah can benefit anyone at all. When the command of Allah comes and the Resurrection is established, these deities will not be able to save any of their followers from the punishment; rather, they will be the cause of loss and ruin for them. (Here the word "tatbib" is used, which expresses severe ruin both literally and in meaning.) This ruin will be greater because these people placed blind trust in these false gods, and as a result they advanced further in turning away and denial; therefore they became deserving of the most severe punishment. Just as these deities could not benefit, they could not harm either, but because of this blind trust, the loss increased.

﴿And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoers﴾ (11:102). "And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoers." The meaning of "such" is that, just as was described in the narratives, just as those nations and communities were destroyed and annihilated when they committed injustice. The wrongdoer here refers to polytheism; that is, when they turn away from the lordship and sovereignty of Allah and make someone else their lord and ruler, they thereby wrong themselves, because by being afflicted with polytheism and corruption they become deserving of the punishment of the Hereafter. Such nations, due to polytheism, are deprived of the call to Tawhid and the call to reform, and thus the earth is filled with injustice and corruption.

This severe punishment is given by Allah after a respite, when people have indulged themselves thoroughly, and thus they fall into trial. إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لآيَةً لِمَنْ خَافَ عَذَابَ الآخِرَةِ ذَلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَجْمُوعٌ لَهُ النَّاسُ وَذَلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَشْهُودٌ (103) وَمَا نُؤَخِّرُهُ إِلا لأجَلٍ مَعْدُودٍ (104) يَوْمَ يَأْتِ لا تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ إِلا بِإِذْنِهِ فَمِنْهُمْ شَقِيٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ (105) فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ شَقُوا فَفِي النَّارِ لَهُمْ فِيهَا زَفِيرٌ وَشَهِيقٌ (106) خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالأرْضُ إِلا مَا شَاءَ رَبُّكَ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ (107) وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ سُعِدُوا فَفِي الْجَنَّةِ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالأرْضُ إِلا مَا شَاءَ رَبُّكَ عَطَاءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ (108) (11 : 103 to 108)

"Indeed in that there is a sign for him who fears the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day on which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day which will be witnessed. And We defer it only for a limited term. On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission; some of them will be wretched and some happy. As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning and wailing, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Indeed your Lord is the Accomplisher of what He intends. As for those who are happy, they will be in the Garden, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills; a gift unbroken."

The conclusion drawn from the end of these towns is that the fate that befell these towns will befall the people of Makkah as well. If they are not destroyed in this world and are given respite, as the people of Musa (peace be upon him) were, they will surely be afflicted with punishment. Therefore, O Messenger, you and those walking with you should move straight forward on your path, not incline in the least toward these polytheists and wrongdoers, establish prayer, be patient in difficulties, for Allah does not waste the reward of the good-doers.

فَلاتَكُ فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِمَّا يَعْبُدُ هَؤُلاءِ مَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلاكَمَا يَعْبُدُ آبَاؤُهُمْ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَإِنَّا لَمُوَفُّوهُمْ نَصِيبَهُمْ غَيْرَ مَنْقُوصٍ (109) وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ فَاخْتُلِفَ فِيهِ وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَفِي شَكٍّ مِنْهُ مُرِيبٍ (110) وَإِنَّ كُلا لَمَّا لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ رَبُّكَ أَعْمَالَهُمْ إِنَّهُ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ (111) فَاسْتَقِمْ كَمَا أُمِرْتَ وَمَنْ تَابَ مَعَكَ وَلا تَطْغَوْا إِنَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ (112) وَلا تَرْكَنُوا إِلَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا فَتَمَسَّكُمُ النَّارُ وَمَا لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءَ ثُمَّ لا تُنْصَرُونَ (113) وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ طَرَفَيِ النَّهَارِ وَزُلَفًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ إِنَّ الْحَسَنَاتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئَاتِ ذَلِكَ ذِكْرَى لِلذَّاكِرِينَ (114) وَاصْبِرْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ (115) (11 : 109 to 115)

"So be not in doubt concerning what these worship; they worship only as their fathers worshipped before. And We will surely pay them their portion without diminution. And We certainly gave Musa the Book, but it was disputed about, and had not a word already gone forth from your Lord, the matter would have been decided between them. And indeed they are in disquieting doubt concerning it. And indeed, to each your Lord will fully pay [recompense for] their deeds; indeed He is Acquainted with what they do. So remain on a right course as you have been commanded, [you] and those who have turned back with you [to Allah], and do not transgress. Indeed He is Seeing of what you do. And do not incline toward those who have wronged, lest you be touched by the Fire, and you have not other than Allah any protectors; then you would not be helped. And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in some hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds; that is a reminder for those who remember. And be patient, for indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost."

[Continued in part 2]

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 11, verse 100–102 (part 2 of 2):

﴿And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves﴾ (11:101). They did not wrong them; rather, they themselves inflicted injury upon themselves.

"They had rendered inoperative the means of their understanding and perception. They had turned away from guidance, denied the signs and miracles of Allah, and they mocked the things with which they had been warned. Therefore, they were not the oppressed; rather, they were those who wronged themselves."

﴿So their gods, whom they invoked besides Allah, did not avail them anything when the command of your Lord came; and they added nothing to them but ruin﴾ (11:101). "And when the command of Allah came, the gods they used to call upon besides Allah were of no use to them at all, and they gave them nothing but destruction and ruin."

This is another purpose for bringing these narratives. The beginning of this surah itself was with the point that those who follow a religion and system other than Allah's will not have a good end. After that, in the narratives of the messengers, all the messengers warned their peoples, one after another, of an evil end. All the messengers told their peoples that the self-invented deities they had adopted as their guides could not save them. Thus the essence of all these narratives is that no deity other than Allah can benefit anyone at all. When the command of Allah comes and the Resurrection is established, these deities will not be able to save any of their followers from the punishment; rather, they will be the cause of loss and ruin for them. (Here the word "tatbib" is used, which expresses severe ruin both literally and in meaning.) This ruin will be greater because these people placed blind trust in these false gods, and as a result they advanced further in turning away and denial; therefore they became deserving of the most severe punishment. Just as these deities could not benefit, they could not harm either, but because of this blind trust, the loss increased.

﴿And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoers﴾ (11:102). "And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoers." The meaning of "such" is that, just as was described in the narratives, just as those nations and communities were destroyed and annihilated when they committed injustice. The wrongdoer here refers to polytheism; that is, when they turn away from the lordship and sovereignty of Allah and make someone else their lord and ruler, they thereby wrong themselves, because by being afflicted with polytheism and corruption they become deserving of the punishment of the Hereafter. Such nations, due to polytheism, are deprived of the call to Tawhid and the call to reform, and thus the earth is filled with injustice and corruption.

﴿Indeed, His seizing is painful and severe﴾ (11:102). "Indeed, His seizing is painful and severe." This severe punishment is given by Allah after a respite, when people have indulged themselves thoroughly, and thus they fall into trial. Then their excuses also come to an end, because by sending messengers Allah establishes proof against them. Then, when injustice prevails among these nations, and the oppressed fall under the firm grip of the oppressors, and the situation reaches the point where reformers who give the call to truth become extremely few and ineffective, and their word does not prevail against the oppressors, because the oppressors have already gone far ahead in injustice. After that, the people of faith separate from those oppressors who have advanced far in injustice. These believers then regard themselves as a community; they follow their own religion and their own Lord, they have their own leader and their own bonds, and they leave the oppressive community to reach its natural end, in accordance with the sunnah of Allah which He has ordained for this universe, forever and ever.

This worldly seizing is, in reality, a symbolic punishment for the Hereafter, and those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter fear this seizing, because they are seeing it. Allah has in any case given them this insight: that the God who can give such severe punishment to a people in this world can give even more severe punishment in the Hereafter, and therefore they fear. Here the Qur'an suddenly takes man from the scenes of this world to the scenes of the Resurrection, and this is a special style of the Qur'an: after scenes of this world, it suddenly presents a scene of the Hereafter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verses 103–104:

This seizure in the world, which reminds one of the punishment of the Hereafter, instills fear in the heart.

إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لآيَةً لِمَنْ خَافَ عَذَابَ الآخِرَةِ (11:103) "Indeed, in that is a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter."

The truth is that in this there is a sign for everyone who fears the punishment of the Hereafter. However, the truth is that only those people can take this lesson whose hearts harbor fear of the punishment of the Hereafter; their eyes are opened and their thinking and vision are sharpened.

But those whose hearts have no fear of the Hereafter have deaf hearts and closed eyes. They cannot understand that He who created them can also create them again. The vision of such people is limited, and they can see only this world. They can take lessons and admonition even from the awe-inspiring events that occur in this world.

Now it is told what that day will be like.

ذَلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَجْمُوعٌ لَهُ النَّاسُ وَذَلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَشْهُودٌ (11:103) "That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed."

It will be a day on which all people will be gathered, and whatever happens on that day will happen before everyone's eyes. This is a scene in which all people will be assembled; in this gathering, they will have no say of their own, but rather they will be driven and brought into this visible scene. All of them will be present together, and all will be waiting for their outcome.

On Surah 11, verse 105:

﴿On the day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission.﴾ "When it comes, no one will be able to speak except with God's permission, and then only to present some plea." Awe will prevail over everyone, and there will be a dreadful silence. People will be struck with fear. Speech there will be by permission, but asking for permission is no easy matter. It is God alone who grants permission to someone, and only then can a plea be presented.

Now people will be divided according to their final end:

﴿Then some of them will be wretched and some will be blessed.﴾ The manner of expression is such that we seem to see with our own eyes: those who met with wretchedness are in Hell, their breathing labored, panting and hissing. And we see that those who are in Paradise are also visible, and for them there are gifts that are everlasting and never come to an end.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verses 106–108:

All these people will remain in Paradise and Hell "for as long as the heavens and the earth endure." This is an Arabic idiom used to express continuity and permanence. Idioms have their own meaning and a particular emotional impact, and here too this idiom is very fine in terms of its manner of expression.

﴿Indeed, your Lord is the all-accomplishing (Fa''al) of what He intends﴾ (11:107). "Surely your Lord has full authority to do whatever He wills." This statement is for the reassurance of the hearts of those who were granted good fortune, that their reward will be everlasting and will never be cut off. Although, by supposition, Allah could change things, since He has determined this for them, they have no need to be anxious. Nevertheless, His will remains entirely free.

Now that the matter has reached the point of explaining what the outcome of both groups will be in the Hereafter, and it has been made clear what the end of the wicked nations in this world will be, what their condition will be in the Hereafter, what punishment will come upon them here, and how they will be treated in the Hereafter, the direction of the discourse now turns toward the Prophet ﷺ, and the address is now to his handful of companions who are in a weak condition in Mecca. They are given consolation and advised to remain steadfast on the path they have taken, and the deniers in Mecca are further warned that their end will be the same as that of the nations whose stories have been related. Although the punishment of Allah has been delayed, Allah had earlier granted long respite to many nations, and after the respite ended, each was given full recompense, good or bad, for its deeds, but at its appointed time. The delay of punishment and reckoning does not mean that these nations were upon the truth; just as the forefathers of those nations were upon falsehood, so too were they upon falsehood.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 109:

Do not harbour even the slightest doubt in your heart that the idols these people worship are false. The address is to the Messenger (ﷺ), but the warning is meant for the nations. This style is often more effective, because it shows that the matter between Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) has already been settled. Allah has given the Messenger (ﷺ) His final commands, so there is no room for dispute. Those who are guilty are set aside, as though they are not even fit to be addressed. In this way the impact is greater than it would be if they were addressed directly.

﴿So do not be in any doubt about what these people worship. They worship only as their forefathers worshipped before them.﴾ (11:109) "O Prophet (ﷺ), do not remain in any doubt about the deities these people worship. These people are simply worshipping in the same way as their forefathers did before them, like blind followers."

Therefore their end will also be like that of the earlier nations, namely everlasting punishment. However, the explicit statement is not made here, because their end is well known and understood.

﴿And We will surely give them their full share without any reduction.⌋ (11:109) "And their end is as well known as that of the people before them, and scenes of earlier nations have already been presented earlier. Yet in this world it is also possible that they may be granted respite, as the people of Musa (peace be upon him) were."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 111:

﴿And indeed, your Lord will surely pay them in full for their deeds. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do.﴾ (11:111)

This emphatic manner of expression has been adopted so that no one, because of the delay and postponement, should doubt that the full recompense of reward and punishment will be given. Let no one doubt that the position adopted by the people of Makkah is false, and that there is no doubt in its falsehood. This is shirk, and this shirkī religion was adopted by many nations before them.

There was also a background to this emphatic style. The circumstances of the Islamic movement at that time were that the disbelievers stood against the Muslims like a hostile force. They were blocking the path of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from every direction. The Muslims were few in number and were being subjected to oppression. The spread of the Call had almost frozen, and the arrival of punishment from Allah had also been postponed until the Day of Resurrection. The believers were being subjected to every kind of torment, and their enemies were apparently succeeding. In such circumstances, some weak-hearted people could waver, and even steadfast people could certainly fall into anxiety. Therefore, the Islamic movement needed this kind of consolation and encouragement. More than anything else, the hearts of the Muslims gain strength when Allah declares their enemies to be His enemies and announces that they are upon falsehood beyond any doubt or uncertainty, [and] takes part in the battle, and how He continually shows the companions (may Allah be pleased with them) the signposts of the way at every opportunity.

This emphatic statement, that the end of the enemies of Allah will surely come to pass, naturally instills in the soul the conviction that the Sunnah of Allah is operating and prevailing among His creation; His religion too will prevail according to His Sunnah, His promise and His threat will both be fulfilled according to the Sunnah of Allah. Therefore, those who accept this religion and those who call to it should continue calling to it in the manner prescribed (masnun), as they have been commanded, neither diminishing from it nor adding to it, nor bowing before oppressors, even if they are tyrants. They should not accept a religion other than the religion of Allah, even if the path becomes long. They should make preparations for the difficulties of the way and be patient until Allah does what He wills.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 11, verse 112:

﴿So stand firm as you have been commanded, you and those who have turned back (from disbelief and rebellion to faith and obedience) with you.﴾ (11:112)

The Prophet ﷺ felt the difficulty, the severity and the awe of this command. It is reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Hud and its companion surahs have made me old." Istiqamah (steadfastness) means to walk in moderation and to go straight according to the Islamic methodology, so that no deviation occurs. At all times there is a need for reflection, and at all times there is a need to keep the limits of Allah in view, and to restrain those human inclinations and tendencies which are sometimes excessive and sometimes deficient. In short, in any movement this is a permanent and continuous duty, and it must be kept in mind in every movement and every stillness of life.

﴿And do not transgress (the bounds of servitude).﴾ (11:112)

Here it is necessary to understand that after the command to be steadfast, this prohibition is not there because one should not fall short in steadfastness; rather, it is a prohibition against tyranny and going beyond bounds. It has come because, as a result of the continuous command of steadfastness, such a degree of alertness is produced in a person's mind, and a person begins to exercise such caution and prudence, that he reaches the level of excess and exaggeration, and as a result of this excess and exaggeration, "the religion of ease" (al-Din Yusr) becomes difficult, and excess and deficiency begin in religion. This point is very important, and a Muslim should keep a moderate temperament and remain on the Straight Path, neither being heedless nor being extremist.

﴿Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.﴾ (11:112)

The word "Basir" (Seeing), with the sense of insight, is apt here: He sees, and His seeing is not superficial; He sees with insight and depth. Therefore, O Messenger ﷺ, you and your companions should remain on the straight path, fearing Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 113:

﴿Do not incline toward those who have done wrong, lest the Fire touch you﴾ (11:113). "Do not lean even slightly toward those wrongdoers, or else you will fall into the grip of Hell." That is: do not place your trust in the wrongdoers, nor feel any kind of reassurance from them. By "wrongdoers" are meant those tyrannical, domineering and rebellious people who establish their superiority on the basis of their oppression on earth, and who make the common people worship them in opposition to God. Do not place your trust in them, nor show any sign of reassurance from them. For if you display such neutral reassurance and trust toward them, you will in effect be indirectly supporting their oppressive actions, and in this way you too will become a partner in that great crime. If you do this, you will fall into the grip of the Fire.

﴿And you will have no protectors other than Allah, and then you will not be helped﴾ (11:113). "You will not find any guardian apart from God who could shield you from Him, and no help will reach you from anywhere." In such difficult circumstances, through which the handful of followers of the Islamic movement were passing at that time, remaining firmly on the straight path is truly a difficult task, and it requires spiritual provision. Therefore, Allah the Exalted points out to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his handful of companions this provision, for the sake of moral and spiritual training and for the cultivation of a bond with Allah:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 114:

﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in some hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds.﴾ (11:114)

Allah, the Exalted, knew well that this is the provision for the journey which becomes useful at the time when all other provisions for the journey are exhausted. It is the provision for the spiritual journey, and it gives a person a strength that enables him to bear even greater hardships. Therefore this provision is the "ascension of the believers" (mi'raj al-mu'minin), and it connects the believers with the Lord, the Generous, the Merciful and the Loving, who is near and hears all calls well. When the believer is alone and distressed, this provision brings the breeze of that intimacy and love, and thus a certain expansiveness is created for him in an atmosphere suffocated by jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) and disbelief.

The verse mentions the two ends of the day, that is, the beginning and the end, and then a time near the night. Thus all the times are covered. If the number of prayers had not been specified, the number has nonetheless been specified by the Sunnah of the Messenger, and likewise the specific times have been specified by the Sunnah.

After the command to establish the prayer, that is, to perform it in its full entirety, this verse comes with the statement that good deeds remove evil deeds. This is a general verse; it refers to all good deeds, and prayer is certainly the greatest of good deeds, so it is also included in this verse. In any case, "al-muhsinat" is not restricted to prayer, as some commentators hold.

﴿That is a reminder for those who remember (Allah).﴾ (11:114) Prayer, in its reality, is the remembrance of Allah. Therefore this attribute is most fitting for it.

Steadfastness (istiqamah) can be adopted by a person only when he has the resolve to be patient over difficulties. Moreover, according to the Sunnah of Allah, there is a respite for the deniers before they are overtaken by their evil end, and one has to wait for it; and this waiting too requires patience. Therefore, for steadfastness and for successfully acting upon all the previous guidance, the command is given: be patient.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 11, verse 115:

﴿So be patient, for indeed Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost.﴾ "Be patient, for Allah does not waste the reward of those who do good." Steadfastness in the way of Allah is ihsan (excellence in doing good), and offering the prayer on time is also ihsan. Being patient over the denial of those who reject the truth is also ihsan. Allah does not waste the reward of the muhsinin (those who do good).

The discussion returns to completing the commentary on the destruction of nations and the ruin of towns. It is said that if the people of goodness had been present in those towns, and had continued the effort of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and the effort to remove corruption and mischief from the earth, and the effort to remove oppression from the earth, and had restrained the hands of those who stretched out their hands in aggression, then such a punishment would not have descended upon those towns and nations that uprooted them from their foundations and cast them down. This is because Allah does not destroy towns unjustly while their people are righteous (salih) and reformers (muslih). That is, they are themselves good and are also engaged, to the extent of their capacity, in making people good. Yes, in those destroyed towns there was also a small number of believers, but they did not have sufficient strength and influence for their needs. Therefore Allah delivered them. Since the majority were the mutrafin (affluent and arrogant) and the mufsidin (corrupters), and the others followed them, Allah destroyed the entire towns completely.

This brief indication reveals the policy that Allah has adopted regarding the nations of the world. When corruption and mischief become widespread in a people, and humans become slaves of other humans in whatever form that may be, yet there remain within that nation people who strive for the reform of conditions, then that nation is a nation that is saved. Allah does not annihilate such a nation. But as for nations in which oppressors commit oppression and roam about freely, mischief-makers continue to spread mischief with no one to stop them, or in which there are people who regard oppression and corruption as evil but do not have the power to change the situation, then with regard to those nations the Divine Sunnah (way) takes its course: either that nation is utterly destroyed, or such a punishment comes upon it that the nation as a whole is scattered.

Therefore, those who wish to establish on this earth the system of Allah's lordship, a system in which Allah alone is the ruler, and those who wish to establish the justice of Allah's law on earth, in which no one's command prevails except Allah's, are in reality the salt of the earth, and because of them the destruction of nations is held back. Therefore, those who strive for the establishment of the Islamic system of life in the world are people of great worth and value. They become like a wall of molten lead against oppression and corruption. Not only do they fulfil the obligation imposed upon them by their Lord, but also the nation in which they work is saved from total destruction and the punishment of destruction as a whole nation. Because of them, Allah's punishment upon nations is deferred.

The final observation is this: Allah created man, and some humans incline towards goodness while others incline towards corruption. In this universe Allah has also established the sunnah that some people will be on this side and some on that side.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 11, verses 118–119:

If Allah had willed, He would have made all people a single community with one outlook and one disposition; all would have had the same capacity and the same mould, and there would be no difference or variety among them. But it was not Allah's desire that the creature who is His successor and vicegerent (khalifah) should be of this kind, so He gave people different capacities and inclinations.

It was the will of Allah that people should differ according to their aptitudes and inclinations. Then Allah also gave people the choice to adopt whichever inclination they wish, to walk whichever path they choose, and to bear the consequences of the path they walk. If they adopt the good path they will receive reward, and if they adopt the evil path they will receive punishment. This is the sunnah (established way) of Allah, which continues in accordance with His will. Therefore, both the one who takes the path of guidance and the one who adopts misguidance are following the sunnah of Allah, this sunnah accords with His will, and reward and punishment are also in accordance with the sunnah and will of Allah.

It was Allah's plan that people should not be a rigid community (ummah jamidah), and that those who attain success are the people whom Allah has granted the ability to be guided, and who gather together upon the truth, because guidance and truth are one and the same; there is no plurality in them, even though they may stand opposed to the people of misguidance. These are the counterpart of those who are rightly guided.

﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾ (11:119)

This shows that the end of those who gather upon guidance is different: it is Paradise, and it will be filled with them, just as Hell will be filled with those who differ from the people of truth and also differ among themselves, because the varieties of falsehood are many.

The concluding passage of this surah is an address to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It explains the purpose of the revelation of the stories of the prophets to him, and the believers in particular should reflect upon this. Those who do not believe have been given a final warning, and it has been stated that the relationship with them should now be ended and they should be left to reach the outcome that awaits them, which lies behind the veil of the unseen. The Messenger (ﷺ) is told to worship Allah, to place his trust in Allah, and to leave those people to do whatever they wish.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verse 120:

The blessed person of the Messenger of God ﷺ was also facing difficulties from his people; some of them were extremely deviant and misguided. Moreover, great responsibilities were being imposed upon him in connection with the Islamic call. Therefore there was a need that he be consoled and that his encouragement be provided by his Lord, although he was steadfast and was bearing all difficulties with constancy.

﴿And We narrate to you from the news of the messengers that with it We strengthen your heart. And there has come to you in this [surah] the truth and an admonition and a reminder for the believers.﴾ (11:120)

And O Prophet, these stories of the messengers which We relate to you are things through which We strengthen your heart. In them you found the knowledge of the truth, and the believers received advice and awakening.

In the narratives there is, firstly, the strengthening of the heart; there are truths and realities concerning the Islamic call; there are various examples and models of the prophets; there are different patterns of the Divine Sunnah; there are glad tidings and warnings; and there are the lessons-giving events contained in these narratives.

What will be the end of those people who, even after this promise and admonition, do not believe? These narratives are of no benefit to them at all. For them there is a decisive matter in them. Say to them:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 11, verses 121–122:

﴿وَقُلْ لِلَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ اعْمَلُوا عَلَى مَكَانَتِكُمْ إِنَّا عَامِلُونَ﴾ (11:121)

As for those who do not believe, say to them: "Continue to act according to your way, and we too are acting according to our way. Wait for the outcome, and we too are waiting."

And, O Prophet, one of your other brothers [prophets] also said the same to his people, which has already been mentioned in this same surah, and then he left his people alone, so that they might await their own end.
