Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 11, verse 123 (part 1 of 3):

ghaybu's-samawati wal-ard (12:123)* The unseen of the heavens and the earth, whatever is hidden in the heavens and the earth, is all in the power of Allah. The final decisions of all these matters are in His hand. O Messenger, your affairs and the affairs of the believers, all the affairs of those who do not believe, and the affairs of all existing creatures, and the affairs of the believers, and the affairs of those who do not believe, and the affairs of all existing creatures, and the affairs of all creatures yet to come, are all entirely in the power of Allah.

وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُ الأمْرُ كُلُّهُ فَاعْبُدْهُ وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَيْهِ وَمَا رَبُّكَ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ (11:123)
﴿And to Him the whole matter will be returned. So worship Him and put your trust in Him. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.﴾

Since all matters return to Him for decision, He alone is worthy of being worshipped. He alone is worthy of being relied upon, for He is the Protector; He knows what each one needs, and He is aware of every good and every evil. Nothing of anyone's reward is lost with Him, and no one can escape punishment... He is not unaware of any of your deeds.

The purpose of this surah, then, also began with the theme of worship, turning to Allah in repentance, and finally returning to Allah, and it ended with the themes of Tawhid, worship, repentance, turning to Allah and, ultimately, returning to Allah, and these themes were clarified through the study of the whole universe and the study of human history.

Likewise, the artistry of the Qur'an's expression creates harmony between the beginning and the end of its speech, and all the narratives, themes and their intellectual direction of the Qur'an become mutually proportionate. And if this Qur'an were not the speech of Allah, there would be countless intellectual contradictions in it.

Whoever seeks to discover the flow of the discourse in this surah, and indeed the aim of the entire Meccan Qur'anic discourse, will easily find that in this whole discourse one line has been adopted. The whole discourse moves along this line; indeed, this line is the axis of the discourse, and the whole discourse revolves around this axis and theme. All the threads meet at this central point, and all its fibres are bound to this axis. This axis is the axis and theme of the worldview and of the way of life around which the discourse revolves. What is it? It is that the Qur'an prescribes for mankind a complete system of life and wishes for its establishment.

It is appropriate that we discuss a little this central line, this axis and this pillar. Its expression is well manifested throughout this entire surah. Some points we have already stated, but we wish to take them up again here in order to establish coherence in this commentary.

One extremely important truth has been stated throughout this entire surah: in the introductory verses at the beginning of the surah, in the narratives of the surah, in which the whole surah and the whole course of human history are given, and in the concluding verses of the surah, where the Messenger ﷺ is instructed to tell the polytheists plainly that they should prepare to bear the final consequences. What is that truth?

The important issue taken up in this entire surah is this: that you worship Allah alone, and it prohibits you from worshipping anyone other than Allah; and that worship is indeed the name of the entire system of life, that is, of religion (din). And every threat of punishment, every promise of reward, the reckoning and accounting of the Day of Gathering, and reward and punishment, all are based upon this fundamental belief and principle, as we also said in the introduction of the surah: "Worship Allah alone."

First of all, we must see what method the Qur'an has adopted to fix this truth in the mind, and what is the importance of this method? The forms and manners in which the Qur'an expresses the call to worship Allah alone include one like this: "And to 'Ad, their brother Hud. He said: O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him" (7:65/50 in the cited numbering). And the second manner is:

"Worship none but Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good news" (11:2).

The difference between these two modes of expression is that one is a command and the other is not. Is there any difference between a positive command and a negative or prohibitive form of expression, or is the meaning one and the same? The meaning of the first mode is: worship Allah alone, and there is no other object of worship; and the meaning of the second is: do not worship anyone other than Allah. The second meaning is a requirement of the first. The first meaning is the established meaning and is an explicit command, and the second is its necessary consequence. But Allah did not suffice with only the first mode, that is, the positive command, but also explicitly prohibited the worship of other deities. Even if the negative meaning had been stated independently, it would still have been a necessary requirement of the first positive command. Why then was one and the same matter stated both positively and negatively? Because this matter is extremely important to Allah, and because of this importance Allah did not suffice with the principle that the prohibition is a necessary consequence of the utterance of worshipping Allah, so there is no need to repeat it. In view of this importance, it was also stated in negative forms.

In the statement of the belief in Tawhid in both positive and negative worship, the meaning is: worship Allah, do not worship anyone else. This positive and negative mode of expression was adopted because at times circumstances come upon mankind in which people accept the existence of the Lord, the Mighty and Exalted, but along with Allah they also acknowledge other personalities and deities and worship them too. Thus people in fact fall into shirk, yet they think they are upright Muslims in belief.

For this reason alone, the belief in Tawhid has been expressed both as command and prohibition, and simultaneously in positive and negative form, so that one command may confirm and emphasize the other, and so that no gap or crack remains in the belief in Tawhid through which shirk could enter. This mode of expression is repeated in many places in the Qur'an. A few examples from this surah and from other surahs are worth noting:

"Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book whose verses have been made firm, then detailed, from One who is Wise and Acquainted: that you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good news" (11:1-2).

"And We certainly sent Noah to his people: Indeed, I am to you a clear warner, that you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful Day" (11:25-26).

"And to 'Ad, their brother Hud. He said: O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. You are not but fabricators" (11:50).

"And Allah said, 'Do not take two gods. He is but one God, so fear Me alone'" (16:51).

"Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a Hanif, a Muslim, and he was not of the polytheists" (3:67).

"I have turned my face, as one inclining to truth, toward He who created the heavens and the earth, and I am not of the polytheists" (6:79).

This manner of expression recurs again and again in the Qur'an in describing Tawhid and its reality, and in this meaning there remains no doubt. From this manner it becomes clear what the importance and greatness of this belief is in Islam. This manner was adopted so that the secondary requirements and secondary meanings of this belief would also be brought out clearly and explicitly. Allah, the Exalted, knows His creation well, and He judged it necessary for the benefit of this human being that no vagueness and no gap should remain in any aspect of the belief in Tawhid. And Allah is the Owner of perfect wisdom; He knows the weaknesses of His creation well, and He is most subtle in observation and fully aware.

Now we reflect on the technical meaning of the word "ibadah" (worship). This word has been used repeatedly in this surah and throughout the Qur'an, so that we may understand why the Qur'an so often emphasizes that you should worship Allah and not worship anyone else besides Him, and that this word has been stated as emphasis in both positive and negative forms.

Earlier, in the context of the story of Hud and his dialogue with his people, we clarified the meaning of "al-'ibadah" (worship) well, and explained why the Qur'an repeatedly brings up this point, and how prophets and reformers in human history have laid stress on this point, and what difficulties they bore in this path. But beyond that explanation, here we wish to give a few further glimpses of its meaning.

The meaning of worship, that its scope applies to the rituals that exist between Allah and His servant, and that this meaning is in contrast to the dealings that occur between one human being and another, was not current at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an. The distinction of "ibadat" and "mu'amalat" as two separate technical categories was recorded later. In the first era of Islam and at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, there was no such distinction.

Previously, in our book (Khasa'is al-Tasawwur al-Islami wa Muqawwamatuh), we gave details about this. It is appropriate to quote a few sentences here.

"This division of human actions and activities, that one part consists of 'ibadat' and another part consists of 'mu'amalat', belongs to the period of Islamic history in which fiqh was codified. Initially, the purpose and aim of this division was merely the technical arrangement and codification of the sciences and subjects, as happens in the arrangement and compilation of books of any discipline. But it must be said with great regret that merely because of this technical division, very harmful consequences arose in Islamic concepts and ideas. And because of this conceptual and ideological distortion, the practical life of Islamic society was also adversely affected. People came to feel that only those actions are 'ibadah' which relate to the rituals of worship of God, and that according to the juristic division, other activities, which were presented in fiqh under the heading of 'mu'amalat', do not fall under the application of 'ibadah'. Yet this is, according to the Islamic worldview, a departure from the real matter, and because of this misguidance a deviation came into the whole life of the Muslims."

The real truth is that there is no action of a human being to which the word 'ibadah' does not apply; rather, every part of the Islamic system of life, from beginning to end, is for the worship of Allah. In short, the components of the Islamic system, namely the system of government and politics, the economic system, the Islamic law of crimes and the Islamic civil law, the Islamic family law and all other laws, are in reality 'ibadat'. And all these laws have been framed to bring into effect the meaning of the word 'ibadah'. But all human activities will fall within the Islamic system and within the definition of the word 'ibadah' only when they are in accordance with the Qur'an, the Sunnah and the Islamic Shari'ah, in such a way that a Muslim regards Allah alone as his God and Lord, affirms only His worship and 'ibadah', and practically spends his whole life in accordance with this system. And this is the real purpose and aim of the creation of man and the creation of the universe; if this is not so, then a human being will be excluded from the scheme of the Islamic system and will not be considered within the religion of Islam.

If the subjects and fields for which the jurists used the term 'ibadat' are examined, and the rulings given about them in the Qur'an are read, it will be found that the Qur'an did not present these fields and subjects separately from those fields and subjects to which the jurists applied the term mu'amalat; rather, both kinds of rulings come in the Qur'an and Sunnah linked together within one and the same context, and they are mentioned in such a way that both fall within the meaning of obedience to Allah and the Messenger ﷺ and the worship of Allah, for which Allah created the heavens and the earth and the jinn and mankind; and this is the meaning of La ilaha illallah and of Tawhid."

In the later periods of Islamic history, the result of this division has been that Muslims began to think that if they act upon the part of 'ibadat' and perform 'ibadat' in accordance with the commands of God, and if in mu'amalat they follow some other system and take guidance in mu'amalat from some source other than Allah, they can still be Muslims, even though the other systems of legislation and the codes of life are violating the commands of Allah.

The truth is that this is, on the part of Muslims, a sheer self-deception. Islam cannot be divided, nor can the Islamic system be cut into pieces. Whoever divides Islam in this manner and on this approach will be outside the circle of Islam, and will have no connection with this religion.

This is the great truth that every Muslim should be concerned with: making their Islam a true Islam. Provided they seek to fulfill the purpose for which Allah created them.

These are the few purposeful sentences we have quoted from our book *Khasa'is al-Tasawwur al-Islami* (The Distinctive Features of the Islamic Conception). We will add only a few words to these sentences, which we have already explained in detail in this part. When the Prophet (ﷺ) presented the call of *La ilaha illa Allah* to the Arabs and told them to worship Allah alone, that there is no deity besides Him, those Arabs did not use this word only in the sense of worship. Nor did they know the jurists' division of *'ibadat* (acts of worship) and *mu'amalat* (transactions). Rather, when the command came in Makkah not to worship anyone other than Allah, the Islamic acts of worship had not yet become obligatory. For them, the meaning of worship was to give one's entire life to the obedience of Allah and to remove one's whole life from obedience to others than Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to 'Adi ibn Hatim about the rabbis:

"Yes, they made lawful for them what was unlawful, and unlawful what was lawful, and they obeyed them. This was their worship of them."

The term *'ibadah* applies to ritual observances in the sense that these are a part of worship and a part of human life's activities. But the full meaning and implication of the word *'ibadah* is not confined to these rituals alone.

We have already said on this subject that if worship meant only ritual observances, then there would be no need at all for messengers and their missions. The tireless efforts and struggles of the messengers for the establishment of the religion (*iqamat al-din*) in human history would not have been necessary. The great sacrifices of believers throughout human history would also have been unnecessary. The truth is that these great sacrifices were given solely so that people could be removed from the slavery and obedience of fellow humans and admitted only into the servitude and obedience of Allah, and so that a system could be established in which the sovereignty belongs to Allah and people are obedient to Allah in all the affairs of this world and the Hereafter.

Only the sovereignty of Allah, and obedience to and servitude of Allah alone, is such a purpose and such a comprehensive and exclusive Tawhid, for which the long chain of messengers was sent. For it, great struggles were made in history, and so many sacrifices were given and hardships endured on this path. This work was not done because Allah, the Exalted, had any need of it, but because without it human life cannot be set right, a human being cannot attain honor and elevation, and human living cannot become worthy of a human being. This can be achieved only through this all-encompassing and pervasive belief in Tawhid: a belief that grips the whole of human life.

Where we gave the above excerpt, we had promised that at the end we would discuss this subject at length. So here we will discuss a little the effects of the belief in Tawhid on human life.

The first point is this: if a person accepts the belief in Tawhid with this comprehensive, exclusive and complete meaning, what effect will it have on the limits of his personal life, his natural needs, his physical existence, his thoughts, and then, through those thoughts, on his practical life?

"When this conception and this way of thinking, in its full universality, takes all the affairs of life into its custody, this conception addresses human life from every aspect. It grips all the interests, all the needs, and all the inclinations of human life, and turns their direction toward one single course. Now his dealings are with that one direction alone. A person seeks everything from that direction. He moves forward with all he has in that direction. His hopes are tied to that direction, and his fears are also from it. He seeks only the pleasure of that direction and seeks forgiveness from its wrath, because that Sovereign is the owner and creator of everything, and He alone is the governor of the whole universe."

"This conception turns the personality of a human being toward one single source and fountainhead. From this same source a person derives truths and concepts, from it he takes his standards and values, and from it he obtains principles and laws. He takes the answer to every question from there, and whatever questions arise in his mind about humanity and this universe, he finds their solution from that same source and fountainhead."

Now a human personality becomes an integrated personality. Its consciousness, its conduct, its emotions and inclinations, whether they relate to belief or to a system of life, whether they concern seeking help or seeking guidance, whether they relate to this life or the Hereafter, whether they concern the struggle and movement of life or relate to health and sustenance, whether they are a worldly matter or an otherworldly matter, all these affairs come together. Now there is no division or separation among them, and in these matters the human personality does not take different paths nor follow different methods."

"When a human personality is united and integrated on this footing, these are its very good days, because it is in a state of unity, and the first quality of truth is that it contains unity; it is one, because when Allah, the Exalted, is One, the truth is also one. Indeed, in this whole universe this unity and oneness is an important reality, although its manifestations, forms and circumstances may differ. Despite his various abilities, colors and shapes, a human being is in reality one. Tawhid and unity are in truth the real purpose of human existence. Whenever and wherever a human being sets out in search of his reality, despite the differences in his habits and forms, his reality will be one."

"When this human personality is in such circumstances that these circumstances are in harmony with 'the truth' in every field, then the personality is at its peak, and it is in harmony with this entire universe. There is no contradiction or conflict between its self and the universe in which it lives. Between this personality and this universe, one and the same truth is effective. When the human personality moves in harmony with this great universe, then as a result of this harmony great revolutions take place in the world and great eras come into being."

"For example, when the first community of Muslims reached this station of truth in terms of their personality, Allah, the Exalted, through them made far-reaching changes on this earth, and they left deep impacts on history, and the very currents of human personality and thought were changed."

"And in the future too, whenever such a community and people with this kind of integrated personality come into being in the world, they will leave the same deep impacts on humanity and history, and such individuals and such a community will certainly come into being, Allah willing. Even if the enemies of the Muslim nation oppose it, when such a community comes into existence, it possesses a strength that no obstacle can withstand, because the strength of such a community is in harmony with the strength of nature and the universe, and the source and origin of human strengths and cosmic strengths is one."

"The benefit of this Tawhid and unity is not only that a person's belief becomes correct. Although this correction and rectification is itself very important, because the whole structure of human life rests upon this correction, yet beyond that, the importance of this belief is that the belief in Tawhid creates good taste within a person. A person passes his life with great grace, and harmony and coherence arise among all the aspects of human life. This is because, as a result of this all-encompassing Tawhid, every small and great aspect of human life, and every small and great deed, becomes worship. When a person declares Allah alone as his sovereign and Lord, and serves Him alone in every small and great matter of life, he attains the highest station of humanity. This is the station in which the Messenger of Allah alone attained perfection in all its aspects. This is the station of revelation and the Night Journey (*isra'*)."

﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, the surroundings of which We have blessed, that We might show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.﴾ (17:1)

The Urdu translation of this verse as given in the text: "Blessed is that Being who sent down the Furqan upon His servant, so that he might become a warner to all the worlds."

And in another place:

﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, the surroundings of which We have blessed, that We might show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.﴾ (17:1)

The Urdu translation of this: "Holy is that Being who took His servant on a journey at night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have made blessed, so that We might show him Our signs. Indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing."

Now, holding the Tawhid of servitude as sovereign and Lord, and adopting its complete servitude, we place before the readers another benefit: this worship brings a person out of slavery to other humans, and a system is established in which a person is free from the slavery of another person. When a person attains complete freedom, he also attains a respected position. This freedom and this honor are not attained by a person in any non-Islamic or jahili system, because in those other systems a person is the slave of a person, and though the forms of one human's rule over others may differ, sometimes a person is mentally a slave of others, sometimes he prostrates before strangers, sometimes he is bound by the regulations made by other humans. These are different kinds of slavery, and though their forms vary, their nature is the same: in all of them a person is subordinate to and under another person. In one way or another, he is bound.

It is not possible for people not to be bound by some law and code. If they are not bound by the laws and codes of Allah, then obviously they will be bound by the law of someone else, and thus they will fall into the slavery of other humans.

Whenever a person falls into the slavery of other than Allah, he is at every moment a slave of the desires and wishes of other than Allah, and because of this slavery he falls from the station of humanity down to the level of animality.

﴿And those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat, and the Fire is their abode.﴾ (47:12)

What greater loss can there be for a human being than to lose his humanity? As soon as a person comes out of the sovereignty and servitude of Allah alone, first he becomes a slave of his own desires and appetites, and thus he falls to the level of animals, which are subject only to their desires. After that, he falls into the servitude of his fellow servants. Then such people become slaves of rulers and chieftains, in that these rulers and chieftains bind them in the shackles of laws that they themselves have made in their own interests, and these laws protect only the interests of their makers. These lawmakers are sometimes in the form of a king or dictator, sometimes in the form of a ruling class, and sometimes in the form of a ruling dynasty. This characteristic is present in all those systems which are not derived from the guidance of Allah, that is, which are not derived from the Shari'ah of Allah.

Human slavery to humans is not limited only to rulers, chieftains and lawmakers. This slavery is apparent in those classes, but in addition, every person is also a slave of other hidden forces. Sometimes these other forces are even stronger than the others. For example, a person is bound even by customs and traditions and clothing. Under the pretext of being progressive, people make customs and dress for their own interests. These accessories are imposed upon people in the form of clothing, in the form of cars, in the form of big mansions, in the form of scenes, and then in the form of exclusive gatherings. No jahili-minded man or woman can escape these unjustly imposed accessories. Rather, those who are caught in these jahili customs and accessories remain always confined within their circle. Today, the way people blindly follow these accessories and customs, if they followed even a few commands of Allah with such blind observance, they would reach the station of the pious, night-vigil worshipper. If this is not blind slavery, then what is it? If the sovereignty of other than Allah is not this, then what would it be, that a person is a slave even to the fashion set by other people?

Sometimes a respectable person sees a woman wearing such clothing that her figure and shape are visible. This clothing is neither suited to her face and appearance nor to her physical build. Then this woman adopts such manners and such gestures that signals come toward her from every side, and she becomes a joke. But the compelling power of the fashion houses forces these people to obey them, and to put these people into this disgrace, in such a way that they have no power to refuse, while their whole environment is caught in this slavery. If this is not slavery, then what is it? If these fashion houses are not sovereigns and lords, then what are they?

When people turn away from the worship of Allah and take up the worship and servitude of other than Allah, they fall into many kinds of degradation. The above-mentioned humiliation of fashion is one of them. Likewise, the rule of the wealthy and the chieftains is not the only hideous form into which people fall, when a human being becomes the slave of a human being and one servant serves another servant. Beyond this, there are many other evils that arise in such a society.

From this we come to understand well how far-reaching are the effects of worshipping Allah alone, and of acknowledging Allah alone as Lord and Sovereign, upon a person's soul, his honour and his wealth. When a human being becomes the slave of a human being, his morals, his honour and his wealth should not remain secure. Whatever the form of worship of other than Allah may be, whether it is in the field of legislation by other than Allah, or in the form of customs and traditions, or in the form of false beliefs and notions.

For example, if a person becomes a slave of other than Allah in beliefs, ideas, conceptions and theories, then he believes in idolatry, in tales and in superstitions. Wherever in the world the ignorance of idol worship prevails, it is the result of slavery to this false way of thinking. Among such misguidances, the common people fall prey to various kinds of illusions. And out of fear of them, they go to the courts of imaginary gods, make vows and offerings, and present sacrifices. Sometimes they also give sacrifices of children and human beings, and this happens purely because of slavery to corrupt and useless ideas. In such societies, people fear gods fashioned by their own imagination and illusion alone. Then these people also fear the soothsayers and priests, who convince them that they have a connection with those gods. In such societies, people also fear jinn and calamities, and they also honour those people who make them believe that jinn are under their control. Then they obey the guardians of such idols and shrines, the religious leaders. And all the people of such societies are cowardly and weak-hearted, always frightened and alarmed, and a fear is always upon them. And in this way all human powers are wasted.

A middle-class household with an average income spends a large sum on oil, perfume and face powder. It spends a considerable amount on grooming and styling its hair. Then, to keep pace with changing fashions, it buys new suits every year. Along with these suits it also provides matching shoes and other garments. And all of this is done in obedience to those gods who sit behind the curtain and fabricate these fashions. Upon investigation, it will be found that a middle-income household spends half of its total income on fashion and customs. Behind fashion and face powder stands the hand of international Judaism, which has ensnared all people in the net of fashion, and as a result its international companies run. And these companies raid people's wealth, their honour and their dignity, and the people are utterly helpless.

Now, finally, observe: when a human being becomes the slave of a human being, and the master makes the law for the human being, see how much sacrifice the slave must give, and how much sacrifice is not required in submitting to the servitude of Allah. It will be known that in servitude to other than Allah a person must give far greater material and life sacrifices.

Besides this, the idol of the homeland, the idol of the nation, the idol of classes, the idol of production, and other idols which have assumed the status of divinity, and to which drums are beaten and flags are waved in this world, and then their servants are invited to make sacrifices of life and property in the name of these idols, and they give them without hesitation. If they do not give, then such social pressure is upon them that they are considered traitors and are insulted. If there is a contest between someone's wealth and honour and one of these idols, then wealth and honour are sacrificed upon these idols, and these artificial idols are given such a lofty status that blood is shed at their shrines. And behind this entire scheme stands the hand of those lords besides Allah.

All the sacrifices that are given for the sake of jihad in the path of Allah, and so that on this earth only the worship of Allah may prevail, and so that people may be freed from the slavery of idols and tyrants, and so that man may be raised to that lofty rank and brought to that exalted horizon which Allah has appointed for him, all these sacrifices are very small compared to those sacrifices which some people give to establish a system of human lordship over human beings. If not more, then at least equal to them are the sacrifices of those who shrink from striving in the way of Allah and fear to give martyrdom, life, wealth and children. They should consider for a moment that in the case of slavery to other than Allah, they will have to give far greater sacrifices. Rather, for other than Allah they will have to give, in addition to life and wealth, the sacrifice of honour and dignity as well.
